analysis.name: Aditi Mukherjee
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the easiest classes I've taken. Study early for the Excel Certification exam and attend every class. The in-class projects make up a big part of your grade. She's a good professor, but be on time for class because if you are more than 5 minutes late, she won't let you do the project. No extensions, so don't turn things in late.

Easiest critical tracking class you will ever take. Meets once a week for a project you do with a partner. If you're stuck she'll help you through it. No exams, only play posits and the excel certification/final exam. Definitely chose the excel certification its super easy. Please take this and not CGS trust me.

Most of the class is assignments with unlimited attempts and step by step instructions. Only somewhat difficult thing is the excel certification midterm but that's relatively easy too. Professor mostly just lets you learn through the online textbook and doesn't really teach herself, but its easy to get an A.

Easiest class you will take. Only one exam (on Excel). 90% of the grade is assignments ~2 hours max per week. Meets once per week for max of 1 hour and the Prof is as enthusiatic as you can get about Excel and Access.

Very light class, hardest part was the Excel Certification Exam, but that wasn't even that bad. Some of her lab instructions were confusing and there was some busy work, but overall not bad at all. Only one lab a week.

analysis.name: Md Ali Babar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This sounds scary but it really isn't. I didn't put as much time in as I should have but I still did pretty good. Finish reading the chapters & give yourself enough time to read through the ppts a day or 2 before the exam you'll be fine. He's really nice and if bad weather etc. cancels class, he adjusts the exams to fit. Really nice, extra credit.

If you have to take any type of genetics for your major, take this course with this professor. All the lectures are his own power points, don't need the textbook. 6 total exams but none of them are cumulative, so you don't have to study that much for each test, and they're all multiple choice. no final, and he gives SO MUCH extra credit!

The class isn't as bad as everyone is making it seem. He provides a lot of extra credit opportunities. His exams sometimes have challenging questions but all of the material is from the slides. I read the textbook for the first exam but didn't find it that helpful so I just used his slides for the next 4 which is all I needed. So study his slides!

Lectures are difficult to understand and exams are on tiny details from the lectures. Some of the questions were based on specific context of examples in the lecture, not even the science behind them. Exam questions can be unclear or incorrect and he will fix them only for the person who emails in, and only after messaging him multiple times.

dude its so bad he is almost completely unintelligible in the lectures, literally just reads off a script right from the book, and its weighted at 85% exams, which have questions on the most tiny random details you never expected to need to know. do not do it its literally comically easy to fail a class that should be easy bc of the grading scheme

analysis.name: Andres Rubiano Acosta
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 102 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Worst experience I've had. The professor is disrespectful in emails and the TAs never reply. Lectures consist of old YouTube videos that only cover the basics, but the exams are incredibly advanced and feel completely disconnected from the teaching material. It feels like being taught addition and then being tested on calculus.

DO NOT take this professor. It takes at least 10 hours of work a week to earn an A, and he requires that you record your screen for all assignments. He cares about his students and is very knowledgeable, but he has no grasp on how difficult the class is for those with no CAD experience. I would only recommend him If you have an easy semester ahead.

Possibly one of the most miserable experiences I have had at UF thus far. Quizzes do not show up on the canvas assignment page, little to no feedback on submissions or exams, the grading scale is way too harsh given that the class is graded solely by 4 exams.

Lectures are "short" but so dense you pause every second if you actually want to understand the content. Excel calculators he made us create were just time wasters, since only the first exam had us using them. Hardly communicated with us and gave zero feedback. Easy exams if your work is done, but overcomplicates how he wants us to prepare for them

Worst class I've taken at UF. Lectures were shallow 8-12 minute, 4 year old yt videos that didn't have enough detail. Assignments were not graded but expected to be 100% correct on exams. OH were practically mandatory which defeats the purpose of being online. The professor and TAs severely neglected the course material and structure. Do not take.

analysis.name: Andrea Goncher
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Really nice professor but mostly boring class. Only fun parts in my mind were learning cad and arduino circuits, rest of the class is kinda dull. Its very easy though so I recommend.
She's really nice the class is just pretty dull and boring. One homework assignment a week and a lot of them are done with your group. Culminates in a final group project that's really easy.

If you are between professors for EGN2020c, go with Goncher. Her section has reasonable coursework that did not take up too much time during the week. The class is 5% of grade homework assignments and then a final project worth 25% at the end. It's not too difficult if you split up the tasks. Overall good professor.

If you take her for Engineering in Design and Society she is very nice and the class is mainly project based and hands on. I took it online because of corona but if you submit all the assignments on time you should get an A.

I took this class on a flipped format, we had to watch very long lectures before class which seemed pretty redundant as the professor would jus go over the content in class. She cares about her students and was approachable during office hours. Offered plenty of extra credit through extra exam questions, turning projects early, and by participating

analysis.name: Austin Vining
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Can't say much about him I had 0% interaction. The course tests are pretty difficult. So much reading I had a hard time keeping up and staying engaged. It's basically READ, READ, READ, TEST!!!

He seems nice enough but he doesn't participate very much at all. I feel like he needs a lot more experience. Lots of work and slow grading, he isn't the one that grades. The videos were inaccessible, I mean I even wondered if there were videos at all or if it was just his PowerPoint?

The tests are FIVE HOURS LONG! Study, study, study and don't try to hold a job while you take this professor. He expects a lot and delivers little. He never even spoke to us the entire class except to ask for forgiveness when his modules were not uploaded properly.

He never shows up! He doesn't respond in a reasonable time and changes your grades after you rate him for evals so you will give him a good rating. His teacher's assistant does everything. He is prideful and lacking compassion.
Showed no interest in his students, only emailed when he made mistakes, had his teacher's assistant do everything.

analysis.name: Roger Austin
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: he is kind and an easy grader with few assignments (2 tests & 2 essays) but UNORGANIZED. he doesn't even have his grading scale on the syllabus. Doesn't put grades on Canvas. Lectures are also not structured and he goes off topic a lot. participation (which is a grade) is difficult bc you need in-depth knowledge outside of class on politics.

Dr. Austin was great! He's an engaging lecturer, and the class is not hard. It's a midterm, a term paper, a final (take-home), and participation, but none of these were too difficult. You learn a good bit, and he's a hilarious guy. He assigns readings sporadically. He also talks a lot about current events, which helps contextualize concepts.

I am currently a junior at UF, and I can say hands down, he is the best professor I have ever had. He is a genuine, friendly and passionate professor who wants to see his students succeed. I have nothing but positive things to say about this professor. If you have an opportunity to take one of his classes, you won't regret it.

very sweet professor but SO unorganized. Never knew my grade in the class and he does not know how to use canvas correctly. only take him if you are a super type B person and you're ok with deadlines being constantly up in the air ...

Professor Austin was my first ever class as an incoming freshmen. His class is very fun and very easy to get a good grade. There are only 3 grades but he is a very easy grader so there is no need to worry. If you aren't a political buff like myself the class can be a teeny bit harder but I had no problem getting an A+.

analysis.name: Ana Longo
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 117 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Don't be scared off by the negative reviews following the 2021 spring exam 3. Dr. Longo had detailed lectures, lots of reading (as did the other three profs) and a difficult test but overall not too bad if you studied the learning objectives. Ppl retaliated bc they got a bad grade, doesn't reflect the prof. If u can't handle bio1, hope ur not STEM.

I think many reviews here are unfair to Dr. Longo as people posted them after being upset about the exam. I found the exam to be very fair and lecture-based. I watched lectures on 2x speed the day before, studied 5 days in advance, and did very well. Dr. Longo is available in office hours which I recommend if confused, and is overall a good person.

People are being very harsh to her as a direct result of the Spring 2021 exam. I thought her lectures were really interesting and her teaching style was easy to follow. That being said, the exam was poorly worded and when the TAs predicted a 10 point curve, we got nothing. She does not care about students' success, but hey, welcome to college.

I honestly enjoyed learning from Longo. Her lectures were to the point and I liked the small jokes and memes she included. However; her exam was oddly specific and the wording was confusing; it did not reflect what we had learned that well. If you study you should be fine, but if you don't pay attention to detail you won't do well with her.

There are many other reviews on this page that are not fair to Dr. Longo. Students flooded Rate My Professor after failing the exam, which is more a way for them to express their anger than honestly evaluating the professor. Dr. Longo taught evolution very well, there werent too many assignments or lectures, and it is totally feasible to get an A.

analysis.name: Michael  Beck
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I LOVED Dr. Beck's class!! He was passionate about the class, and you can tell that he cares about his students. He doesn't give out too much work, the quizzes and exams are super easy, and he prepares you very well for them. His lectures and activities were genuinely engaging. I definitely recommend him for SYG2000. 10/10 would take again.

Dr Beck is one of the most amazing professors I've ever had. I'm not really a religious person, but I'd say this course was a kind of spiritual experience. I genuinely learned so much. His lectures are funny, engaging, & conversational. He takes time to really explain everything you need to know.

Engaging and respectful professor! He's very insightful and made the class enjoyable. He's well educated and talks about his experiences with sociology on hand. Definitely recommend him for any class you take with him.
Dr Beck is the goat. Best professor I've ever had. I literally thought about changing my major to sociology, but there's not much money in the field. Take every sociology class you can with him.
Dr Beck made sociology come alive. He really stretched us to debate hard topics and appreciate diverse perspectives. Definitely five stars.

analysis.name: Stacey Ann Benjamin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 136 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: This professor is very hard. For an intro class, the content is difficult and explained in a confusing way. I reached out to friends in much higher chem classes and they thought the tests were worded in an odd way. I have never struggled ever in any academic sense until this class. I studied nonstop for every test and could barely get a B+ overall.

Professor Benjamin clearly doesn't care about anyone taking this online, as she made the exams mostly free-response math with no review given, while in-person students received MCQs with practice exams provided beforehand. The class is entirely self-taught, and the "lectures" are 5-minute Youtube videos. Please don't even bother, just take CHM2045.

Please don't take this class if you don't absolutely HAVE to. One would assume that as a 2 credit introductory course that it would be fairly easy; but that's not entirely true. The material itself isn't too bad. But the professor is no where to be found and refuses to give students any practice besides the few questions on her canvas. Not worth it

took in person and not only were lectures pointless because they were a reiteration of what was on the slides but the course was super exam-heavy - 3 exams worth 17% each and a final worth 22%. no amount of studying/studyedge saved me from the weight of the exams. for a two credit course just do yourself a favor and go straight to 2045 if you can

This class was inconsistent and confusing in structure.  I chose to take it as a refresher.  I the material is at a basic, introductory chem knowledge level (not really difficult.)  Going into the class, I knew the material with at least a 90% mastery.  What I was not able to master were the tests that followed no rules for units or significants

analysis.name: Christina Boucher
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst teachers Ive ever had the misfortune of having. Reads slides like an audiobook. Tests cover two or more chapters every two weeks. Lets us assume that everything will be on the test when half isnt. Cant trust what she says is important to know. Furthermore, shes unaccommodating to students and doesnt try to pretend to care.

She doesn't seem prepared for lectures at all and makes up confusing explanations on the spot. She also complained that there were too many people in the class so she made the entire grade based on 4 tests, which were largely unrelated to what we supposedly learned in lectures.

Even though the class is super interesting for math nerds, she just butchered it. She basically reads from the slides and that is it. Honestly, she does not seem to be prepared to give lectures at all. Exams are not the worst. However, you should review her slides.

She just reads off the slides. She had her TA teach the class more than 8 times throughout the semester because she was absent. Tests are very difficult as they are all free response and no specifics are given on what they will be about.

One of the exams covered 4 chapters - a total of 184 slides from the PowerPoints. Two of these chapters discussed matrices and how they apply to sets and graphs. The homework contained many problems about matrices. On the test, not a single problem about matrices. Yet, we were tested on a theorem that was only discussed on 1 slide with no examples.

analysis.name: Christophe Bobda
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Taking a class with Bobda is like a Kitchen Nightmares episode: everything's in flames and he has no idea. Lectures cover anything as long as it's NOT relevant. The labs have two sentences of instruction, no further elaboration necessary (it's very necessary). And nothing works... ever. I go thru the 5 stages of grief, every time. Do not recommend.

i found this class to be alright (taken post course change), though the labs can really surprise u with work if ur not prepared. start early on them. its cool to see all work come together to make a cpu. bobda is really nice and understanding, the class is insanely unorganized though and studying for exams was annoying.

Really hard to grasp the material during lectures. I found there was a lot of unnecessary information on the PowerPoint it is a lot of confusing information and isn't very organized. You learn best in this class through doing the labs and quizzes and asking for help from PIs!

Dr. Bobda reads off of slides that he seems barely familiar with and often rushes through. The content of these slides often is lacking and doesn't provide any help with the assignments. Much of this course seems like regurgitation of other courses such as Computer Architecture. I would recommend avoiding his courses if you can.

Most unorganized class I've ever taken at UF. Homework assignments are consistently unclear yet graded on accuracy. Labs are more about debugging VHDL code rather than learning Digital Logic. Lecture content gives very little help with labs.TAs aren't on the same page. Very caring professor but he simply does not know how to properly run the class.

analysis.name: Katie Basinger
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: there were a ton of typos and other issues in her slides/lectures and homeworks and exams. also 1st exam was a trainwreck mostly due to her fault bc she made multiple attempts allowed and said to use to advantage then later penalized those who abused it... overall class isn't too bad its mainly just using excel. join the groupme!!

Some of these reviews are exaggerating, not the worst professor to have but probably better alternatives. Excel HW assignments and open quizzes due every Sunday, HW could be time consuming but it is doable within a day. Watch office hour recordings as she reviews HW problems, she's fairly helpful. Overall manageable workload but not the easiest A.

Prof. Basinger-Ellis frequently came to lectures unprepared and made mistakes often. During the midterm, she first allowed infinite attempts after messing up, then threatened to penalize students for using them, creating a ton of confusion. Her quizzes and HW constantly needed changes and were not proofread. Take this class with another professor.

When I took this class, Basinger was the "instructor" but she didn't make any of the lectures. She just reused the lectures from an older professor who could barely speak English. She rarely answered emails and did next to nothing on the part of preparing us for exams. The first 3 chapters are worth way more than the rest so hit the ground running.

In Intro to ISE, she was a great mentor to go to. She answered any personal questions regarding ISE, gave great advice (even about classes and when not to take them), and made me feel much more connected to the ISE department. She & Dr. Kirli worked hard to make this new class engaging & beneficial to ISE students. No idea why everyone's hating.

analysis.name: Rori Bloom
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I've had Dr Bloom for three classes now and she is interesting to say the least. She is not flexible with new ideas/different approaches to prompts, but is a very nice woman. She will eventually give you an A if you participate, but if you are used to AP Lit style writing where you go beyond the prompt, be prepared to be flamed for it at first.

Had a great time taking this class. Bloom is definitely sweeter than a lot of the other French professors. I did feel like I wasn't getting as much French practice as I would have liked taking this class, but other than that, had a great time. Readings were interesting.

While this class interesting I cannot recommend Dr. Bloom. Her grading criteria was completely random and she did not give clarification when asked. She only has like four assignments the entire semester, so one error was detrimental, I asked her for help and she refused, then failed me anyway. If you need any type of accommodations, she will hate.

I took her fairy tales class and her enthusiasm was contagious. She is somewhat of a tough grader without super clear expectations, but she does an excellent job of teaching course content. 50% of the grade is made up of 2 essays, each with 1000 words, the rest of the grade comes from discussions and participation. I would def recommend for quest 1

Interesting material and I can only say good things about this professor for her teaching. Most UF professors are easy A's, but this is not one of them.Fortunately, the curve will save you and your final grade will turn out to be good.But trust me, you'll be worried every minute until you get that final grade.I guess she likes to motivate her stude

analysis.name: Ted Bridis
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I found this class pretty boring because of the 3 hour lecture but none of that was Bridis's fault. He's a great professor and knows a lot about reporting. I would miss class from time-to-time, and it was no big deal. Lectures were online and the weekly quizzes or homeworks were simple to complete.

Prof. Bridis knows his stuff and his class is extremely useful. He's a funny guy and the class went the full three hours maybe once or twice. Tests aren't a cake walk, but he will go out of his way to let you retake them to help you at the end of the semester. Would highly recommend.

I loved this class! Definitely super useful and I was a big fan of his lectures and sense of humor, you could tell he's lived! He's always there to help so don't hesitate to reach out. For summer A we only had 6 quizzes and 4 assignments, so not many grades. The quizzes are really specific so have the lectures out and read the questions carefully.

Incredible professor!! He is incredibly knowledgeable about the journalism world and left every class wanting more. Every week consisted of a Packback assignment, and a quiz based on the lecture plus a couple of other assignments throughout the semester and some extra credit. Very easy to get an A. 100% recommend and can't wait to take him again

I absolutely loved Professor Bridis for JOU3110. He is one of the most down-to-earth professors I have ever had. He is always open to help you, and you can tell he truly loves what he teaches. The course content isn't that bad, some of it can get a little tricky. He makes sure to post the PowerPoints, which can be a great resource.

analysis.name: Erika Brooke
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Tough exams (3) even with a study guide. Had an assignment about every 2 weeks so it was manageable. The class is very organized and easy to follow which also helped. Second class with Dr. Brooke. She was very responsive and so was her TA. Even offered extra credit. Wish she taught more classes.

Dr. Brooke is very knowledgeable and impressive. She has a great setup for her online classes and integrates different assignments to keep it interesting. TA grades most things but there are only 3 exams that were very manageable. You probably should buy the textbook to ensure you get all of the material, but I did not use mine all the time.

This was my second class with Dr. Brooke and this one seemed significantly harder. There are three exams each of which is far more challenging than needed, beyond that, the workload is very manageable.

Dr Brooke was amazing. There was a lot of reading. If you only watch the videos, there is a good chance you will pass the quizzes. However, the assignment involve the textbook, so I recommend getting the online version and search up key words. There is a three page paper at the end, but it's fairly easy. 

Most importantly, THERE IS NO FINAL!!!!

Dr. Brooke was excellent! She was extremely accommodating of my disabilities and always accessible via email to answer any questions I had. Her quizzes were challenging, but as long as I kept up with the readings and lectures, they were manageable. Some classmates complained a lot, but this is UF—put in the effort. It's not high school. Take her!

analysis.name: Mario Cano
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I have Dr. Cano for CCJ3701 as well. He is so kind and funny. His lectures are interesting and he is knowledgable. He gives review days before exams and tells you exactly what to study. He also has extra credit days just for showing up to class. He tries to make his classes as accessible as possible and is very understanding.

Amazing class! He is really knowledgable about court cases, so he will tie that into what is being taught. Exams can be challenging, but if you study the material you will get an A. Exam reviews are extremely helpful. All of the essays I actually really enjoyed writing and they were short. Read the textbook as well since that is what the test is on

Dr. Cano is awesome! I took his courts and sentencing class, and I would highly recommend it to any pre-law student. As long as you read the textbook and make sure to stay on top of the case brief assignments, you should be good to go. Lots of extra credit and clear expectations for written assignments. Take this class!

Dr. Cano is amazing. He is flexible, caring, helpful, and understanding. He has clear grading criteria, good lectures and offers lots of opportunities to do well. If you attend class, read, and put in effort you will do great. He is so nice and funny and really tries to make class interesting.
He made an intimidating class way less scary and very passable. He's the best! Take him for sure, he is super funny and nice

analysis.name: Cheryl Resch
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 119 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She clearly explains data structures and shows how certain algorithms work. She is the best CS teacher I had in this school so far and basically revived my faith in the CISE department. She's SUPER GENEROUS with extra credit and it's sad to see students complain about the class being hard when they don't even show up to lecture!

One of my top 3 professors I've taken at UF. Professor Resch may be slightly passive aggressive if you say something out of pocket or if she has to keep repeating herself, but she is one of the most actually caring professors I have ever taken a class with. She kind of feels like a new yorker, she might be passive at times, but she genuinely cares.

Though I didn't love all the content in this class, Dr. Resch made the experience significantly better. She is organized, passionate, funny, and makes it easy to grasp difficult/boring concepts. The Canvas is very organized, exams are straightforward, and projects are perfectly manageable (very easy to get help on Discord and in office hours).

Amazing professor. Take her if possible! She is passionate about the subject and knows her stuff. Caring and funny. Does not simply read off the slides. Take good notes and utilize the allowed cheat sheets for the tests. The ARM coding assignments can be difficult, but you will be fine if you go to discussion. TA's help greatly. iClickers are used.

I hated taking this class with her. Her lecture slides were a mess. The rubric always had mistake. Very unreliable turnaround times with grading. 50% penalty for one day late and has a rude know-it-all tone when responding to students in the Discord server. She always expected us to figure it and would hardly help.

analysis.name: Alyssa Cole
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Alyssa Cole herself does not really contribute much to the course outside the grading, while most of the material you will have to absorb on your own time. Nothing good or necessarily bad about her teaching, just overall indifferent as she plays a very little part as far as teaching the material.

Professor Cole is one of those professors who values the intelligence of their students. She gives you pretty much free range to develop your interests within the bounds of her class. Can't recommend her enough.

This professor is very rude and does not reflect the rating given. She relies only on the textbook or perusal for assignments, so there's really no purpose to being a professor for this class. She's not very accommodating, and can be quite mean. I would stay away from her if you don't want to be ridiculed as a student. Harsh grader with no feedback

I absolutely recommend Professor Cole! Buffalos and Bloods is a small, discussion-based class, and most readings can be found online. I can honestly say I wasn't super interested in modern American or military history before this class, but I enjoyed it anyway. There's a few papers, but she's a fair grader, chill with deadlines, and very supportive

Great class structure and teaching style/personality allow for some chill but really interesting and educational discussion. She is very lenient with due dates as long as you communicate your needs. Takes the time to get to know each individual student and is a great person to have a conversation with on topics you may find interesting.

analysis.name: Cameron Buckner
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class was very interesting and he gave a bunch of fun examples to better explain harder concepts. There were 2 exams (a midterm and final) that were both FRQs. Class was simple and can't see how anyone get less than an A.
Clearly very smart and passionate, would be better in a smaller class environment but generally goated
Intelligent professor that clearly communicates expectations and presents information well. No reason you should be failing this class.
Easy class, professor has interesting lectures

analysis.name: Florin Curta
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: VERY easy quest class. Super chill TA's, and lectures (objectively) don't feel and aren't mandatory to succeed. If you show up, note the key definitions and use them in your writings. No tests, quizzes, midterms or finals. only 4 assignments in the course and they are self-explanatory. He knows what he is talking about for fs. He posts his lecture.

I am a first year freshman and this class is definitely a culture shock for me. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but the lectures feel unengaging. I respect the knowledge, but the admin of the course isn't my cup of tea. If you take this class, take notes on the key terms and do not take notes on all of the examples. No tests. Show up.

He teaches history as if it is your major and you are a grad student. Even if there are no prereqs, you NEED extensive background knowledge on his lessons. You will not keep up otherwise, especially because he assumes you know all the context and does not elaborate, talks fast, and all your grades are based on pop quizzes.

Easy grader, but one of the worst Professors you can have in History. Lectures are rambling and incoherent, will frequently demean and belittle students, does not believe in teaching anything that doesn't already gel with his particular, super-Christian worldview (he WILL force it on you), impossible to get in touch with in-person for office hours.

Prof. Curta was clearly very passionate about the field of study but make sure you have at least a background in the time period. I had none, and struggled because of it. His lectures are very quick and if you don't keep up with the information he's giving, you'll be very confused on the quizzes.

analysis.name: Chelsea Cantrell
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Although Cantrell is a kind and engaging lecturer, the course lacked organization. Assignments were graded very late, making it hard to track progress, and grading felt harsh with little explanation for point deductions. She also NEVER answers emails, so concerns are almost always never seen. Overall, she made the course structure very stressful.

NEVER EVER grades ANYTHING!!! Made's students do strange things to get her message across. For example, when the class wasn't participating enough, she asked everyone to stand up, everyone did, then put their right hand out, then pat their head. Cantrell "~Oh good, so now you can hear me, and you are using your brains." Just super disorganized.....

If there was a worst class to take at UF this would be up there. So disorganized, never know what is assigned, her homework is long and tedious, and she grades things at the last minute. Oh and, if you email her, expect it to be never answered or answered by the time you graduate.

Professor Cantrell is a good lecturer and always entertains our class. However, she was extremely bad with grading assignments and providing feedback. Our class only had around 3 assignments (out of 8-ish) graded by the time the semester ended, and then she batch-graded the rest in one day, and none of them had any feedback. Harsh grader IMO.

Pt1:
She is a nice person, lecture have good flow, the quizzes were easy. But she is too busy to respond emails and grade the assignments, so any question you should ask the TA that is very attentive. She had only graded 4 assignments when final had come and finished grading them until the final day. Only the final had detailed feedback.

analysis.name: Donald Monk
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: try taking the course with someone else. he only reads off the slides and doesn't even understand himself the complicated parts of the chapter. He will dwell on the easy parts though so he feels like he's actually teaching.

Took Monk for FAR1. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to help everyone succeed- you just have to put in the work outside of class. Ask questions and participate. His quizzes are fair. Exams are pretty difficult and the final is cumulative. Didn't have any practice exams on canvas, but Automatic helped me prepare a lot.

Monk is a very enthusiastic professor, but did an incredibly poor job at pacing his lectures. Would spend way too much time on minuscule details and often seemed as if he would rush finishing content days before exams. Provided no mocks or true practice questions, so was hard to get a gauge on how exams would be. Take someone else if possible.

His lectures would go off into tangents and he made no effort to give students practice problems outside of the textbook. The exam questions would look nothing like his quizzes or the homework problems. He claims to be a big picture kind of guy but also gets lost in the weeds of his own content. Take someone else if you need to take this class.

Professor Monk genuinely made lectures interesting and his class directly coincided with automatic tutoring. I would do the automatic tutoring packet before the chapter is taught in class and it was the best way I leaned the content.

analysis.name: John Banko
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 358 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Probably the worst class/professor of your college career. You'll be taught how to do the work in Excel, but you can't use Excel on the exams. Why? Well, in his own words, he's "evil." His advice is to run up and down the stadium stairs then take practice exams. Very practical. I felt confident based on lectures and practice problems, failed exams.

This guy is ridiculous. Flat out refuses to discuss exam grading or what questions may have been missed, even though he reserves right to test on those types of questions again. Honestly, doesn't care about you learning or not, just that he went through the motions. If majority of students are failing a test, is that not on the teacher?

If you could have taken this class a year ago with Tapley and didn't, kick yourself, because you just made the biggest mistake of your college career. Lack of a formula sheet for 50-100 formulas, no more charts that used to be given. Unnecessarily horrible for fairly reasonable material. The free response will destroy your will to live.

Banko is the worst instructor ever and his class is just awful. I am a straight-A student, 4.0 GPA, working on honors thesis. I worked VERY HARD in this class, paid for tutoring, and sacrificed a lot of time studying, but my best was not good enough. I still ended up with a C. I am not a finance major, but good luck to those who need an A or B.

What a horrible teacher.  Took it over Summer C and was a total waste of time and money.  He doesn't teach - he talks at you.  Test questions are many times harder than examples in the book, don't even try. My favorite saying was, we have too many finance majors so anyone who would normally get an A will get a C.   FABULOUS

analysis.name: David Lindberg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Honestly a very nice guy. Very acommodating with deadlines as long as you email him. Attendance is definitely a MUST if you want to pass because the material is quite difficult and it all continuously builds on previous lectures. Also there's 13 mandatory in class assignments that you can't make up. Overall a great explainer too.

Amazing professor. In class pop quizzes were scheduled so you really didn't have to be at class until those days. However, those are graded pretty strictly and are open note and collaborative. Would suggest going to class instead of asking peers for the notes. Exams are extremely fair, do the practice exam and you'll be fine.

Difficult class, but the professor was fantastic. The syllabus was incredibly in-depth with grading expectations, so I was never super lost when calculating my grade. He does NOT tell you your grade while you're completing the class, so you have to do it manually (he gives you the formula). If I need to take more math, I will absolutely choose him.

Professor Lindberg is easily the best professor in the Department of Stats and one of the best professors I have ever had. He knows so much and teaches so clearly; The breadth of my stats knowledge became so fleshed out after taking his class. He uses a lot of materials and does video reviews before the exam. I would take any class he teaches.

For such a large topic, Lindberg teaches the class very well. Attendance is required bcs pop quizzes, but they are open-note/collaborative. The exams are easy and he has prep sessions, examples, and formula sheets for each. He is a very specific grader, but if you show your work he gives full points on all assignments. Responds good to email!

analysis.name: Deborah  Smith
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Half the class will get a 60 or under on an exam but the class is "graded on a curve" so its okay? Lectures are very very tedious, and when you're working 40 hours a week, how can you expect me to spend a minimum of 12 of your class alone, as if I'm not attempting other courses as well. Don't like the grading style, 3 exams worth 70% of your grade.

Not approachable at all, tests were extremely complicated and hard to understand and when asked for feedback she denied completely. Lectures were too heavy and time demanding, makes it complicated to understand one lecture, takes hours. It seems as she wants her students to fail.

45-50 min lectures that take you 3.5 hours to get through on a fast day. Tests were FOUL, unfairly made and poorly written. Perusall assignments are not worth your time. Overall very disorganized and some of the lectures you cannot even understand. Class average for exams was around a 68%. Heavy curve but it doesn't get you an A. Deb is the worst!!

Not only a terrible class but very unprofessional. Would say exam grades would be given by a certain date and gave no update when she provided them well after the given date. Multiple people including myself after surprisingly bad exams asked for feedback on how to better prepare and were ghosted. It felt like she actively wanted us to fail.
The methodology used by this profesor is meant to make you feel. Not approachable to receive feedback. I would recommend to avoid this profesor.

analysis.name: Derek Hunt
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Super cool guy and actually does what he teaches in real life. Online labs are kinda annoying because they're pretty long, but they drill in information pretty well. Everything in this class is super applicable to real life and it feels like I'm learning actually useful things. Highly recommend taking this class for kicks and giggles.

While the use of medical acronyms can be a bit confusing at first, once you get a handle on them and understand them better, it becomes easier to understand the lectures and content. The first responder brand of humor is also a big positive for me.

He's been in the field a long time and has the stories and expertise to show for it. Your learning depends on how much effort you put in. You can skate by as an easy course, but if you're willing to, there's a lot of fun, important info to learn. Highly recommend attending his lectures on Zoom if possible.

I am an engineering major, this class has nothing to do with my field, but what a cool learning experience. From the beginning, there is so much you wouldn't even imagine you could learn in a 99 percent online class (only 2 labs in person). So much fun and boy does he have stories to tell.

Hunt is an amazing professor. He loves what he teaches and loves his students, even though online. He makes all quizzes open note, and gives you study guides to tell you what to know for the midterm and final. He eliminates A-, so anything 90 and above is an A, and he wants absolutely everyone to do well. He is overall an amazing guy!

analysis.name: Timothy Difato
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This course requires a lot of studying for exams! The professor ensures to give lots of preparation such as lectures, PowerPoints, study guides. Professor gave lots of curves for exams, which were very helpful! Very chill professor.

I had Professor Difato for Spring 2022; he is just outright amazing and chill. I always went to his office hours to ask questions on my quizzes (I usually was the only one there but that gave us 1 on 1 time) and he provides detailed feedback on what to fix. The quizzes are extremely fair, just watch the lectures and you'll do fine! Amazing class!

Mr. Difato is very clear/engaging. Quizzes are fair, and very few assignments. However, the textbook makes up a lot of stuff (ex: tries to quantify concepts by making up equations) and he blindly teaches by it. Solid lecturer, but this course needs new content. Makes students call on each other, but you can't call on people with their hand up?

While she posts the slides, attendance is technically required and you will learn a lot more by attending them

I thought she was good teacher, I found her easy to follow along and study for but there was a cheating incident in my test room and she had us all retake the exam and I truly belive it was harder and included questions from topics we were not told to study and blamed those of us who did nothing wrong. She also is not clear when asking questions.
there was a cheating situation and she punished the students that didn't do anything.

Didn't read the textbook nor did I pay attention to any of the lectures. Although from what I heard in the background she seemed good. I only used smoking notes and just read it a bunch before the exam and was able to succeed.

One thing I forgot to mention in the comment that I wrote below is to definitely started studying at least a few days out or a week or 2 out if you're behind in lecture and just focus on the big picture stuff

analysis.name: David Lucier

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Lucier is so sweet. You can tell he cares about his classes and he wants you to succeed. He's a great professor and is very helpful. You get what you give in this class and it's very important to show up.

Professor Lucier had so many examples from his experience in the industry. Each module had an assignment or a quiz. He is a quick grader with good feedback. There is a midterm, final, and big group project due at the end of the semester. Most of the grade comes from your own part of the project, with a smaller portion for the overall project.

I was David's first class that he taught and he was absolutely AMAZING! He cares about the students and incorporated a lot of his experiences that he has had into his lecture. It may say to get a textbook, but he gives you all of the materials to do well. 2 exams, 1 group project and presentation, about 10 small assignments. He is such a great guy.
Really enjoyed my class with this professor. Greatly recommend!!!
Lucier is an incredible professor, he makes class enjoyable. I wish he taught more courses because I would take him a thousand times.

analysis.name: Gianna Englert
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ms. Englert is hands down the best professor that I have ever had. She makes long readings easy to digest while also catching your interest. If I could take her class again I would love to. Looking forward to the next class I may be able to take of hers.
Very engaging lecturer and great professor. Loves what she teaches and really cares about her students.

I could not recommend Professor Englert more. She was the most kind, understanding, and brilliant teacher I've ever taken. She just has a way of producing discussion and making you always feel involved. When she talks it is so easy to listen. She is insanely knowledgeable, the best at UF.

I have never been a fan of politics and am quite uneducated on the subject, yet taking this class was extremely manageable. Weekly readings and in depth discussion daily. Discussion is open and quite fun. AWESOME PROFESSOR who cares about her students. Office hours are super helpful (especially for essays). 

All good things here!
Professor Englert has a phenomenal understanding of all of the texts we read in class, and leads thought-provoking conversations. She has been my favorite professor at UF- I definitely recommend her!

analysis.name: Eleni Papadopoulou
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very sweet professor! Vocab quizzes are easy if you make flashcards when she hands out the weekly vocab and the exams aren't impossible. LOTS of extra credit opportunities to boost grade. She does call on random people to help answer questions, but she works through the answer with you if you're struggling. Very non judgmental zone
Very sweet and caring! She creates a non-judgmental learning environment and takes the time to break down every concept with patience and respect. I would gladly take any class she teaches.
Gives lots of extra credit and makes things very easy to understand and do. Super nice and very non-judgmental. There's no awkwardness around making mistakes. Very clear in expectations.
Very caring. Breaks everything down and makes sure all the students understand the materials.

Wonderful teacher! I put "2-Easy" because I thought it was super easy, but I've also been doing Latin for a decade so it may have been easier for me than others. However, I still think it was an easy class. She explained everything so well and there was extra credit on every single assignment.

analysis.name: Elinore Fresh
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Do not take this course. It is both unnecessarily hard and you learn nothing practical. There's an unclear grading rubric, you have to hope you translated things the same way she does, and she loves to play devil's advocate/ragebait. Class is her showing off she can read Chinese or going down rabbit holes.

Ai Laoshi is a very good professor. I was a bit nervous taking the class because many students in the class were already Chinese or had some background, but she made it easy to learn. There are a lot of vocabulary quizzes and homework every week, but the coursework is not too much. She is always willing to help and answer questions!

Class is very fast paced and if you don't have a background in Chinese it will be more difficult but Ai Laoshi is pretty generous on grading with homework assignments since she takes off decimals for mistakes. Vocab quizzes are very frequent where you have to know the character, pinyin, and definition in English, but again she takes off decimals.

People say that Ai Laoshi is a difficult professor, but it's the language makes the class challenging. Chinese is a hard language to learn, and traditional makes it worse, but Ai Laoshi is very understanding and flexible. If you are motivated to learn or already speak Chinese, I highly recommend taking the class.

Ai Laoshi (Professor Fresh's name in Chinese class) is fantastic! She is very knowledgeable on the subject and has many interesting stories about the time she spent in China. The class is hard; it is quick paced and the quizzes are definitely tough. However, this is essential for effectively learning Chinese. I would definitely recommend her.

analysis.name: Mahtab Eskandar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

Lecture was vague and unorganized, questions unanswered and she seemed unprepared

analysis.name: Evan Lauteria

Skipped basically the last 2 months of lecture and still got an A. Highly recommend.

Gave us online "games" to play and write essays about, very straightforward. A couple of easy worksheets. Two exams that weren't bad. You don't really need to read. Skipped the last half of semester and just reviewed the slides he posted. I would recommend attending lecture at least once a week if you plan to skip though.

amazing. attendance is not mandatory, 90 is an A, 2 exams (worth only 30% of your grade), 4 short papers with lenient graders, one of which gets dropped including zeroes for no submission, and he's funny. first professor i willingly loved going to class for, please take him. not a single bad thing i have to say i hope he wins the lottery

dr. lauteria is goated. he's so enthusiastic about the course and makes going to class enjoyable. just make sure you get a good group for group projects, but even if your group sucks you'll be fine. exams r based off of his lectures/slides. despite the class being relatively easy, i definitely learned a lot!! take him if u can

Great lecturer; kept me extremely engaged. There's 2 exams that are super easy as long as you know the vocab he gives you. Four homework assignments are playing a video game, talking about them in groups, and writing short papers about them (easy and fun). Attendance is extra credit. Take this professor.

Her quizzes had little to do with the topic of the class and I found her to be unreasonable

Hind is enthusiastic and likes her course but it is extremely boring and useless.

Loved this class! It was a great class to take during freshman year since there's a lot of group discussion. Prof. Hind is passionate about what she teaches and makes each class interesting.
There's an assigned reading for each lecture/class. No tests but there's 4 major essays. You'll do fine if you go to her office hours and revise with her
She's a terrible teacher. The worst professor I ever had. Avoid her if you can.

HOPE Humans Oil Energy & Plants. professor is good and extremely passionate, but assigns a lot of readings that do not relate much to the essays. you can write about anything for each topic and she will grade for credit. go to office hours and talk with her to discuss how to improve paper, will not be a hard grader. LOTS OF READINGS!

She sometimes seems slightly scary, but she's so nice and helpful. She also gives you very good feedback.

She was very nice and sweet, but I hated this class, she just read off the screen. From someone who isn't majoring in classics, this class was useless, and I hated coming to it. There's a minimum of 3 discussions, a group presentation, 12 quizzes ever Friday, a midterm, and a final. I passed, but this area isn't my strong suit it was just so boring

I loved her class. She meets students where they're at, and she's very knowledgable about her specialties. If she's teaching anything about Augustan age elegy, I'd highly recommend it. She's also very strict on attendance, but if you're someone who participates and clearly isn't just skipping for fun, she's very understanding about it.

She was a great teacher! Her Latin classes are definitely a bit harder than some of the other ones in the department, but they're not bad at all. She seems a little scary sometimes, but she's not, she's super nice!

It was more of a Latin literature class than i was expecting, and WAY more of an augustan-age class than i was expecting, but it was a great class overall! She was knowledgable, and very helpful with answering questions after class.

analysis.name: Matt Friedl
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Content is interesting, but Friedl just reads off the slides (attendance unnecessary). Exams are very specific, hard to study for, memorize the slides basically (you get a cheat sheet tho). He makes an interesting class fairly boring - not very engaging, monotone, very rigid guy (stern on not rounding and such). Not the worst but not a good choice.

Majority of grade based on group projects and exams, which he does not know any of the information if you ask questions. group projects are tough if given a bad group, and exams are almost impossible to study for. graded by 2 exams (60% of grade) and perusall assignments (5% of grade). cheat sheet for exam is not useful

His lectures are straightforward and easy to follow along, plus he had memes sprinkled throughout. Each week, we were assigned ~2 Perusall articles and needed 4 decent comments on each article. He allowed us to handwrite a one-page note-sheet for each exam, which led me to getting a perfect score on the final. No extra credit, not needed anyway.

Dr. Friedl is a good professor, it's just the class that is pretty boring. The 2 exams are 60% of your grade so they are pretty important, but he allows you to use the front and back of a paper of hand written notes. There's quite a bit of reading each and using Perusall, but honestly if you just do it you'll get the credit; it's graded by an AI.

This professor is honestly one of the worst professors I've ever had at UF. I received a decent grade in his class (A-), but his lectures were extremely monotonous and he was extremely unaccommodating and unfriendly. Additionally, not only was there an excessive amount of reading, he also was quite slow to respond to emails. 10/10 don't recommend.

analysis.name: Feihong Wang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: SUPER interesting course!!! Great professor. Pretty hard not to get an A on diaries and discussion if you just follow the rubric. Quizzes are pretty simple. Professor Wang was really fun to have and genuinely cared about the class she was teaching. My only issues with the class is that all grading is done by TAs and some of them are very strict with the prompts, and also the exams were open book, but all the exam content was indeed from the book with lectures being very minimal content wise.

The textbook used for this course is super information heavy and hard to take good notes on. The exams & quizzes are open note, but exams are not nearly as easy as the quizzes & the lectures don't really help unless they are directly asked about in the exams. Ctrl F is your friend for this class. Discussion posts & diary entries weren't hard either

She is very sweet and caring, you can tell she cares about her students and wants them to know there is always help from her or TAs. The class wasn't much work, just discussion posts and weekly quizzes. The only thing was the online exams, even though they are open textbook and notes, the questions were very niche/specific. Lock in for the project!

Listen, the class wasn't that difficult, but I literally only scraped by with an A which is insane considering it's psych. Her exams are more of a "find extremely niche information mentioned in one sentence in the textbook" rather than applying relevant knowledge. The lectures were barely relevant. It wasn't horrible, but I wouldn't take it again.

analysis.name: Jack Famiglietti

Very hard to get an A in this class, because this is the most work you will ever do for a 2 credit class. DO NOT put off the project deadlines and be sure to put good effort. He's a pretty good teacher, not a good  test maker. Put things on the test he barely mentioned in lecture. Overall very fun class learned how to use mills, lathes, weld, etc.

Pretty dull instructor, reacted pretty poorly to the class failing the second exam and presented the curve as charity rather than taking personal accountability. New professor but needs much improvement

Failed the entire class on an exam and blamed us for "not studying hard enough". He's new and clearly has no idea what he's doing and though he says he cares about improving his actions suggest otherwise

Dr. Familgietti is an amazing professor. He is always willing to work with the students and give them feedback on their projects. He is VERY clear about what he expects work-wise.

DML is inherently a hard course, but if you show up to lectures, PAY ATTENTION TO THE ANNOUNCEMENTS, and attend office hours on occasion, you will do perfectly fine

analysis.name: Eric Schwartz

I spent 40 hours on lab 2 in order to earn 53/100 if that tells you anything about him.

Don't expect to learn much of anything during lectures. Schwartz's approach to teaching is woefully inadequate and ineffective, and largely consists of messy powerpoint presentations coupled with his inarticulate and unfocused narration. However, the labs are generally very well devised, and most of the learning will happen here.

Too much material in the course. You don't have time to get in depth. Expect to gloss over every topic and memorize just enough to get by.   Schwartz just reads powerpoint slides so lectures are useless although mandatory. Textbook is essential to actually learn anything.

I have easily spent 250 hours on this course. 8 labs total, averaging 30+ hours per lab, Plus test prep. If you take this professor you will be completely at the mercy of the TA's in regards to learning. Currently I am on the border of passing the class, depending on how well I did on the final. I was warned not to take him. I didn't listen.

analysis.name: Meagan Frenzer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She makes me want to — myself. There are so many assignments and on each one there are four annotations needed. I can understand this until it's 10-15 assignments each week with four annotations each. And they're graded harshly even when it was clear that effort was made. Would not rec; she's a kind person, but would not want her as a prof again.

2/5. You do learn a lot in this class, but the workload is overwhelming. There are about 7 assignments each week, and each requires 4 annotations. The grading is unclear and inconsistent, with no feedback at all. Some assignments go ungraded for weeks, then many grades are posted at once, making it hard to know how to improve.

Everything about her and her class was lovely. Her lectures were very informative and interesting. She gives extra credit opportunities. She is not a hard grader as long as you follow the prompts, she gives great feedback on assignments and how to improve next time . Would totally take again.

Professor Frenzer's love and excitement for history is reflected in lectures. Her lectures are energized and engaging, but also move at a fast pace. This class is a reading intensive class more than it is a writing intensive class. She grades fairly and justly: the grades she gives are very reasonable. I highly recommend taking Professor Frenzer.

She's a great professor and moves things around when theres an unfortunate event, but as long as you do the journals and show up to class you should be fine. Lectures cover things about the journals but if you dont show up your grade will drop 1/3 of a letter grade which is insane. Also grades come in late and at the end of semester so just beware.

analysis.name: Faris Kronfli
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would highly recommend this class for psych majors needing to fulfill their requirements. Dr. Kronfli is very easy to reach and willing to help answer any questions. There are no exams, just a discussion post, reading guide, quiz, and group project due every 2 weeks. Very manageable :)

I thought this class was a great experience. The guidelines are very clear and the workload is incredibly reasonable. The workload is not excessive and due bi-weekly. I felt like I learned so much and the assignments helped me retain what I learned. I would definitely recommend this class and teacher!

Professor Iwamoto was great! Of course, Japanese language courses have a lot of coursework, but that's the nature of the course. So if you don't mind that and you have the opportunity to take a class with Professor Iwamoto, you should!
He has high energy and ensures every student in his class understands the grammar. His office hours are useful too

Professor Iwamoto is one of the best professors I've ever had! He made learning Japanese (which by itself is a very difficult topic) digestible and created a fun and interactive learning environment. I think he does a lot to make sure students don't feel to nervous to speak and encourages everyone to try their best.
The best professor I've ever had, and you can tell he enjoys what he's doing. Average level of difficulty for a language class, but he genuinely wants to help you succeed.

analysis.name: Ivy Munoko
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Munoko was one of my favorite UF professors. Her flipped classroom approach encouraged collaboration and made it easy to ask questions. She covered many useful topics, and although only two exams made up most of the grade, they were fair and reflected the material.

Munoko is quite possibly the best professor in the accounting department. Pay attention to her lectures, read the textbook and do the practice questions she gives to prepare for the exams. Definitely not a free A, but most of the class gets at least a B. Classwork was annoying cause she doesn't drop any assignments so you have to go to every class.

Not bad! I just made quizlets of everything she says in the pre-class lecture videos and I got a B on exam 1. Exams are 70% of your grade, so do the +2% extra credit. Assignments are easy A's if you don't miss any classes class since they're done in class and hard to complete alone. But she is accommodating and helpful if you must miss.

Dr. Munoko is a very nice person, but her exams are worded strangely and material will be presented in a strange manner that is not introduced at any other time in the course. There are only two exams which make up 70% of your final grade. Despite this, she might be the "best" professor to take for BP.

I really liked Munoko, she cared about the students and pretty much all of the non-exam grades were easy 100s. Beware of the exams though, they were brutal and it was really easy to think you knew more than you did. I ended up doing poorly on the first exam and hustling to raise my grade on the final, but there was a nice curve.

analysis.name: Jesse Kim
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Kim is a good guy. He posts all his lectures in a very organized fashion, and attendance is not mandatory. He's a solid lecturer; he had no issue pausing to explain any concepts students didn't get. His exams are extremely fair, akin to some of the harder homework problems. Only gripe is that the weekly homeworks can be pretty time consuming.

Professor Kim is a great lecturer, and I never had to use any of Shabazz's online lectures. He goes deep in depth to the mechanics of the material taught and it helped me understand and wrap my head around the concepts. For Calc 3 at UF as a whole, the homework is annoying and repetitive (but helpful), and the quizzes and exams are easy.

Chill lectures but pretty indistinguishable from Shabazz's posted online. Every calc 3 teacher teaches off the same set of notes so it doesn't really matter who you take. Overall the most important thing is to just to do practice tests before the exam and you should do fine. I found modules 2 and 3 to be the easiest so dont stress after exam 1.

Good professor, but I started going to Shabazz's lectures instead and liked hers a lot better. When I did only go to his, the lectures are good and I like that he uses Desmos3D so we can visualize, but sometimes he goes too fast or explains things too in depth before we learn enough about the topic to really understand.

I stopped going to class in person and only used the online lectures, they were very good. Homework is not horrible and you get several days per assignment. There are homework and quiz drops. Lots of extra credit given for doing practice exams. I was able to easily put this class on the backburner and still get an A.

analysis.name: James Biondi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: the nicest professor I've ever had at UF. He genuinely loves the subject he teaches and makes it so so interesting! Grades pretty easy as long as you literally just go to class and listen to him.  Anyone who says he grades hard probably just never went to class because his essay prompts for the exam are so predictable.

Teaches extremely well. Easy to talk to, will listen to any questions you have and will help expand on them. Extremely smart and informative, does not judge students differently based on beliefs, but rather allows them to expand on their beliefs and demonstrates the importance of learning about all sides of a political conflict.
If you memorize the slides and listen to lectures you will be fine. There are readings but you do not need to do them at all. The exams are straightforward and straight from the slides.

He is an ok professor. Clearly passionate about what he teaches but he does not grade exams well. He will not give clear feedback on exams and grades somewhat subjectively. I do not really recommend, take another class if you can. I don't want to be unkind but thought I would share my experience.

James was honestly a terrible professor overall. While the class information was interesting he honestly made it feel boring. He would just ramble in class and then grade your essays based on his personal opinions. He has no rubrics and uses participation to tank your grade. Don't take this class and tell everyone you know no to. Have a nice day :)

analysis.name: Jason Von Meding
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took Quest 1 Human Shelter Development.The class was pretty easy, 3 projects that aren't difficult, a discussion and open-note quiz every 2 weeks, and optional in-class assignments. Attendance wasn't manadatory but the lectures aren't recorded. However, I do recommend going to class because the lectures are interesting. He was great & so cool!!

An amazing (and very easy) option for a Quest 1 class. Even though you aren't required to go to class, it's honestly interesting material. There are a couple projects but honestly all are pretty simple. Just be aware that the final project is a group, so be scouting out people you'd want to work with during the year (benefit of going to class).

Very easy Quest 1 class. Lectures are optional (most of class does not go) and not needed to do well on the Canvas quizzes. They have some good information if you're interested in the topic, but can be a snooze fest if not. No exams. The major grades in the class are projects: 2 individual and 1 group. Would 100% recommend.

Dr. Von Meding is an amazing professor! I took him for my quest 1 class during summer B. He's extremely caring and he really wants you to learn and succeed in his course. The workload also isn't super bad especially for the whole course being complete in 6 weeks! Make sure you have a good group for your big group project and you'll be set.

Professor Von Meding was great! He is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. If you have the chance to take him for Quest 1, I would highly recommend doing so, especially over the summer. Guidelines were super clear and all the TAs were awesome. 10/10 would recommend.

analysis.name: Ashley Jones
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very long and very boring lectures that are extremely hard to follow along with. She never gives any assignments, no group works, no discussions so I have not retained a single ounce of information. When the midterm came, she only gave us two days to prepare and 85% of the information given on her “study slides” was not used on the test at all.

Not difficult at all, but make sure you actually attend class because participation brought my grade down to the point where I had to do extra credits to get an A. The actual lectures are so boring and uninspiring due to how monotonous she speaks even with interesting topics, but she is generally nice. The TA was great however!

Do not be lured in by the title of the quest class. She is an Art History professor and will make whatever class you take only about art. Most boring lectures of my life and they wasted so many hours I won't get back. It is not a terribly hard quest class but there are way easier ones out there. Overall, don't waste your time if you have a choice.

Take another Quest 1 if u can. The lectures were dull with Prof Jones presenting in a dark hall using PowerPoints with only pictures & no real content, making studying hard. However, both Professor Jones & the TAs were nice. I just wish the course had a more engaging structure & captivating lectures. 30 points ext credit tho. Participation graded.

Most boring class I've ever taken in my entire life, no hyperbole. The lectures are mandatory, but it is difficult to pay attention to her lectures as she runs on monotonously. Even if you can manage to maintain attention, she goes on random tangents, making 80% of the info covered in lecture stuff you don't need. Discussion with TA was amazing.

analysis.name: Piyush Jain
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is honestly one of the nicest teachers I have ever met. If you don't understand something, he's willing to meet with you and guide you to understanding. The book is definitely helpful so you should get it! Go to office hours and do practice problems often to get a firm grasp of the content. You will be fine if you put effort into the class!
Very straightforward with what each exam will be on, whenever you dont understand anything hes always willing to help
Great class, just keep up with the homework and you'll do well on the quizzes and tests. Gives appropriate grades and ensures the whole class won't fail, unlike other professors.
Very nice guy, and I would say he is a very solid professor compared to a lot of the other ones I have had at UF. He is always willing to help if you can't understand something.
Had Dr. Jain for the Pharmaceutical Engineering class. Great professor and easy class. Everything is graded extremely generously.

analysis.name: Jamie Gillooly
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Be prepared to come to his lectures! He doesn't do clicker questions, but he supplements a lot of the information in class rather than putting them all on the slides. I liked how he would give us lots of examples and tell us about news connected to our learnings. Unfortunately, we didn't get a practice exam, but I still felt prepared for the exam.

Don't know why people were clapping for him the morning of the exam in his “review session”. No practice tests and twists test answers to make you feel confused. Easiest unit material wise, but the hardest exam. Without smoking notes Idk how you would pass. Makes himself out to be some famous biologist when in reality he publishes some garbage.
You must attend his lectures to understand what is going on, but he makes the lectures interesting, and he uses examples to explain concepts, which is helpful.

Professor Gillooly was very passionate about the section he was teaching in our class. One thing I found to be really annoying was the lack of a practice exam, and how almost every question on the exam was phrased weirdly and had confusing answer choices. Definitely attend his lectures because that is where most of the content is explained well.

Dr. Gillooly is a passionate and highly knowledgeable lecturer. He taught the evolution section of my BSC2010 course. Do yourself a favor and attend every one of his lectures, take effective notes, and make sure to pace the lectures with the associated textbook readings. If you do this diligently, success in his unit will come easily.

analysis.name: Kara Riggs
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you are taking genetics, take it with Riggs. I have heard horror stories of genetics, and I'm so happy I took it with Riggs because my experience hasn't been near that. Her exams aren't hard, and she doesn't use an A- in her grading scale. She also doesn't let you make up exams, but does drop your lowest exam grade, including the final.

Dr Riggs is the sweetest professor! She is so understanding and gracious. If you truly show up and show you care, you'll get the A. No homework pretty much and easy assignments plus extra credit. You WILL regret not taking her within your time at UF. Only issue is textbook required is like $130 but if you message her she will find a way!

There were only a few assignments but they were very straightforward and the exams were super easy. She provides studyguides for each exam and as long as you fill them out and memorize them you'll be well prepared.
