The exam averages and medians were all super high and overall this is a good course if you want a simple life science elective!

Easy class. She records lectures and I find her to be clear&quick. The subject isnt hard and you only have to watch a video and do one quiz a week. Two projects required. She responds quickly and kindly. My one critique is that the tests would ask some questions that had never been said in the lecture OR slides. Honorlock exams.

Took this over summer A. I expected the class to be tough because it was a 6 week course, but I actually thought it was fairly easy. The exams are wayyyy easier than the homeworks, so don't let them overwhelm you. TAs did an exam review before each exam. Exam every week since it was summer A, but lowest is dropped, lowest hw dropped and lots of ec.

analysis.name: Thomas Knight
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Class is very test heavy, with no extra credit offered. Two lowest quiz scores dropped but in reality they hardly change your gradebook unless you get a 0. The grading scheme syllabus is just ridiculous, the lowest test score I got was an 80 and then got 95's on the last two exams and I still have an A- and he won't budge.

Professor Knight's short lectures are incredibly helpful. He doesn't cover everything, but you'll only need to skim through the textbook for the remaining concepts. Tests make up your entire grade, and the concepts become more challenging as the semester goes on. I strongly recommend studying previous exams if you want to pass this class.

This class was hybrid, so it was lectures online (and he had an in-person option, but I just never went). But this class was extremely lecture-heavy and test-heavy. He's a great, funny guy, but he doesn't really care about students. There's no extra credit, and tests count for 75% of your grade, and 12 quizzes count 25% of your grade.

Test HEAVY. Econ has never been my strong suit; however, had a graduate econ major tutoring me and scratching his head at some of the wording of practice test questions. Studied the previous exams as noted in reviews and was confused on exam day. Nice enough professor, hate how test heavy this class is.
Test heavy. Does not care about students, no extra credit.

analysis.name: Karim Asghari
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 215 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The material is overall simple but his tests are brutal. His lectures seem okay to comprehend and his study guide is helpful. The test questions are tricky despite it being multiple choice because each choice is not straight forward and has a multitude of options such as all of the above , none of the above, A and B or A,B and C or B and E.

Worst professor ever. He knows his stuff but is not a great teacher. Lectures are hard to understand. UF really needs to make this course and in-seat class. The test are very difficult to study for because his questions are very specific. He ends class 2 weeks early? Why not distribute that time throughout the course. Step it up UF!

The material itself wasn't too bad but his tests were ridiculously difficult. They're multiple choice but the options go like A, A &B, B &C, all of the above, two of the above, none of the above! You have to know the material in detail. Smokin notes help as long as you're ready to remember each and every word of it. You have to work really hard!!

This class was honestly awful. I dont understand how people thought this class was good. The exams have so many grammar mistakes and are very tricky. Buy smokin notes and literally know every little detail. do the extra credit As well. Didnt feel like the lectures were good for exams and hes not a good communicator or very nice but JMO.

This class was harder than I expected. You don't go to class, you just watch his lectures (about 3 a week, 1 hour ish each). There are 4 exams that make up your grade, but he offers some extra credit. I put this class on a pedestal and did everything in my power to do well, and I still got Cs on his exams, even when I felt confident.

analysis.name: Rick Lind
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Far and away the worst professor I had at UF. Aero Design course is chaotic. Decades out of touch with industry, denying value of iterative design or DFM in aerospace. Condescending, frequently snaps and even curses at students. Nearly every word he says in 1-on-1 conversation is sarcastic. Behavior could fly for a more talented engineer...

You can tell he knows his stuff so well that he sometimes has trouble explaining things on a level that someone learning it for the first time would understand. Study a lot and his exams are generally pretty fair. Love that there is a project at the end of the semester. Write down everything he says and ur good. He is a little condescending though.

Lind is a di*k, but he does give extra credit so hes really not that bad of a guy. He can be reasonable, just dont ask to postpone a test date for a LSU football roadtrip, he will rip you a new one. He rarly helps during office hrs and sometimes turns you away before you ask anything. Study the Notes 100x and youll be OK. Rework all notes/examples

I feel like Lind isn't getting enough credit on here. Yes, he is ridiculously hard, and he expects more out of you than any other professor that I have had in my five years here. And yes, I wish he were easier on us. However, I learned more in his class than I learned in any other course at UF. Put in the hours, and you will be rewarded.
This dudes chill, but i dont really understand why he wouldn't let us have a cheat sheet or use a calculator. I still don't understand why memorization is being used. But ig hes chill

analysis.name: Tobias Lodemann
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The exams are the same for both Dr. Lodemann's and Dr. Sefair's classes, so I recommend taking Dr. Sefair's section since he is the professor in charge of the course, and the one who best explains the contents of the course.

Dr. Lodemann is really sweet personality wise; however, he seems to never come to class prepared. I have had him now for two separate classes, and I have seen a theme of him not being able to answer questions regarding the material, homework, or gives the wrong answers in class. He does not prepare students for the exams and is very disorganized.

This guy barely understands his own material and uses another teacher's slides. I was better off reading the slides on my own. His tests are really badly written and meant to trick, not to test knowledge. Class is very easy and could have been taught in a month if it weren't taught by him.
He's a nice guy and cares about his students, but he is a pretty bad lecturer and the class is pretty difficult. Take it with someone else if possible.

analysis.name: Willard Scott Keeran
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 257 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Probably one of the more boring professors you'll have, but I did like the way the class was set up. The workbook (which was about $20 from Target Copy) was very helpful in terms of following along in class and for studying. Some of the tests were more difficult than they needed to be. Overall not too bad.. The average grade was 82% for perspective

Worst experience in a class ever. Calc 3 in and of itself isn't difficult, but Keeran makes it  1000% more difficult than it needs to be. The exams  are VERY unfair and have absolutely nothing to do with the lecture notes or homework for the most part. The practice exams he posts are cake in comparison to the real thing. HIGHLY DO NOT RECOMMEND.

I took one exam and I'm already incredibly flustered with how things have gone. He tests hard, but during lectures, he says things will be very easy. Plus, he doesn't offer a lot of extra credit, so it's hard. Coming from a student who loves and has high interest in Calculus, this class was made difficult by him.

He seems like he hates teaching and is always in a bad mood, but that might just be his personality because he is super sarcastic. He also kind of looks like the food critic from Ratatouille. He writes faster than I can think and is pretty bad at explaining most things. If you have taken calc before you're fine. If not, don't take his class.
Horrible. Condescending. I did not find him fair. Hard tests. Lightly touches upon topics.

analysis.name: Michael Link
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Link seems well-meaning, giving extra credit, extending deadlines, bringing food, and being active on Discord, but the class is chaotic and stressful. Exams run past midnight, content is overloaded, grading is extremely slow, instructions constantly change, is constantly fear mongering about AI, and students are left constantly anxious.

He cares, but he comes to class under-prepared. The exams and labs are broken to the point of it being detrimental to the class. His fearmongering is worse than Professor Schwartz, The lecture material does not prepare you for the exams, There are people who display culty behavior when talking about him. Pls avoid his class unless u knw wht u doin.

He means well. Weird student fans that sees no problem with 6+ hour exams. Impossible to reach outside of class for anything important. Constant stress over AI and the honor court, even if you did nothing wrong. Canvas is so messy and retakes are so disorganized you can't keep track. Everything takes months to get graded, even if it's auto-graded.

Pretty good guy, cares a lot about his students and put a lot of work into the class. He spread himself thin adjusting for the class, the retakes/extensions helped students but it also made the class more unstructured and slow. Hard to get him to post practice materials/readings/activities/class slides/projects/grades (anything) remotely on time.

The class is a mess. Lectures dont teach you anything. The culture is off. Prof speaks like a child, fearmongers and has a I know it all and you should have known this attitude. Class consumes loads of your time. I second a previous comment that there is a cultish feel exhibited by some.

analysis.name: Sheridan Lea
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Taking Prof. Lea for Skeleton Keys. Super interesting course and Prof. Lea's commentary is kinda hilarious. Her tests were on Canvas and open note, but you don't really need notes if you pay attention in class and copy down her ppts. Note that she does quick participation quizzes as attendance. Definitely recommend!

She's super sweet and very passionate about her studies. The class is relatively simple, exams are open book and quite literally pulled straight from the textbook. Lectures follow the textbook pretty tightly although you need to be present for in class assignments. Super chill, answers emails pretty fast, and very down to Earth and understanding

Sheridan is so much fun to take a class with! She is so passionate about the content, and it shows. Sometimes she moves quite fast through lecture slides, which are not always promptly posted after class, but she is overall amazing! She is flexible, always makes herself available, and gave us a tour of the Pound Lab on the last day. Love her!

This course is overloaded with busywork. 12 labs that aren't hard but are tedious and time-consuming. Ms. Lea was pleasant, but grading was extremely slow. One assignment was docked 10 points for being 3 hours late… after they took a month to grade it. Honestly, it was almost funny. No meaningful feedback was given. The class is probably too big.
Exams make up most of your grade, but they are open book, so it is easy. There are in class assignments, so make sure to attend. Otherwise, an easy class.

analysis.name: Michael Moulton
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 101 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I mean... This class was ridiculously easy and I would recommend it to anyone who needs an easy elective. I finished the course within a month, if that helps; you could finish it in a day if you put your mind to it. Answers are easily accessible, two attempts on exams, and the final is optional. ANYONE can pass this class - seriously! TAKE IT!

I took this Summer B. The professor is very funny and passionate about teaching the subject. He has long office hours, and is very accommodating. There was a movie played once or twice a week, and attendance was not mandatory. Only problem was the online software did not work on my computer so I had to do it at the library.

Easiest A ever + fully online! Took this class to meet my science gen ed requirement (and I'm not a science person at all). Every week there are short lectures (5-20 min), short readings + annotations, 3 discussion posts, and 2 quizzes. This may seem like a lot, but his requirements to get 100 on each assignment are super easy and takes max 2 hrs.

This class is such an easy A, there is no way you can fail out of this class. You have a week to complete set assignments and readings which won't take you over 2 hours (if that) to complete. Be ready to complete discussions which end up being interesting as you and your peers discuss what you found interesting about that week's module.
Easy A. Barely even a class. Just let Quizlet do the work for you.

analysis.name: Larissa Williamson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 387 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Between much too wordy definitions with far too few examples to illustrate what they are telling me, multiple choice questions designed to trip me up in the semantics, and the mousiest personality I have ever seen in an adult, this class is easy, but supremely grating on my nerves. Easy because what I don't get I can Google.

Her lectures are verbatim printouts of what is covered in the text. She does not elaborate on the points she discusses; rather, she merely sits in front of the printouts, annotates them, and reads them aloud. You can easily just read the text yourself; her lectures don't add anything new. Very disappointed with the quality of this course.

GET STUDY EDGE it is the only reason I learned anything. Attendance is mandatory but you can log on and do it from anywhere. Lectures are her filling in blanks on the lessons. There's a lot of homework which helped me learn but it's a no calculator class and there are questions that make you use one. Also a CODING group project….. good luck!!

Absolutely terrible professor. You cant understand her at all which means you will have to teach everything yourself. Homework and quizzes are straight bs and her notes dont explain anything at all. She is no help at all and graded one of my exams wrong and was adamant on not rounding up my grade less than 0.1% so I could get an A.

Take it online. Attendance mandatory but could do LC at home. Random coding project. And lock in for midterms or u might get cooked. Final has no overall practice but question are similar from year to year. Not difficult class as long as u know how to manage without a teacher.

analysis.name: Missy Shabazz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 243 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Shabazz is by far the best math professor that I have had so far. Her class can be challenging and some weeks she likes to go crazy with the homework/quizzes, but overall her class is manageable. She is very friendly, has conversations during lecture, and is willing to help anyone who asks for it. I would definitely recommend her to everyone.
Great teacher, cares about students and is very helpful and available outside of class :-)

Dr Shabazz is overall a nice person, but the worst teacher. There's homework due every day which can take hours to complete, and had nothing to do with the exams. It was a major struggle for me. The only reason I pulled off a decent grade was because of the extra credit. If you want to do well, get study edge, because the class will be a nightmare.

Class is very organized, and her lectures make the content accessible & easy to understand. The online resources (past tests, lectures, practice problems) make preparing for the exams and quizzes painless. As long as you stay on top of lecture due dates, this class has very lax grading. Exams have gotten easier compared to the older ones in Canvas.

Dr. Shabazz is by far the best calc 3 professor in the UF math department. Although I can understand some negative reviews saying she sometimes skips basic steps, making it hard to follow along, that is the nature of the course and you will not find a better lecturer. We always finished on time; she gives 3% extra credit and partial credit on FRQs.

analysis.name: Neha Rani
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her lectures were completely a waste of time and she looked like she didn't want to be teaching. We were not prepared by her lectures or the TA's discussion to create the main group project. All the documentation assignments took away from our time teaching ourselves full-stack dev and it seemed like busy work. This class was so frustrating.

Essentially a semester-long group project with hours and hours of useless busywork sprinkled in. During lectures, all she does is read off slides with near-zero emotion in her voice. The only reason to attend class is the required, completely unrelated in-class assignment every week. Easy A, but the biggest waste of time I've ever been put through.

really easy class, i didn't go to class at all after the first week. attendance not required and there is no point to go to class because its all group projects outside of class with no exams so no content to learn. didn't really learn anything in this class from the prof, just learning stuff when doing projects... have a competent group

This class is full of pointless busy work—weekly activities with long readings and lectures where she just reads off the slides. I was excited for Intro to Software Engineering, but Rani made it dull and unhelpful. The only good part is the group project, but even that comes with weeks where we have 3-4 useless assignments due.
Lectures are useless when it comes to learning anything useful for software engineering. Every week there is an in-class assignment that is a complete waste of time.

analysis.name: Melanie  Viege
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took this online class because I had to and I hated it. Seriously  take CHM1025 in class not online, here you will learn nothing. As long as you do your homework and other assignments you'll at least pass. However, Viege is a really bad at explaining things and is very unhelpful.

Professor Viege was fine for an online class. Of course, it is hard to rate a professor that isn't that involved in the course as an on campus course, but for what the class was, she made it very easy to keep track of due dates and deadlines. Professor Viege constantly reminded people of exam times, which is all you can ask for from an online class

Never had a conversation with Dr. Viege but the assignments and final exam were fair and representative of content given. Your TA is more important on how your grade is determined. Make sure to have a good relationship with your TA. Also, make sure to double check the night before your assignments are due that they were actually submitted.

Quizzes can be specific. A question's answer was 0.044 but I put 0.04. Even though sig figs were never mentioned, it was still implied. Other questions will have implications/ specifications, some won't, but remember those little things. Knowledge Check + final can be studied by going through each lab and their information/ procedural calculations.

Entirely dependent on your TA. My TA was Colin, and he was amazing! The labs themselves were very straightforward. Make sure you look through the rubric on post labs to make sure you answered everything they are looking for.

analysis.name: Natalia Aleksiun
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: NA is a very accomodating teacher, who clearly is passionate about the subject. No complaints, just a lot of reading. Her TA though... not it.

Dr. Aleksiun is amazing. She does a great job handling a challenging topic and is very knowledgeable. Grade based on weekly assignments, attendance, midterm, and final, all of which were not extremely challenging but still test your knowledge effectively. I loved this course and Dr. Aleksiun and would recommend it highly.

Professor Aleksiun is a great professor. Her class was full of difficult topics that she handled really well, and I found the weekly assignments to be pretty easy if you do the readings. The class is dark, but interesting, and I definitely recommend it to those who enjoy history.

analysis.name: Marinas Naibi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Her exams are poorly managed. She has no prep material for exams, which makes exam prep an overly difficult process.

Ive seen a lot of people here say this professor is a lot of work. I took AST1002 during the Summer, so it may be different for me. Prof. Naibi is fair and understanding. Shes passionate about the subject. While theres a little bit of work, its really not all that much. Just do your quizzes (easy for the most part) and go to class, youre fine.

My TA graded discussion posts like she took joy in ruining our grades. First college class I've gotten multiple D's on discussions. The projects take forever if you don't pay for a website like CourseHero. A ton of online assignments due every week and if you miss a few theres no shot you're getting an A. TOOOO much work for an 1000 level gen-ed.

The class itself is A LOT of information but its kind of interesting. The quizzes are super easy and the exams are mostly questions from the quizzes or practice exams. The projects arent too bad and the homework can sometimes take a while but its not hard at all. The lectures are sometimes hard to understand and usually contain a lot of info.

It was an interesting class and most of the assignments/quizzes are on quizlet. The information is complicated though and kind of hard to remember unless you're interested in it. The lectures can be long sometimes but not too bad. The exams aren't hard if you study, but most of the questions are from the practice exams/previous quizzes.

analysis.name: Carissa Nicholson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You don't actually interact with Professor Nicholson too much in this class, as the TAs do all the grading and the lectures are done by somebody else. However the work is pretty easy, online assignments on a weekly basis. Depending on your TA, they may grade harsher than others, but overall should still be an easy A if you put in the work.

She's almost not involved in this course its mostly you and your TA. The work was pretty simple throughout the semester besides the final project but that was also ok. What really bothered me was how long it took to release the grades for the museum essay. I turned it in oct 5 and the grades were released dec 2 which is an insane wait time.

This class is not necessarily hard, it's just annoying. A lot of random assignments but they aren't difficult, just a waste of time if you don't care about the subject. The only time I communicated with the professor was in a Q&A discussion post. She's fine, nothing bad/good. Everything seemed to be graded by the TA's, who take forever to grade.

The work is usually pretty clear and pretty managable especially if taken online, but she (or the TAs) take FOREVER to grade things. As of writing this, I submitted an essay a month and a half ago and it is not graded yet. My TA answered emails quickly but graded too harsh. They are sticklers over the dumbest things, but give good feedback.

The assignments for this class are nonsense and are graded so slowly. We did a paper over a month ago with no feedback whatsoever and now we have to start our final project and cram our proposal into a 2 minute video presentation that has many requirements. Online lectures are super boring and slow. Only redeeming quality is the light workload.

analysis.name: Jason Nowell
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 151 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Coming from someone who struggles with math, these reviews are so inaccurate. Professor Nowell is very accessible and would drop everything to tutor you. Xronos gives practice problems and review that mirrors the exams. He drops 4 quizzes and deadlines are flexible. If you're taking this class, PLEASE go to office hours - you'll see improvement!

Made Pre-calc way harder than it should be. Tries to explain topics so that you understand more than just the formula but ends up confusing students. Exams ALWAYS have something on them that was never taught in class.

The way he teaches in lecture makes everything hard. The steps that you thought you knew from middle and high school has to be thrown away to understand his style of teaching. The problems he does in lectures are way easier than what he puts on the test. Every test we took, there were mistakes he made on the exam. You really have to try hard .

Sets and Logic is an inherently difficult class but Professor Nowell did a good job explaining these difficult, conceptual topics. He gave the class a say in what kind of exams we wanted and provided extra credit throughout the course. He was very helpful when you went to him for help.

Jason, who although seems like a very kind and smart individual, does not know how to effectively teach a large body of students. His lectures and lecture notes are extremely confusing , even when they are on simple concepts. All of the work throughout the semester (homework, exams,lecture notes) contained multiple typos and mistakes.

analysis.name: Nigel Newbutt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I don't think I could say enough good things about Dr Nigel, he is an amazing professor. Very reasonable, caring, and engaging with every single student. You can tell how passionate he is about the subject and his work as it shows in every class, announcement, and conversation. If you have the chance to take his course, DO IT! I'm sad it's over.

Dr. N is the best!! You can tell he truly cares about his students, and he is passionate about his material. He does do a lot of in class group work but it's nothing difficult, just be engaged with your group. There are also not many assignments to submit throughout the semester. I would take his class again if I can.
All of the assignments are super easy and very manageable. Dr. N grades pretty quickly and always gives helpful and positive feedback. Definitely a very easy class.

Professor Newbutt is amazing! I wish more professors were like him! He shows a general and authentic interest in his students. He wants to help if you need it, offers meet-up times that are convenient, gives extra time when needed, and is hilarious! The class is laid back and you move at a comfortable pace.He makes every week interesting and fun!
I'm going to be honest. This guy is the GOAT. As long as you attend class, participate here and there, and do the assignments, you will get an A. Love that guy!

analysis.name: Steven Noll
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 217 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: There's a reason why Dr. Noll is one of the best professors in the country. I had a double block but his lectures are so engaging and fun that it didn't feel like a double block. He has a great sense of humor and genuinely tries to know the students he's teaching. Even if you don't like history I suggest you take a class with him.

Probably one of the best professors at UF. He is a true students teacher. His class is challenging and complex, but if you show up everyday, you would have to try to make a C. He gives extra credit so there is no excuse to not get a good grade.

He is funny but could occasionally make jokes at students that definitely create an uncomfortable atmosphere in the class. On writing prompts, you will be graded with no explanation while students that use AI get better scores than you. For the most part an easy class.

Great guy, very entertaining and funny lecturer. 3 papers (full book for each), 2 quizzes, midterm(?), 10 weekly readings/summaries (long, 20-40 pages). MANY extra credit opportunities. Super interesting class IMO. Noll goes on political tangents sometimes but amazing otherwise. TA feedback inconsistent with (sometimes harsh) grading.

Dr. Noll is the most unusual professor I have ever come across, but I mean that in the best way possible. He is crazy and fun when lecturing and keeps his students engaged by throwing them a stuffed manatee when they participate. I highly recommend Dr. Noll. Attendance in lectures is not mandatory, but it is in discussion sections.

analysis.name: Nicholas Serrano
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I have taken two of Nick's classes as a LA major and I have truly enjoyed both of them. He is such a passionate, knowledgeable person and if you are interested in landscape, his lectures are very relevant and interesting. He is also really quirky and super funny at times. I have always found the workload super reasonable.

(Cultures of Landscapes of the American South) Interesting class material, though a little boring at times. I stopped taking notes halfway through the semester because the material was easy enough to remember. Participate in Friday discussions with your TA and you will get an A. TA grades everything. Four papers, weekly discussion posts, no exams.

He's pretty chill and I think his class is interesting. Then again, I'm an old guy so I might have different standards. The lectures are engaging, I like the iClicker polls, and the essays aren't too difficult.

Dr. Serrano (or Nick) is an interesting guy. He is very knowledgeable and passionate about culture as it relates to architecture and American Southern heritage. His lectures are long and boring, but you can tell he cares. His writing assignments are a bit lengthy for what purpose, but his TAs are great and care a lot. I recommend this easy Quest 1.

class is really worthless if you go in wanting to actually learn something, but the professor is nice enough. its a fairly easy quest 1. that being said, there are a few too many assignments and any class with iclicker, especially iclicker forced onto you after add drop (yes really, we all got scammed into spyware) shouldnt be taken in my book.

analysis.name: Nancy Ruzycki
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. R is legitamately BAE -if you ever have the chance to take her, just do it already 3

Dr. R is a very knowledgeable teacher that truly cares if you learn the material. She offers a ton of extra credit and her exams are setup to where you get to choose from a list of questions of different point values. Her due dates are always flexible as long as you show that you actually want to learn the material. Definitely take her if you can.

Amazing teacher that really cares about her students. You should show up to class because her lectures are very clear and not boring, and there are sometimes in-class assignments that are grades, and participation quizzes. But there's (PLENTY) extra credit to fill in any points you lose. It's not the grade that matters in her class, it's learning.

She insults students for struggling with the disproportionately heavy workload and constantly acts like an overbearing parent while talking about how the younger generation isn't independent enough. I've seen her belittle people with injuries and reduce the hardest working students to literal tears. Most of your time will be spent doing busywork.

Dr. R is by far the best lecturer I have had. I'm not an engineering major and she made the information easy enough to understand. She would also bring snacks once a week for the class (usually popsicles or candy). She remembers students by name, and is very flexible with deadlines. GO TO OFFICE HOURS she is extremely helpful!!

analysis.name: Conor O'Dwyer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The weekly quizzes are tough even if you do the readings because the questions are pretty specific. There were three exams and they were kind of difficult so it was essential to do the readings and review the lecture notes. There are three books for the class and we read a chapter in all three of them each week. Attending lecture is not mandatory.

He is a great professor. Takes the time to explain topics thoroughly and is very knowledgeable in his field. He is really respectful, and his class was overall easy. Two exams that were based on lecture slides that were posted, and two in-class writing assignments that were not difficult. He is not a tough grader at all.

First half is based on textbook (basic social movement theory), second half is interesting cases. Lectures are based on the readings, not super inventive. Very nice and helpful if you go to office hours. TA grades everything so that's a toss-up.

Professor O'Dwyer was amazing. He is incredibly kind, knowledgeable, and passionate. His lectures were organized and nuanced, sparking engaging discussion. There is a lot of reading, but I took notes on only the lectures and earned 100% on every exam. I learned much more than anticipated and left the class with a solid political science foundation.

He is a very knowledgeable professor but not a good lecturer. The tests were on material that we had not learned (like maps of eastern europe) and they were not simple. Attendance is MANDATORY meaning that if you miss more than 1 day you're grade will suffer (excused or not). Wouldn't take him again, but I learned a lot - mainly from the readings.

analysis.name: Asli Odabasi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: AVOID FOS2001. It had a reputation as an easy elective, but was reformulated into something else entirely . Frustratingly complicated assignments with confusing instructions. Weekly quizzes with a very short time limit, and the exams are administered with ProctorU, an invasive proctoring program. Do NOT take as an elective, you have been warned!

This class was incredibly easy. 4 open-note multiple choice exams, a weekly open-note quiz, 3 assignments throughout the semester, and short weekly readings on Perusall that were very interesting. Nearly all of the answers to exam questions are in the notes. You will probably spend an hour or less per week on this class. Would highly recommend.

This is the easiest biological science credit class. All the exams are open note. There are 3 big assignments that are graded somewhat toughly, but still very easy. There is some reading, but they are short through Perusall, but content from them do end up on exams. Some weeks have a lot of assignments, but they don't take more than 5 minutes.

The class is all lectures with quizzes and exams, plus one 300 word assignment, like 11 assignments in all. Plus it's an easy A as long as you watch the videos. Seriously,  Dr. Odabasi is wonderful! The class content wasn't enthralling  but it's also not my major.

Very easy class. You get 4 open-note exams, and you have access to the slides during exams. There are only 3 real assignments that require a little extra effort, but at that point, that amount of effort is still less than what you'd apply for a core class. A few textbook readings that you have to annotate, but again, super easy class.

analysis.name: Naibi Marinas
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 112 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She's not good at teaching and organizing an online class. She changed what counts towards your final grade a few times, changed submission policies and due dates, and was generally very unclear about these changes. I'm sure she's very knowledgable but she's very unclear about her policies and ignores students' frustrations. Exams are pure quizlet.

Way too difficult for a 1000 level class. If you're planning on taking it to fulfill your physical science credit take a different class. Way too much work. The stuff she puts on the exams is not what she tells you is gonna be on the them and the exams are very hard. She is hard to understand during lectures and is just overall not a good teacher.

Dr. Marinas doesn't do lectures for her online course, so you are required to read the textbook which can be a lot of work for some people, but it's just time, not hard. Tests are straight from quizzes, and quizzes are straight from book, so they're SUPER easy. Having to read makes me feel like I actually learned. More courses should be like this.

Do Not Take This Class. This professor is the most unreliable professor I have ever taken. I took it on-line and she never answers questions and acts like she has no time for her students. I am so disappointed that UF actually has a professor that is allowed to teach like this.

I took this class for a gen ed and because it sounded very interesting. That is where it stopped, it was and still is the most boring class I ever took at UF. It is a really specific test and quiz that are really hard and unreasonably boring. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

analysis.name: Eamon O'Connor
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great guy! Had my quest 1 with him, and he was chill. Weekly reading assignments and 1(pretty easy) group project, and 3 essays. Lectures were pretty cool, and I found him engaging and pretty funny. Participation in class encouraged but not necessary if you're the type that worries about that.
One of the best professors I've ever had, very understanding, is easy to understand and has interesting assignments. Would forever take this class again

He's an awesome professor who makes lectures fun. I have a hard time paying attention in general, but he knows how to keep it interesting. Assignments are fun, and interpretation is quite open. It's a really good way for students to really understand and explore their interpretation of an answer, and sharing. Expect to actually enjoy class.

Loved this class! I'd take it again in a heartbeat. It really opened my eyes to the way we tell stories through digital means and even positively influenced my own work. Very caring professor that likes to have fun with his students while teaching, which makes the learning much more enjoyable. Learned about lots of new media as well!

He's great, always fun to go to his class and engages well with the students. He gives some great readings to learn from and the presentations are really funny. I enjoyed a lot of the assignments we did and had fun looking at my classmate's work in critique, was always hilarious and a fun learning environment. Love this guy

analysis.name: Karim Oweiss
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Attendance is mandatory, despite the lectures merely repeating the slide content. The heart and muscles are not talked about once, even though this is a bioelectrical systems class. I was very disappointed with the course and the professor's teaching style, and would have preferred more practical topics.
He's tough and can't teach anything to save his life
Lack of details about assignments

Professor Oweiss knows the course material with high technical competence. He can answer any question the student asks regarding the topic in a clear and concise manner. I regularly found myself encountering ideas I had heard about previously but they were said in a new and more concise way that allowed me to more deeply understand basic principles

analysis.name: David Ortiz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ortiz was, hands down, the best instructor for an online course I have ever had. Not only did he personalize each and every bit of feedback, he also responded to every email, note, or joke I had written in the margins of my papers. He gave me an amazing experience, and the personal yet professional touch he added was amazing. 10/10 Recommended

The main criticism I have for David is that he grades incredibly harsh for an intro course. Also, David's feedback when trying to make an outline for an essay was unhelpful in my experience. I relied on the other TA (Thomas Schuyler) to guide me when writing a paper. David does however manage to make sense of the complicated lectures via discussion

David is the saving grace of PHI2010. The class is hard and I couldn't understand the professor at all. In the discussion class led by David though he explains everything extremely well. (Make sure to take notes for essays.) He is a tough grader for your essays, but overall he's an amazing TA. If you take PHI2010 take advantage of his office hours.

The hardest grader I've ever had at UF. I managed to do okay, but there are only four graded essays for the semester, he never once graded above a 95, and for every single essay the class average was a C-. Definitely not impossible to pass, but if you want a good grade, don't take this class. The grading criteria is too strict and we worked hard.

David Ortiz is a graduate TA at the University of Florida. I will not lie, the only reason I understand the core concepts of this class is because of his discussions. However, he grades far too harshly. He grades us as if we're third year Philosophy majors, not Intro students. Not only that, but his comments on our papers are simply are useless.

analysis.name: Onursal  Erol
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I have known him for years now, I enjoyed my first course with him so much that have now taken 2 of his courses and participated in his internship workshop. He is the most thoughtful professor I have ever had. He is very supportive, but he also really pushes us to challenge ourselves. The readings and course content as well is just always amazing.

Dr. Erol is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. Class is graded on very few things (essay and project), and it is up to you to participate. Class is taught on a high caliber, and if you don't have a background in the region, there is a learning curve. However, I found my experience and learning to be quite fruitful.

Dr Erol is a very kind, funny, and knowledgeable professor. Grading is not harsh if you stay on top of deadlines and he gives helpful feedback. Lectures were interesting but someone with no prior knowledge about the Middle East might feel out of their depth at times without doing some extra background reading.

I love Dr. Erol, but I also think his course has a few flaws. The course I just took was graded by only 2 assignments. Luckily, he grades very kindly, but it does make you panic a bit. His lectures are sometimes a bit hard to follow, and I think a prior knowledge of Middle Eastern history would help in this course.

I dropped out of his class after drop add not because he wasn't amazing but because I thought the class was going to be more Middle East focused. It's more and environmental issues and ecology. Just wanted to put that out here in case anyone else had the wrong idea.

analysis.name: Motunrayo  Ogunrinbokun
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She picks people from the crowd and ask you to answer the question (Half the time she says your answer is not good enough). Also we learn brand new concepts and then immediately take a quiz, cold turkey.

I liked her during classes, but she is really bad at responding to emails and working with athletes. I was in track and swim season while taking her class, and she had a lot of assignments that could not be made up. This was frustrating because I would miss class for meets, and it would hurt my grade. She also did not show up to meetings.
Run. Doesn't show up to her own classes, no answers to email, and bizarre feedback on assignments

Easy A, take if needed.  Great person BUT: Moved class online over half the semester, not Canvas savvy (accidentally adds assignments we don't have to do, etc.), little feedback, vague instructions, poor grading turnaround, doesn't respond to emails.  Syllabus outdated with incorrect grading scale and formatted for a full term course.

It's an in-person class, but she started having trouble showing up; we had 3 weeks of class in person and 3 weeks online. She's an easy grader but does not leave comments or suggestions for improvement. She is also hard to reach: she selectively responds to emails and cancels class about once a week for various reasons. Easy A tho.

analysis.name: Monikaa Oli
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The lab is one credit but its more of a part time job. Get ready for quizzes once a week based on two modules with material that won't be useful to study from because the TA makes the quizzes up. Multiple projects throughout the semester and a final project each worth 100 points. Most unorganized class I have ever taken and I'm a senior.

Dr. Oli tends to be very disorganised. Course content was a mess; the Canvas pages were very hard to navigate. Emails would occasionally get lost for days or weeks, and communication with Dr. Oli and the TAs was nigh impossible. Requirements and expectations were constantly shifting, making it very difficult to keep track of what needed to be done.

Passivea ggressive to students and her faculty don't like her. Interactions may feel more critical than constructive, which makes it hard for students who value supportive, solution-oriented mentorship... would not get on her bad side.

IDS2935 MICROBES WITHOUT BORDERS (no course option for that). Interesting and fairly fun for a quest class but a lot of assignments. 1 discussion, 1-2 activities, 1 quiz, and 1 assessment every week. Plus 3-4 big PowerPoint presentations. Prof was somewhat responsive but the syllabus is confusing and due dates change often. No required lectures!

I had Sade Thomas as my TA, and this was by far the most disorganized course I have ever taken. The expectations are unclear, everyone is always confused about what we're even doing in the lab, and when you ask questions for clarity they just run you in circles. If you want a decent grade in a 1 credit lab steer clear of this TA.

analysis.name: Robert Parker
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a really nice guy but he speaks reallllly softly so you have to sit pretty close to the front of the room to hear even with his mic. He says you need the textbook on the first day but I didn't get it and ended up with an A in the class. Just do the practice test problems he gives you and you'll be fine.

His class only requires 3 exams (in class) and 5 quizzes that are online. He speaks very quietly so I highly suggest you sit closer to the front. He teaches strickly from a workbook so as long as you attend classes you will be fine in terms of learning the material and not falling behind.

Save yourself, if you dont practice a religion PICK ONE UP YOU WILL NEED IT. Genuinely one of the most unhelpful redundant professors ever. Bad office hours, he will always tell you the same thing "figure it out yourself". Class might as well be online as there is nothing done in the classroom except him giving answers to the weekly handouts.

Majority of learning was through 2 textbooks that covered the same material in different ways. Neither book had great example problems which made understanding concept difficult. Provided lecture videos of problems were very basic level problems which did not help with homeworks or exams. Generally, I had to rely on google for everything.

Have not taken the final yet but honestly I like him. He is clear with his expectations and is always willing to answer questions. He is not a super peppy professor but you can tell he is passionate about biostats and genuinely wants students to learn. Project was graded kinda toughly but overall not too bad of a class.

analysis.name: Sophia Pan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Such a great professor. She is definitely super knowledgeable and interesting in what she talks about. Tons of personal, human responses on papers that are useful towards future assignments. Awesome film choices and super chill movie nights. Don't let the 6000 words turn you off, it is spread across multiple reviews and papers. TAKE THIS CLASS!

One of my favorite classes at UF I've taken! I had some medical issues this semester and Professor Pan was so kind and more than willing to not only work with me, but help me! I HIGHLY recommend signing up for her new course in the fall! Her feedback on assignments is so helpful and she really makes the class interactive and fun.

LIT2000: Super easy, Instructor Pan keeps you engaged for the most part. Class was based on a few small writing assignments. The biggest writing assignment was only 1200 words which is absolutely nothing, and she gives a rubric before hand so it is a really easy class.

i am not really a movie person, however, this class became my favorite class throughout the semester because i learned so much. instructor pan gives great feedback and is very enthusiastic about each movie and teaching which makes the class very fun and interesting. she is very caring and wants you to succeed

Honestly, this was my favorite class. Professor Pan was the nicest and most caring professor I have ever met. Her class is so fun and actually enjoyable to participate in. Her movie selection was also amazing. It didn't even feel like 6,000 words, the workload was very easy and manageable in the way she formatted it. We love prof Pan!!

analysis.name: Panagiotis Saranteas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Panagiotis is an extremely thoughtful professor. He is always motivating students to do their best in class. As this was my first time taking a philosophy course, he gave me all the support I needed to excel, and I loved talking with him after class about moral philosophy and productivity. Definitely take him!

Awesome guy, had him in Fall 2024, but no RMP page was made yet. He really cares about all of his students, and is really good at engaging them. He grades papers to a pretty rigid rubric, but if you show up to his office hours he'll grade them infront of you and let you change your paper to resubmit. I've never seen him give out a 100 (A+ was 98%).
Awesome guy. He really wants his students to pass and will help you however possible. He was a TA in this course and helped a lot with assignments and work..
He was very chill. Sometimes will start talking about random stuff, but he definitely cares and wants you to get a good grade.

analysis.name: Daniel O'Neill
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 96 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The GOAT!!! O'Neill is one of the best professors at UF. You will def need to work for your A (do ALL the readings, take good lecture notes, and use your office hours!), but O'Neill's iconic lectures and clear passion for political theory will also def inspire the same in you. Material is difficult, but not a harsh grader. Remember - details!

Professor O'Neill was an extremely animated and passionate professor who I highly recommend any Poli Sci freshman take Political Theory with. My TA was really informative (although very political) and grading is fair. Sometimes he can go on tangents which are ultimately more confusing than helpful but he was easy to talk to during office hours.

Dr. O'Neill is an amazing lecturer and I highly recommend you take him for an intro level class. His lectures are extremely engaging and although attendance is not mandatory, I recommend going. I don't think its necessary to purchase the textbook to succeed as his lectures pretty much cover all the material you need to know for his exams.

Prof O'neill is such an amazing professor. He clearly loves and understands the topics presented which makes the lectures super engaging. Grades are weekly discussion attendance,  3 exams, and weekly paragraph reading responses. I highly recommend Billsborough as a TA!

He is so smart and loves what he teaches. As long as you attend class, take notes, and study, you'll do well in the class. Three written exams, super straight-forward and easy to ace. Timmy Stolz is the best TA and is always willing to help answer any questions.

analysis.name: Pete  Punthasee
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 110 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: don't expect him to be involved in helping you succeed in this class outside lecture. told us to go to TAs not him, refused to do review because he claimed it wasn't his job, and sent us an email saying to learn how to "let it go" when it comes to our grades. sorry i wanna succeed and actually understand the material? trust me, don't take him!!!

To be honest, Pete was one of the worst professors I've ever had. I am not pre-med and I am not trained to memorize things, and he always said "don't memorize." Went from a 98 average to below a 70 after synthesis. Totally demoralizing. He loves watching his students struggle. Take anyone else.

If you want a professor who doesn't act like you're a burden to him and actually tries and helps you in his class don't take this class. If you have any other commitments, find another professor. Pete makes it seem like his class is the only class that matters. The exams are the only thing that is graded so if you do bad on an exam, good luck.
I had an A up until the final exam. 5 exams worth your entire grade. Exams 4 and the final are extremely tough. Not a fair professor.

If you have any time commitments outside the classroom (jobs, extracurriculars, familial responsibilities, etc.), Pete's expectations are nearly impossible. TAs have shared that Pete does much less for his students now than in the past; they also blatantly tell you to watch Pete's YT videos during review sessions. Think about ur priorities!!!

analysis.name: Youngmin Park
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: 1 month into class and bros a wreck. cant teach the class well, couldnt write a multiple choice quiz correctly, assigned straightforward homework -- and then lost it bc students couldnt answer random abstract math questions on the spot for an 'audit' that was rlly an in person oral exam. now hes cancelling the syllabus?? steer clear.

Caring professor from day one, dedicated to student success. Seven exams may seem like a lot, but each covers manageable material. Always available on Discord and never declined in-person meetings. Extra credit offers low-pressure coding practice. The best professor I have had at UF, highly recommend you take the class if you have the chance.

This guy is an absolute sweetheart. He really wants each and every one of his students to succeed. Yes, the course is test heavy but because tests are frequently there's not much material between each test so it's not as rigorous as you think. He's always available to ask for help through Discord. 10 out of 10 professor.

I'd highly recommend taking any course with this professor. The exams were very representative of the content covered in class. He also provided ample extra credit opportunities and exam drops. He genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed.

Dr.Park is by far one of the best teachers i have had! Go to class, he is super nice and lectures well (most times class gets out early). His exams are very representative of what is learned in class and he listens to his students!

analysis.name: Peter Rudnytsky
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 81 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Do not make the mistake I did: If you are not an English major, DO NOT take this course. I am a 4.0 student and received a C+ in this class. It probably didn't help that I was taking 17 credit hours. Despite that, I did everything required and more. What's worse is I took the class and only needed Eng credits, not the specific course.  It ruined me

I don't know if I've ever had a professor that is so invested and passionate about the coursework and their students. He's a tough grader, but also extremely reasonable and easy to work with. The negative ratings on here are likely from people who didn't score well on the exams, which are admittedly very difficult but also very doable.

Wouldve loved shakespeare w a dif prof.Man rambles 4ever w NO prepared notes or anything.Just comes in&talks for literally the entire 3 hrs, asks for ?'s but deviates &takes 30 mins to sort-of answer them.Grades harsh& doesnt tell u what he expects in essays on test, then tells you you havent done it the right way. Worked WAY hard &ended up with B-

It's definitely possible to pass his class and even get an A or B. But he's very boring, talks forever, and only cares about his opinion even though he wants the class to be a discussion. He'll interrupt you and isn't very helpful when you ask him questions. He's also a harsh grader. Only good thing was the tests were easy--if you like essay tests.

If you're into critically analyzing texts through his twisted psychoanalytic framework -- which he forces you to use -- then this is your guy. It's absolutely excruciating watching him disagree with anyone, he will belittle you in front of the whole class if he feels like it. Half of the class failed the midterm/papers and the books were terrible

analysis.name: Katherine Quinone8
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: You don't learn a lot in the class, but are still expected to take an exam on material that was "taught". The labs were fine, but the lab reports were the worst. You get graded harshly on lab reports for every little thing. You are not always given the necessary data in a timely manner. ALWAYS emails you back about questions after the due date.

I was surprised to see her bad ratings. I had her for WW Microbio and she was great. You had to come to class to take the quizzes, which are 40% of your final grade, but they're super easy as long as you show up. Don't slack off too much though, as you need a 94% to make an A. You can use class resources like notes and slides on all the assessments

New to teaching, it really shows. Going to lecture is pointless. The meat of the class is lab reports, which take 8+ hours per week to complete. She made the 1st exam too long, had to trash it. Re-graded lab reports because TAs didn't "grade to her standards." Don't punish us for following instructions by the TAs. Worst prof at UF.
Very responsive and generally very helpful!

analysis.name: Quincy Gibson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Gibson is a wonderful professor, and I recommend taking her.  There are 4 tests and no final cumulative other things to Inc Grade. She makes every class interactive. I'd recommend record the lecture and transcribe it later.The exams are multiple choice and free response but the majority of the grade is from multiple choice.

does not present her material in a way that students can understand. She is inconsistent on her tests. You must attend class and do all assignments if you want to even pass her class. Her tests are all conceptual and not one multiple choice is presented. Do not take this teacher unless you intend on making a C or lower.
Loved her, lectures were very easy to understand, quizzes were easy as long as you attended lectures. She was always quick to answer any questions I had.

analysis.name: Qingming Huang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He has one TA who was super sweet and gave nice feedback and an A on a decent paper, the other TA was awful and super condescending when grading papers and gave everybody a B- in an intro-level class. The material was over complicated and too condensed. Somewhat nice guy but then wouldn't round my grade literally .001 up for me to get an A.

A genius, down to earth & genuinely cares. Mess up a submission? He'll email u to let u send it to him, no penalty. Had a life crisis? He'll check up on you on a personal level & give extensions. Yes there's a lot of readings and some essays but mostly watch the lectures & use the slides as notes. Skim readings for quotes to use. Communicate w him.

Took the class online during summer b. Very few assignments with a lot of lecture videos. It was hard to understand him but attend office hours and its better. TA grades everything, one was definetily chiller than the other one. Overall, actually watch the lecture videos and take good notes and put time in on your own and the class is not too hard.

I can't understand anything he is saying because of his accent. This isn't meant to be racist at all; I am very against that. However, it would be nice to be able to understand what my professor is teaching, and I couldn't comprehend his explanations in any of the lectures. His accent is HEAVY. IK it's not his fault, but it did interfere w learning

Good intentions as a person but not a great professor. He gave extra credit and was sometimes understanding, but sometimes wasn't. His accent was very heavy, and especially in an online class with no transcripts, it was virtually impossible to understand him. The course was intro level and he made it much harder/ complicated that it needed to be.

analysis.name: Denise Quinlan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Denise was an amazing discussion leader for POS2041. She was open to students of all ideologies and opened the floor for some amazing conversations. She made it clear she was always there to help us do well and she even kept up with our lives, asking how things were going and sending support during tough times. If you have the choice, take her!

She is a great TA and would make an amazing professor! She is understanding and cares about her students. She doesn't grade harshly and wants you to be able to earn an A and succeed in the course. Her lectures are engaging and she makes discussions fun. I highly recommend!
Class was easy and the prof was more than fair on grading.

analysis.name: Liangfei Qiu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Liangfei is a good guy who cares about his students, and his class is pretty straightforward and east if you put in any effort. It may be difficult to work through his accent, but the slides are well put together enough to learn on your own.

I took ISM6423 Data Analysis for Decision Support. The man (I hesitate referring to Liangfei as a mortal because he) responds to emails lightning quick and can talk without faltering for 2 hours straight with no break and no water. Respect.
Amazing professor! His slides are very useful. He knows his subject very well.

analysis.name: Amanda Phalin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 111 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You miss one detail and you are done. She packs on tons of assignments with loads of criteria to follow to a T. As a full-time online student (w/ a full time job), I don't think she understands that just maneuvering around all her loads of crap is hard enough. She treats you like a slacker if you can't keep up with it all and it feels demeaning.

Professor Phalin teaches a completely useless course. The exams are almost entirely (80%) about memorizing obscure facts about a specific country. On top of that, she berates you with 4 assignments per week that are difficult to score well on. Overall, an out of touch professor. No one cares what the GDP growth rate is in 2020 for Canada...

Since the first day of class she's had an unsettling "Not My Problem" attitude towards her students. She's one of those people that's very 'rules-based' and unaccommodating. This class is a perfect example of UF trying to make pointless classes unnecessarily difficult. Her lectures are not worth your time, Smokin' Notes are the way to go.

Professor Phalin is a great lecturer and makes class interesting despite content sometimes being boring. Definitely utilize the cheat sheet she allows you to have on the exam. I used smokin notes to help me figure out the most important information to put on it and it was a life saver!

This class was pretty easy, I didn't use Smokin' Notes, just went to all the lectures and participated. You get a full page of notes, so memorization wasn't an issue. She also gives you a template for this sheet which is really helpful and makes sure you don't miss anything you should have on your cheat sheet.

analysis.name: Suzanne Robbins-McDonald
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Suzanne is one of the better poli sci professors within the department. Her lectures are usually good, just might have a hard time always wanting to go as this class every semester is bright and early at 9:35. You might have to skip a few depending on your habits. She does a great job explaining the material and what is important for the test.

She is one of the best professors I have ever had, her class is well organized and she is VERY knowledgeable on the subject. She makes a boring topic interesting and engaging. Only issues are that there are a lot of readings, and there is also a semester long project with one partner (which is a LOT of work) so make sure you have a good partner.

Totally recommend taking Dr. Robbins for AFG. The class is mostly graded on exams, and I skimmed through the reading and studied with the online platform and got A's on all three of them. The essays are not difficult and can be done in like a day. Discussion was not hard. Just skimming the reading and slight participation should get you an A.

3 papers + 3 exams. Lectures weren't super information dense making them a little boring. I just did all the Inquizitive practice tests the night before each exam and that will teach you EVERYTHING you need as long as you do each module to 100%. Took about 2 hours to study per exam, and I did very well on all of them. Extra credit on each exam.

Very easy to talk to and isn't a boring lecturer. Everything she said in lecture was relevant to exams, but you're forced to attend anyway because of iClicker. Reading the textbook is key to success on exams, but that can be done with the 2 days prior. Went to her office hours for tips on how to study, she was super helpful (I got my B+ to an A)

analysis.name: Scott Taylor
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He was great. Not the best lecturer, but he was CLEAR about what he wanted us to know! I studied the material really hard, and did awesome because the test material actually matched what he taught us. This is how all classes should be taught, not profs trying to trick us. He even made us a super helpful study guide. Super responsive too.

Take this professor. Exams are open note (you can use your iPad during the exams for notes). Questions are kind of hard, but it's easy with your notes. Make sure you watch the lectures and take good notes. One exam is dropped, including the final if that's your lowest. There are also a few quizzes that are super easy that can boost your grade some.

Mr. Taylor is a boring lecturer, but gives enough material to do decent on his exams. He also does extra credit questions on his exams, so you do better than you think. All you have to do is go over the slides several times and answer his practice questions. The combined lab is easy.

3 exams, 1 final - lowest exam dropped. Exams are tough, but open note - not unreasonably hard and it is easy enough to get an A if you watch the lectures. No need to read the textbook. No extra credit.

Would take with him over Ahlgren since tests are only 45% of grade with Taylor, and Taylor does the class online. Would recommend!

Tests were very fair and open note. Short lectures every week that were very aligned with the test that were another professor's. Textbook is absolute overkill. Drops lowest 2 lectures and chapter quizzes. Overall class was not too bad. It doesn't take too much time. I never studied much since the tests were open note.

analysis.name: Sergei Shabanov
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 73 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amazing teacher; super high standards and makes you feel stupid by being so much smarter than everyone, but you will have earth-shattering revelations nearly every day. His class will be the hardest you are taking at the time, period, but also the most worth it.

Goes into great depth explaining the math, but can be hard to follow if you don't have a strong foundation. Grades are dependent only on test scores, but extra work is kind of mandatory unless you can absorb everything in the quick lectures. Additional reading is free through canvas and the reading exercises are very similar to the tests.

One of the most passionate and intelligent professors you will have. If you want to know the "why" behind the "what" in calculus III, I HIGHLY recommend taking this course. Shabanov is so kind and wants to see all of his students succeed. Entire grade is based on exams, but if you do all of the optional homework practice, you won't have any issues!

If given the opportunity to take this class, I'd definitely recommend it. Although the course is exceptionally difficult in many aspects, I would ascertain that this class helps develop one's mathematical intuition and maturity to a very high degree. Generally, the questions on exams (which constitute your entire grade) were similar to those in HW.

Phenomenal professor that's clearly very knowledgeable. Lectures were easy to follow and extremely thorough; he establishes a quasi-proof of every concept. He also has online recordings of lectures that are extremely good for catching up. Your entire grade is tests but he offers standard questions and a lot of extra credit. Would highly recommend!

analysis.name: Tamer Kahveci
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Kahveci seems like a nice professor, but I wouldn't take this course. It's "chill", because there's no homework assignments. Just 4/5 quizzes, and he expects you to comprehend the material without any practice. No practice problems (homework) or textbooks to reinforce the material. The TA was very slow with grading, often taking weeks.

Prepare to have one of the worst courses that can be offered at the University of Florida. An outdated course with a professor who is behind the times and doesn't even keep up with the semester schedule. The only professor I have ever had to teach during the Thanksgiving week break. Students failed this course. Non-Computational Biology!

He's an excellent lecturer and you'll learn a great deal. I wouldn't consider the material outdated as it focuses on foundational algorithms and problems that anyone interested in bioinformatics should understand. I would have enjoyed more coverage of biological concepts and additional algorithms, but the lectures we had were sufficiently in-depth.
The worst professor I've seen in my entire life.

honestly, this prof just gets high points because the class is so easy.... it's easier than middle school.  I would have liked to feel like I accomplished or learned something but I just didn't.  if you want to an easy course go for it but if you want to learn something choose something else.

analysis.name: Suzanne Utley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Bad. Barely interacted with the class, no actual teaching performed. Read the weekly readings, read the vague modules full of typos, and get punished on vague quizzes because the "prof" refuses to actually teach. Quizzes poorly worded, based on single-sentence minutiae from textbooks. Quality papers given 10% off seemingly arbitrarily. Disgraceful.

The modules do not match the quizzes and the images that are on the quizzes could be numerous things w/out knowing context. Don't let the extra credit fool you -not worth the effort as it was also graded harshly. Sherry took points off for things she said were not in my papers that were in fact IN MY PAPER which tells me she blindly graded my work.

The modules and pictures provided are the only references available for the class. The quizzes are supposed to be based on the modules which is continually incorrect. There are multiple grammatical errors in every single module as well as spelling. Answers to quiz questions are unclear and extremely wordy for the time provided to take the quizzes.

She is by far the worst professor ever. Granted you have to do more work as the class is online, but she did absolutely nothing. She never lectured or taught in anyway. She never engaged with students or added to class discussions. She never replied to emails. Her notes are very basic and never helpful. Quizzes and exams were impossible to pass.

The questions for these quizes are very cryptic and the pictures are very difficult  to see and offer very little context for the question. As a full time parent, student, and employee, I was given very little grace and she has little to no understanding of the challenges we face in day-to-day life. Students with 4.0 GPA's have failed this course.

analysis.name: Timothy Drachlis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I think I passed his class with a good grade, thanks to some extra credit assignments. He is an extremely tough grader and takes off tons of points for single errors. His grading is VERY nebulous, although he does give back revised papers. I would stay away from him if you want to be sure you'll get a good grade.
