Very hard class, decent professor. The work amount is intense, I'm part-time and still was swamped. Pro tip: do the smallest stories possible, don't pick broad topics, a paragraph in journalism can be a sentence or two, get the kindle AP stylebook, and communicate with him a lot. If you can find a buddy, even better for proofreading. you got this

A is possible, but you'll have to bend over backwards and regress in your mental health. Emailing the professor helps sometimes, so use that. Proofread multiple times for AP style. But your stories will rarely be good enough for him no matter the quality and effort so there is that. Don't write more than 600 words - more words = more mistakes.

DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE!!!!! UF should be ashamed of themselves for allowing this to be a mandatory requirement for non-journalist majors, especially having this guy be the only option. You will not earn higher than a C and you will be miserable the entire semester. Throws around that “fact error” 50/100 point penalty around like confetti. Awful.

By far the worst class I have ever taken. I have never felt more discouraged. It's not even about being a good or bad writer for this guy. Nobody is good enough. I wish that I would've listened to the reviews instead of having the “should be fine” mentality with this prof. This is your warning- do not and I mean DO NOT take this course with him.

analysis.name: Susan Underkoffler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: It is very clear that she loves what she does. Makes the material fun and I learned a huge amount.

First she gave us assignments on spring break. Guess after complaints she gave us the next week off. Then she moved up the final project date to sooner a week before it was due. Also said that this was due to grades being due on the 26th but had the final exam due on the 28th? Absolutely will not take her again.

Awesome class! She was one of the best professors I ever had, knows this field, and I learned so much in this course! She really cares about students and wants them to do well. Gives lots of time to finish exams and discussion questions and gives extra credit for participation. Not bad to look at either! Too bad she only teaches online.

analysis.name: Anastasia Ulanowicz
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She's a great professor who facilitates conversation and lectures well. However, she is a very tough grader and will make you work for an A or B. She's incredibly nice and will help you in office hours. She also offers some extra credit along the way to help you out, although she also gives quite a few pop quizzes and assignments.

Professor Ulanowicz is one of my two favorite professors at UF (The other being Carolyn Kelley)! Her classes are informative (I have been in several) and she makes your writing better, while still maintaining humanity, unlike other professors that I have encountered. She cares about your education and is willing to help you.

Professor Ulanowicz is awesome. She put a lot of background information about the text into the lectures and really encouraged conversations, especially with different perspectives. There could probably do to be a few more assignments but overall super enjoyable class and obviously very smart, engaged professor

Professor Ulanowicz is AMAZING! Take her class if you're genuinely passionate about the subject, and I promise it will be one of the most rewarding educational experiences you can have. Her lectures are information-heavy, and you'll fall behind quickly if you miss class, but she is a phenomenal lecturer. Also a very quick and very fair grader!

One novel per week. With audio books, it wasn't hard. If you can do that, then absolutely take this class. There is nothing about her teaching style that makes anything harder than it should be. There were two 3pg papers and one 8-10pg. Keep up with the reading, don't wait until the last minute to do the papers, and you'll do well and enjoy class.

analysis.name: Larry Ukeiley
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He sucks. People say he's nice but can snap back at you if you ask a question he doesn't like. Makes you do useless derivations that will NEVER appear at a work place. He needs to make this class more practical - final exam covers too much material. It seems that he thinks aerodynamics is the only course his students are taking.

He is huge on doing long meticulous derivations that no one is paying attention to in class and rarely works out actual problems.  This class is made to be difficult, on exams be prepared to apply complicated formulas that you haven't worked out a problem with.  If you have applied a formula before, he likes to ask you to derive it from scratch.

This guy is horrible. All he does is copy the derivations from the book (except he makes tons of mistakes). Because of this, going to class is completely useless; however, it's technically required because he gives unannounced quizzes. Unfortunately you have to take his class if you're an aero student. Just be warned, and be prepared.

This is for EAS4810C. This class is atrocious. Prepare to spend 30+ hours on each lab just to get in the 70-85 range. I'm convinced that Dr. Ukeiley instructs the TAs to grade as hard as possible because there's really no other explanation. Ukeiley's structure for this class will wear down your mental health, so be ready.

Takes getting used to
1st half lots concpts Second half more application
Lots of time to do HW, I would procrastinate, do NOT recomend

Felt unprepared for exams, easier than expected
Past exams useful
introductory true/false to warm you up
short answer to get you going
long question at the end
long Q like HW, easy to predict with HW and past exams

analysis.name: Ulrich Stingl
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: As long as you watch the lectures, you will do fine on the quizzes. Make sure you understand the quiz questions because the exams are very similar to them. Overall, he is very fair and will clearly tell you what you need to know for the tests.

Awesome professor! Study ahead of time, do study guides, watch videos and you will do fine. I learned so much from this class. I would definitely take him again. You will see quiz questions again on the exams.
Dr. Stingl is one of the best professor! He respects his students and gives a lot of help when needed. It is an easy A class as long as you study for it!

Very easy class but still informative! Straight-forward, no BS. Watch the lectures and study a little and you'll be fine. Modules are very short and exams don't cover much material at all. Unless you don't try at all, there's no reason you won't do well in this class. Class could probably be made a little harder but I'm definitely not complaining

Professor Stingl offers fair grading, minimal homework, and well-prepared quizzes for four exams and an optional final. Balanced coursework, respected teaching, and adeptness with online tools define his approach.

analysis.name: Paola Uparela
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: took Quest 1 Comida & Conflicto and even though the class itself is not hard there is a lot of work involved. about 2 quizzes a week about articles that can be more than 10 pgs long and videos that you have to submit on friday's about a particular topic. I honestly thought it was a lot for a quest, but she doesn't have exams so that's good

I took SPN3930 and SPW3030 with Paola and they were my favorite classes I've taken at UF. One of the most knowledgeable/interesting professors I've had. Classes are reading heavy, but she is always excited to help during office hours. Essays have loose prompts, and she encourages thinking creatively & giving our interpretations of the topics/texts.

Interesting lectures but she barely provides a space for students to share their knowledge on the topic. So keep your knowledge to yourself, she knows more than everyone else. The good thing is that you do not need to be creative or original in this class, as long as you write the final paper that she wants you to write, you will get an A.

Fantastic professor. There's a lot of reading in this class, but that's to be expected, it is a literature class. She was always very available outside of class, and really wants her students to be successful. Great feedback on all assignments.

analysis.name: Uttam Gaulee
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He was certainly a calm haven when I was going through a storm of chaos. Accommodated me and provided me some really useful resources. I liked his anecdotes and unique perspectives

He frequently checked with each individual student to make sure we were on track for our final project. He knew it was tough but he was intentional; but he did have empathy. I would have dropped this class in the middle without the support. He kinda sensed that I was too anxious about my project and provided examples and tips to be successful.

Gaulee is an exceptional teacher except that I hated  the  way he put us through a tough group project. You had to identify and call university leaders and make reports. Even though it eventually turned out pretty well, working in the group was a pain

He used piazza for course website, which was super easy! He brings uncommonly wide range of international and interdisciplinary perspectives, which may easily confuse you to death, specially when you don't see the connection. Here's your bet: Keep calm and tell him you're confused. He will explain it for you. Super crazy trill professor :)
I scheduled an one-one-meeting with him and that made a whole lot of difference. He was a great listener and he addressed my needs.

analysis.name: Alper Ungor
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 103 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I liked the lectures. The topics are interesting and the professor is enthusiastic about the material. He encourages participation and often asks leading questions to help students feel engaged. You should attend this class, and definitely do the homework. The tests are a bit of a time crunch and you will need to have had the practice.

He spent a ton of time going over the easy concepts and flew through the hard stuff. His lectures are straight from the textbook (examples are even the same) and the discussions do not help at all. I would avoid taking this class with him.

Great teacher, hard exams. he's one of the most professional lecturers I've had, he comes to class prepared. The homework isn't for a grade but you wont pass unless you do it well and understand the concepts.

I heard bad rumors about him prior to taking the course, but let me tell you he is the best professor you could have for this course. The other professors make the class more difficult than it needs to be (it's already difficult enough) and are much more strict on grading. Yes, the material is difficult but he tries to make it understandable

Awesome and extremely professional teacher. His work ethic and class definitely changed the way I view academics; I used to think all that mattered in school was getting an A's but he helped show me value of the material and that has resulted in me having increased interest and dedication to all of future classes and academic endeavors.

analysis.name: Victoria Pagan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Pagan is the absolute best. I've taken tons of classes with her, and she does a great job keeping people engaged. Her topics are always really interesting, too -- she doesn't teach boring classes like "Roman History" or "Latin Literature." She's taught classes on sports in Ancient Greece, conspiracy theory in classics, and Gardening! How fun!

Dr Pagan will always do her best to make you enthusiastic about anything she's teaching, but is honest with you about what she thinks and is hilarious. She's kind and super understanding about any issues you're having, especially if she can see you're willing to put in effort. Always highly recommend her class -- if she's teaching it, take it.
Dr. Pagan is literally so nice, I love her. She tells the funniest stories and she's very down to earth, but she was literally UF's teacher of the year last year, so she knows her stuff.

dr. pagan is the sweetest. gardens to read and visit is a great quest 1. few assignments and she's an easy grader. she accepts late work ("docks points for it" but i've never gotten anything but an A). she brought us cupcakes for her birthday. she genuinely cares about students and makes an effort to talk to everyone individually. i adore her!!!
This was a super super easy Latin class (I took it back in 2023, forgot to rate her) but she was amazing and so funny. She's also super understanding.

analysis.name: Victor Del Hierro
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very easy (everyone gets an A even if you don't do all the work) and personable. He can be super strict but just gives off good vibes and energy. Class is just talking about books he likes. Some stopped going after a while but I found his classes useful he just has attitude but no aptitude

Dr. Hero is an amazing professor! He's the best ever in history of Florida men! I loved going to his class and hearing the music!! Dr. Hero is best DJ since Tiesto! What a wonderful person. I went to every class just to listen to the music. Greatest of all time professor and a real A+ human. He even offered to buy me a book he's great professor Dr.

Professor del Hierro is a master at disappearing acts—especially when it comes to emails. Need clarification on an assignment? Good luck! By the time he replies (if he ever does), the semester will be over. Communication is clearly not his superpower, so don't expect much unless you have a carrier pigeon handy.

He is very kind and understanding. I enjoyed the project-based nature of the class and actually ended up gaining super useful skills and connections, such as a connection to the Director of Medical Humanities at UF COM from a podcast project we were assigned. I love how we were able to tailor the class to our own interests/aspirations in this way.
Very judgmental. Gives the impression he didn't do the readings for his own class...

analysis.name: Vincent Bindschaedler
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This review is for CAI4104-ML Engineering. Very knowledgeable professor, asks great questions during lectures and clearly understands the material well. Class had 5 HWs, some were easy and some had to spend 12+ hours on. Frustrating since feedback on the last 3 came near finals week. Intense exams, take notes during lectures and use those to study.

This is for CAI4104 MLE. Great class, but for me it was as much work and as hard as OS. Exams are intense on memorization. Lectures are high quality and you will learn a lot. The homework teaches you well but they are HARD. Caveat, didn't know Python so I lost time debugging silly mistakes. If you want a huge jumpstart into ML, take this course.

Applied ML. Excellent professor, definitely one of the best I've had at UF; probably my favorite class I've taken so far. If you're interested in machine learning at all, definitely take it with him. He's a natural at teaching/lecturing and conveying concepts clearly. Exams were just the right difficulty. Learned a lot and all of it was practical.

Dr. Bindschaedler does a very good job at teaching applied ML without making it a ton of work. He covers higher level concepts on a lower level for students and doesn't go into any complex math. For the course description, "Applied" ML, he does a great job since it teaches mostly how to use and apply SK-learn and Tensorflow. Overall great course.

He was knowledgeable, helpful, and explained the topics well. He went over numerous practice problems and exercises, and really did his best to help students learn. Everything about this class was reasonable. The tests were tough but the projects were realistic.

analysis.name: Denis Valle
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
HE IS NOT RECOMMENDED AT ALL FOR EDUCATION!
 AVOID HIM EVEN IF IT"S YOU'RE LAST CLASS IN THE DEGREE.

This class is tough. Attack the work early as you're really at the mercy of message boards for help with codes. He is not understanding if you need help,No leniency so don't even ask. Set a few hours aside MWF for concept quizzes, data quizzes, and actual quiz time, and take the class with someone you can call with Qs. Quizzes are tough but openbk.
ALS5932 is a great class. Dr. Valle is able to present complex ideas in a simple and straight-forward way. Look forward to more of his courses.
Stats class had good content. Difficult to understand his accent and also not very understanding of others problems.

This class was difficult to keep up. As a graduate student you already have so much work to do and this class expects you to have a pop-quiz at 8.30am every week (open book luckily), you have to submit discussion questions on sunday night and it takes the whole week to work through a homework set due on friday.

analysis.name: Thomas Vazquez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Vazquez is great for Theatre Appreciation. I took the class online, and the work was very light. You could easily use ChatGPT for the whole course and get a 95+. Only reason not to get an A is if you forget to do the work, and the work is very easy to do. Quizzes are also online on canvas and there's no final exam, making them open note!

I took this class for my gen ed credit. The class was super easy and pretty interesting. Most of the grading is done by TAs and the quizzes are a little specific at times. Overall pretty easy course. The professor ended up dropping the lowest quiz and discussion post at the end of the semester. The final was a super easy project.

Professor Vasquez was incredibly kind and supportive. As an online student, I appreciated how easy he was to contact. Even if I was getting some points taken off, he made it clear what he wanted to see improvement on. The course was engaging, not overwhelming. Highly recommend this class!
This class is very difficult. Assigned readings are long quizzes are obscure and homework assignments are vague are made harder than necessary.

Took this class over Summer B and was honestly pretty simple and interesting. I'm not a theatre major but the different plays were very interesting and made the assignments enjoyable and easy to get through. Grading was very clear and TA's would respond and grade fairly quickly. Def recommend if you need a humanities/diversity credit or for fun.

analysis.name: Corbin Verschaeve
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: i think he is a very tough grader when it comes to the papers but he is very easy to reach if you want better critcs because he will be very nic picking but not explain it in the notes. If you pace yourself in this class you will be fine. Also, you can always ask for resubmitting major papers until the end of the semester.

He grades every paper like it's a doctoral-level thesis. He marked me down because I used words that were linguistically and grammatically correct, but different from the words he would have used. He does allow resubmissions if you make corrections based on his feedback, but be prepared for multiple rounds of corrections. Avoid him if possible.

I would disregard the other ratings. You definitely have to put in work in his course to get an A, but it is not anything crazy. I dedicated a reasonable amount of time a week to this course and ended up getting a 99. Communicate with him consistently throughout the semester because he is very responsive and provides stellar feedback.

He seemed like a nice person but he's such an annoying grader. Took points off for literally anything. For a gen-ed or "freshman-level" class this was definitely one of the hardest and time consuming courses I've taken and his feedback was useless. I definitely had to put in A LOT of hard work to get an A. Take this course in-person and AVOID HIM.

Graded me 0s on everything, would not reply to any emails on why. Made racial remarks on my ability to speak English, only graded my work poorly with no rzn. Did not reply to any emails, told me my work was terrible. 
gave me no feedback, I compared my work to others and it was day and night.

Switched to an online class where I got graded all As.

analysis.name: Yuanxin Wang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The sweetest professor you will ever find at UF! He is a lenient grader and does not ask for documentation for missed attendance. He truly cares and workload is light unless you fully read the readings every week (not necessary to do well). TAKE HIS CLASSES!!!!!

I cannot recommend this professor more! He is super flexible about absences and is very forward about what he expects and is leniant on grading. The class has a short weekly discussion post, two exams, one paper, and a presentation which sound way worse than they are! If I could take him again I would in a heartbeat!!

OH MY LORD THIS PROFESSOR IS AMAZING. PERIODT. One discussion post per week, about 100-150 words. Then you're also graded on a presentation, a paper, and a essay-based midterm and a final. This professor is the GOAT, ngl, and he also gives us the prompts a week before the exam date. TAKE HIS CLASSES RIGHT NOW

Lots of reading but never did any of it. Prof is chill, just make sure to raise hand at least every other day to ask a question for participation grade. Took over summer B. 2 papers, weekly mini-paper, participation grade (attendance graded), and group project you do on one of the 6 weeks. Paper prompts given week ahead of time. Easy A

What a king. He's new and clearly wants you to like him, which isn't hard because he's very likeable. Really encourages discussion and makes you feel smart. Lots of readings but he lectures on them, so you can skim. Tests are easy if you review the readings. Learned a lot, thought a lot, and I would gladly take another class of his.

analysis.name: William Littlejohn-Oram
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I ended up having William for both CRW1301 and CRW3310, and he is truly one of the best teachers I've had. The classes aren't hard. You get out what you put in, so if you want to become a better writer, put in effort. The papers are simple too. William creates a relaxed environment and is eager to help you. Go to office hours to talk to him!

This class gave me hope that my semester would be okay. Yes, it is an easy credit, but it's also so fun, inspiring, and a great time. The class goes by so fast every time, and the professor is one of the bests I've had. He is extremely kind and is extremely knowledgeable that it was admirable. He clearly loves what he does!

He is quite literally the best instructor I have ever had. He gives insightful feedback for my poems, and he is such a caring instructor that can be reached out to even after the course ends. He is just a wonderful human being who happens to be a great instructor.

William has absolutely been a pleasure to study under. He has done a wonderful job of creating a safe and fun class environment. He has a completely unserious disposition, but is incredibly passionate about writing, reading, and analyzing poetry. He will critique you honestly and effectively, and is genuinely driven by helping you be a better poet!

Mr. Littlejohn-Oram is an incredible teacher who is enthusiastic about what he does. He made me feel comfortable in sharing my work and left great feedback. I learned so much about writing poetry, and he made the three-hour lectures very fun and stimulating. We did writing workshops and went over famous and unique poetry works during the classes.

analysis.name: Adam Veige
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Chem 2 with Dr. Veige can be described simply as a "train wreck". He is cocky, and his arrogance is clear with his exams that are designed to be near impossible. The class average for one exam was a 60% and he blamed that average on students not studying hard. Believe me when I tell you if you want an A in chem 2, stay far away from him.

This class was very difficult, I left every exam feeling defeated even using study edge and studying a week a lot. His exams are tricky and nothing like the questions you see in class. Get study edge and it will help but he is a difficult professor.

If you want your GPA to suffer, this is the BEST CLASS TO TAKE! Dr. Veige's chem 2 is such a nightmare, it's hard to describe. Dr. Veige is cocky, arrogant, and it is clear that he doesn't give a hoot about your performance. He provides little to no guidance when it comes to preparing for exams, which are impossible. SAVE YOURSELF AND YOUR DIGNITY!

Veige is helpful with the content during office hours. However, the exams in this course felt like they were written to trick students so his help did not improve my grade. The material was presented differently in lecture than it was presented on the exams which was extremely frustrating. I felt like I couldn't do anything right in his class.

BEST CHEM 2 PROF!!!!! He's so nice and has a greater demeanor. That said, you should definitely read the textbook/watch yt videos or else lectures didn't make sense and a lot of classmates struggled on exams. At very least write down the practice problems before lecture since he goes through those fast. Everyone wanted to take more classes with him

analysis.name: Chunmei Wang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Made a simple linear algebra class much harder than it needs to be. Weekly quizzes are unreasonably hard with questions far beyond what was covered in class. Lectures are poorly organized and a mess to watch. Lots of extra credit and lenient grading but be prepared to spend a lot of time learning the advanced stuff yourself.

The professor didn't use a textbook, instead copying content from another university's lecture notes without sharing the PDF. Homework was uploaded as screenshots, not LaTeX. Typos and unclear notations, like (A^{-1})^{T} = A^{-T}, caused confusion. Clarification requests on vague homework were refused, saying it'd be unfair.

Tough class, she just reads from the book without providing a clear explanation of the material. Weekly quizzes and mandatory attendance. Get ready to learn from the book if you actually want to understand the material. On the plus side, lots of extra credit and two quizzes dropped.

analysis.name: Jianping Wang
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Although the class was a Summer A Genetics course, I thought Dr. Wang did a pretty good job at teaching. She is generally regarded as the best AGR 3303 prof. The class moves fast and there usually is a test each week. I found the tests to be reasonably difficult but the lecture and attendance pop quizzes do help a great deal in the long run.

I took her class in Summer A, and although it was a fast-pace class, it was manageable. Grade consisted solely on tests, but she gave a lot of extra credit through pop quizzes. Also,  she asks T/F questions every class, which show up word for word on the exam, so make sure you go to class. All around, Dr. Wang is the best professor at UF.

My first B in college. The exams were all trick questions with little time to truly grasp what she was asking. She however gives you plenty of opportunities to better your grade. I felt the powerpoints and lectures were not helpful for the depth of knowledge we had to know to do well. The textbook was easier to understand (surprisingly).

The class was very straightforward. Your grade is dependent on 4 midterm exams and 1 cumulative final exam, but your lowest exam score is dropped. Exams are all multiple choice. She is very knowledgeable about the material, but her accent can make her difficult to understand. Content is only delivered via in-class lectures. Limited extra credit.

Very nice lady. Has a tick accent, but it didn't bother me too much. First 2 exams you will do well if you understand the material. The last 2 exams were very math-heavy and you had to understand application more. Uses iClicker for mandatory participation and attendance. No homework, only quizzes online that are timed. You get a free exam drop.

analysis.name: Andrew Wolpert
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's probably the most adorable person you'll ever meet. I don't think I ever saw him without a huge smile on his face. His lectures can be dry at times but you can tell he really cares about the topic. He's a fair grader and cares about students. Attendance is mandatory. I'd definitely recommend taking good life with this professor.
He's such a sweetheart! He has a fairly standard lecture style, but I do like what he chooses to focus on in Greek history and he's also just the nicest person ever.

Wolpert is definitely a great lecture who makes his class very interesting. He clearly is knowledgeable and passionate. However, this is by far the hardest class in terms of grading I've taken (I've also taken orgo). NOT an easy A, you realllly have to put in the work if you want to do well.

Dr Wolpert, was extremely helpful,friendly, and funny.  While the topic of Athenian Democracy is hard enough to grasp, he broke every aspect down and made it easy to follow.  He doesn't allow cell phones or computers in class, but he does put all the slides on e-learning prior to class. Come to class, it makes it much easier. tests- essay in class.

I found his class boring AT FIRST.  His lectures are long but he tries to make them interesting. Very THOROUGH, passionate, excited about subject.  Lots of reading, mostly covered in class.  Powerpoints are too wordy, but his slides are available online.  Looks like mumbo jumbo unless you attend.  Glad I took this class, he's great, learned a lot.

analysis.name: BingKan Xue
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Good class, but lecture and homework is math-based, while exams are physics problems. It makes the homework not very useful to study from. Use previous years' exams to prepare. Take mech 1 if you want an easy A, take theoretical if you want to learn more physics (...or math, really).

We had two professors for this course. I enjoyed Prof Xue's lecture style much more and his exam questions reflected the lecture content very well. His organization of the class was understandable and he did not over-assign reading sections (unlike the other prof). Attend class, the iClicker gives a lot of extra credit.

Very difficult course, as expected... Introduction to theoretical physics is the first course in the undergrad physics curriculum really introducing you to the formalism. I don't think prof. Xue did a good job explaining the content well. A lot of the math, although meeting the prerequisites for the course, was glanced over with no explanation.

Tests ranged from difficult to straight-forward, but Prof. Xue gives tests from previous years to study. Homework made up 40% of the grade, but extra credit is given throughout the semester. Class sometimes diverged from the lecture notes, but he overall adhered to the structure of the notes.

analysis.name: Ye Xia
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: WORST professor I have EVER experienced at UF. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. The whole class is 2 exams and 1 project. He gives ZERO direction on the group project so you're completely on your own. Assigned homework ON THANKSGIVING. Also the lectures are completely useless. You will want to commit SIGKILL if you take this class

Honestly, I found this class quite interesting, but mostly because of watching the textbook author's lectures on YouTube and reading the textbook. Professor Xia's lectures are dry and drawn out which make them hard to get through. The test questions are easier than the complex homework, but many felt like “trick questions” based on unclear wording.

CSE senior here, Xia was easily the worst. The final exam and project (65% of the final grade) were never released, only the final grade after the semester was over. The prof reads off slides and exams are needlessly difficult. Tip for survival: Jim Kurose (textbook author) videos on youtube. Kurose lectures better in half the time and he smiles.

Might be the worst professor at UF. This guy still being allowed to teach is the worst thing to happen to UF since the shoe throw. In all my life, I've never seen a teacher just not grade the course. Both the final exam (40% of the grade) and semester-long project (another 20%) that we all spent time studying for and working on were just ignored.

Professor Xia is very knowledgeable about computer networks. This class is a lot of reading and homework, but his lectures essentially go over the textbook with slides created by the authors. There are 6 homeworks, two exams, and one semester-long project. Start homeworks early and study several days out from exam and you will be fine.

analysis.name: Xiaochen Duan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is genuinely passionate about math and it's very easy to see that as a a student. He offers additional help if you're struggling personally too. I also personally found his sense of humor very entertaining and it made it easier to keep focused on the class. 10/10 would take again.

Xiaochen is genuinely one of the best TAs at UF. He wants you to succeed in the class and gives you every opportunity to do so. He explains things really well and is always available in office hours to help you!

Best calc TA you can have. His discussions are so fun and he really dives deep into the material and connects it with calc 1 basics. He also prepares you very well for the quizzes and cares about his students.
Absolute goat, no doubt the best TA you can choose for Calc 3. Helpful, passionate, he's got everything.

Mr. Duan was one of the best Teaching Assistants I have ever had the privilege to learn under during my time here at UF. Mr. Duan was always positive and enthusiastic to teach, and would consistently check up on every student to make sure that every one of us actually understood the material that was being taught. Very kind guy would def take again

analysis.name: Long Xiao
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You are set in this class if you study the slideshows - he will never ask you a question that you can't find in the slides. You are supposed to read the textbook, but you don't really have to in order to be successful in this class. He is very kind, reasonable, amusing, and respectable. I really enjoyed his class, and I cannot recommend him enough.

The absolute GOAT. Constantly cracking jokes during his lectures while still going in depth. Posts everything in a timely manner to Canvas. Very flexible to meet with outside of class and responds fast to emails. Some class content can be a little confusing, but it's 100% doable as long as you stay on top of the reading. 100% recommend for anyone.

the best prof hands down. u get a double sided cheat sheet on exams that u can type and print out, lowest quiz is dropped, both he and his lectures are super funny. sometimes his questions can be confusing, but still super easy. he randomly takes attendance 10 times during the semester but youll want to go to his class anyways. extra credit too!!

Honestly such an amazing professor, if you have the chance to take a class with him do it. It is a lecture-based class, attendance is taken randomly on 10 days. There are 8 quizzes which are 4 questions each and based on lecture notes, and 3 exams throughout the semester that he gives you a study guide for and lets you bring in a cheat sheet.

I loved his class. He is super kind, helpful, and approachable. He was always available for extra help and resources to succeed. He also teaches very well. You have to study and understand the material to do well on quizzes and tests, but he sets you up for success. I wish I could take more classes with him because he is the best!

analysis.name: Xumin Zhang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Xumin is funny, enthusiastic, and very knowledgeable. I took his Quest 2 class on Poverty and it was interesting, but a lot of group project work and many reading assignments. In my opinion, the material from this class could be condensed into only a few lectures because it's very repetitive. He is the most responsive professor I've had!

Dr. Zhang's attention to detail, knowledge of agribusiness concepts, and responsiveness are what sets him apart. He genuinely cares about all of his students and his work ethic and dedication to his classes is admirable. The lectures, quizzes, and discussions are straightforward and interesting. The Landscape project is tough be he helps a lot!

Dr. Zhang is the definition of a good Professor. He is very enthusiastic and informative during each one of his lectures, his assignments are very fair, his exams go good as long as you study well. I had him for two classes, one of which was online, and he was great in both. Dr. Zhang, not only wants students to learn but also excel.
Xumin my goat, take this class its so easy

analysis.name: Siyao Xu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Reviews hating on Super Cool Siayo (not Siyao) are misinformation. Girlboss has such a cool cherry sweater and generally just great fashion. She teaches 2061 and we love her for it. She posts a review video before each exam where each question she goes over happens to be the exact same as the exam. 5% extra credit for total grade took me ten mins.
These people who are complaining are the same people who would be crying in 2048. Girlboss is a win!

Dr. Xu was very new to lecturing when I took the class, but she was super receptive to anything to make her class better, even changing her entire quiz format to help us learn better. She loves having people in her office hours and is very easy to ask questions to. One of the sweetest professors in the department for sure, would take again!!!!

Her lectures tend to feel slow, but she gets through all the content fine. Her exams and quizzes are based off the homework but contain some fundamental differences so you will need to understand the content. She brings up relevant research in class sometimes which is cool and she listened to our feedback very well. Her extra credit is generous.

Professor Xu is very clearly new to teaching and is still figuring things out. She is extremely caring, easy to approach, and lenient with grading (exam questions were VERY similar to her reviews). Her lectures were ok. She was very receptive to criticism so I think her courses will only get better from here

analysis.name: Xiaoguang Zhang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A professor whose class is almost entirely determined by 3 exam grades. Lectures are really rudimentary and don't do much to prepare you for the exams which are much harder than the reviews. You'll most likely end up teaching yourself the topics or learn from and do review with the TA's. You can definitely do well in this class but Zhang won't help

He was a very nice guy, but his lectures just weren't great and hard to follow. He'd ramble about unimportant stuff for 75% of class and then rush through what actually mattered and most of the time miss important slides completely. Nothing he said ever really stuck for me, but you're going to have to do a lot of work on your own regardless of prof

Dr. Zhang was pretty good. I enjoyed his class and he was a good lecturer. The grading scale is very lenient as it is an 85. Exams were mostly easy and he provided practice exams and practice problems. There are weekly quizzes and assignments. Neither are too difficult.

Dr. Zhang is a professor who clearly cares a lot about physics and puts a good effort into his lectures and course overall. At times, lectures don't always focus on relevant info to exams and class can be difficult to follow, so be prepared to rely on his provided review problems and homework to fill in some of the gaps in learning.

He seems like a very caring, nice, and knowledgeable guy... but he sucks as a lecturer. He mumbles and wears his mic way too far from his mouth. It's extremely hard to hear anything he has to say, especially when the concepts are this difficult.

The class itself was very hard; exam 1 average was ~75% and exam 2 average was ~55%.

analysis.name: Xiaofei  Bai
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bai deserves all the good things. He is by far the best Professor at UF. I know everyone says “this Professor truly cares about their students” but Dr. Bai blows every other professor out of the water. He is there not to hinder students but to see everyone succeed. Pay attention, do the work, do the extra credit. Effort will be rewarded.

Dr. Bai has been the best professor I've had. I don't typically rate professors on this platform, but Dr. Bai deserves it. He cares more about his students understanding and interest in the material more than anything else. His lectures are fantastic, the exams are material based and you won't be surprised by anything and take adv. of xtra credit.

Professor is super enthusiastic and will help you if you have any questions regarding the lecture. Lectures are presentation that are very easy to read and understand. Tons of extra credit. Tests are not that hard if you go over the lecture slides and practice questions he posts.
If you have to take genetics, take it with him. He wants you to succeed and makes it so attainable to do very well in his class. Exams are straightforward and there's extra credit.

Ive never rated a professor before but I feel like Bai deserves the shoutout he truly cares about his students doing well and you should take him if you want to do well in genetics his test are very straight forward most of the exam question come from in class Iclickers which he goes over and the other comes from homework.He also ofers extra credit

analysis.name: Myunghee You
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Her class was easy but her organization needs serious work, a majority of her lectures consisted of scribbles on a white board and she barely covered the useful slides that she has posted on canvas. The exams are open note, but short on time. Its an easy class but not an easy elective to get an A in because of the two heavily weighted exams.

She provides a lot of information, but does not communicate exactly what will be tested. We had 4 exams, two multiple choice and two essay format. Her grading criteria is unclear and subjective. If you're thinking of taking this as an elective, I'd suggest taking something else.

Dr. You is very nice and obviously cares about our success in the class. Over the semester, there were 5 discussions posts and one essay, with two open note/online exams that were taken in class. The graphs that she made for lectures were hard to understand, but the slides themself had all the information. Easy A and really nice person in general!

2 open note exams in class heavily weighted. 5 discussion posts, EASY & a final essay. Grades discussions and essays very easily. Exams are pretty hard as you dont have much time to look for the answers in the slides so use other sources. All theories we talk about I learned in crim theory so u dont need to listen to lectures but go for attendance.

Mrs. You is the sweetest professor I have had, and she really cares about her students. I easily got a 99.75% in this class as both exams were open notes and all answers were in the PowerPoint. The class only has a few assignments though (5 discussion posts, 2 exams, attendance grade, and an essay). In my opinion, it is an easy A class.

analysis.name: Yang Lin
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Lin has changed the course since these comments have been made. He's reduced the amount of technical information students need to know and regularly checks in with students if his material is too complex/mathy for a Gen Ed. He gives practice material in-person, attendance helps. Weekly readings are the main hw, but it's an easy grade boost

This professor was a very easy grader and knows that students just want to pass this class. However, his lectures/readings are incredibly unhelpful. He doesn't communicate clearly in person or via email so expectations are unclear. Overall, I'm happy I took this easy Quest but I truly hope that I never come into contact with this professor again.

DO NOT TAKE UNINTENDED CONSEQUENCES IN THE ENVIRONMENT. This professor is extremely frustrating and the class is very confusing. He makes exams based on AI and the weekly readings have the barest of connections to the environment, and often have very complex physics and chemistry topics that for some reason are necessary to understand.

Never take this if you're looking for an easy quest. He made this class unusually hard even though he knows most students are taking it to satisfy the mandatory requirement. You have 2 exams where the questions don't make sense bc they're AI generated, large assignments, a huge project and in person discussions. His lectures aren't even cohesive.

This class was very confusing and had little to do with the environment. The readings were mainly about complex math and physics theories and were far above the level of the class. The tests were made using AI and were, therefore, confusing. I feel as though I got nothing out of this class, and it was a waste of time.

analysis.name: Youping Chen
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She was very hard to understand during lectures. In addition to her accent, she started wearing a mask about halfway through the semester which made understanding her twice as hard. Otherwise, she is a decent teacher. Exams are graded lightly with an additional 10% added on to each exam if you do the extra credit. Cares a lot about students

Lectures were basically pointless other than getting attendance credit. She was very hard to understand, spoke fast, and had pretty bad handwriting, so you would actually gain nothing trying to listen during lectures. Only hope is to read the book and learn yourself. She does give exam redos for extra points which does help out a lot.

Quite possibly the most useless professor at UF. Not only does she speed through lectures to the point where it's impossible to keep up, she doesn't prepare well enough for lectures to adequately answer questions when students ask them. Her exams and final project are also ridiculous, as she's just as unclear about how to approach them.

Understanding her in lectures was extremely difficult. Her exams would often have the same questions she did as examples in class, so it's great to have paid attention during lectures. She allows a formula sheet during exams that you can write anything on. Write class examples. Homework was tough for sure. She allows exam corrections for points tho
She knows the subject very well.

analysis.name: Yixuan Li
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: MAN5246, great professor. The lectures were long but the exam was not difficult since you were able to bring a sheet of notes. Group assignment lacked clear instructions but overall would take again.
Class is overall very easy in terms of work and content. The exam is very similar to the study guide and class slides. Highly recommend as an easy elective!
Great class and great professor. The workload was very light and exam was very straightforward!

Hey Masters' student! Do not worry, this professor is not severely group project heavy! VERY FEW assignments, and they are all very manageable. There are no textbooks (just slides) and TECHNICALLY you do not have to attend every class. BUT she does random extra credit and participation assignments in class, so go to class. Easy A :)
Overall a very straightforward class that is has a very managable workload. Highly reccomend professor Li!

analysis.name: Heather Young
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was very paper heavy. Some assignments are confusing, but just email her. She responds with clear instruction if asked. Be prepared to write about the same topic throughout the semester. Papers got a little tedious but it's very easy to do well. She offers several extra credit opportunities. Everything graded by TAs.

All around the best professor I have had at the University of Florida. She is very fair with grading amd every assignment has a rubric to follow so there is never any confusion on what you need for class or when it is due. If you are looking to take a speech class for requirment or not this is the one to take.

This class is a lot of work, very tedious, time-consuming, and annoying. Your TA grades everything. That being said, there's so many extra credit opportunities that have brought up my overall grade like 3%. Put in the effort and you'll be fine, still an annoying class tho. I took this during the summer with 3 other stem classes and still got an A

The class consisted of weekly writing assignments (~300-500 words) and discussion posts. The assignments were very repetitive and oftentimes asked for the same information as the previous week's assignment. The grading guidelines were sometimes unclear, though the assignments themselves were very easy. Highly dependent on your TA.

Final exam was easy. The speeches were doable, just put in some effort and you'll get a decent grade. As long as you turn things every Sunday and do the participation quizzes during the main lectures, getting an A is easy. I didn't need to study or prepare too much.

analysis.name: Alex York
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 103 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This was a great class! The lectures are kind of boring and the homework takes a long time, but I think this class works really well being online. Spend maybe 2 or 3 hours a day (including the 1hr lecture) and you should be fine. Exams are very fair and straightforward, but be weary for tricks!

Busywork, busywork, busywork!! Next to zero extra credit, exams are weighted heavily. Homework is incredibly time-consuming. His Summer C lectures were disorganized and sometimes quite long. Expect a fairly straightforward but time-consuming class. Exam content is straightforward, but this class feels more like applied precalculus than calculus.

Bang average professor, long boring lectures he zips through without much explanation half the time. Homework takes a ludicrous amount of time to do for what the content is. That being said, the class concepts are not hard. Just be ready to spend 3 hours on one unit between the lecture/lecture quiz/hws.

The lecture videos were good means of learning, but they were monotone and boring especially with the long lectures at the end of the course. The exams are weighted heavily, but the exams are easy if you take the time to study and do practice exams that are provided.

There are about 2-3 lectures per week, and each lecture has a 10-20 question homework as well as a quiz with 3-5 questions. The tests are exactly like the quiz questions and are pretty easy. I never had to interact with the prof during the course because it was online and I had no technical difficulties. The beginning of course is easy, end is meh.

analysis.name: Gaia Zori
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Zori was one of the kindest teachers I have ever had. Her class was fairly easy with weekly group assignments, one individual paper, and one group presentation. She had two exams, both with extra credit and open-note quizzes.
She is extremely kind and one of those few teachers who enjoys her job. Her class was low stress and fair exams and assignments. I wish she was my teacher for every class.
Great professor. She is very knowledgable on the topics she teaches. She cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. It is an engaging, debate-structured class.

Dr. Zori is one of the best professors I have ever had!! She loves to teach, and it really shows, she is very knowledgeable, understanding, and helpful. She wants you to succeed. I cannot say enough good things, take any and every class of hers you can!
Dr. Zori's expectations for assignments were very clear and she is a very fair grader. The class is structured as a debate with 500 word reflections afterwords.

analysis.name: Zhifeng (James) Chen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Tests consisted of key terms from lecture/textbook (he gives you a list of them in advance) and analysis of primary/secondary sources that we went over in class. The lectures can be fast and dense, if you get the big picture it's alright. Lot of readings, but they were really interesting! Slow grader, but a good lecturer that wants you to succeed.

Professor was condescending and impatient with student questions/concerns. Pulls very vague impossible details from books on quizzes and tests every/every other week. Office hours did not help, email gets you no where. Accused students of cheating with no basis. Multiple students withdrew mid-semester from distress. It's not worth it - AVOID!

Worst class i have ever taken. Does not give clear instructions. NO TECHNOLOGY ALLOWED. Good luck on the quizzes, they are the most obscure terms and questions you'll ever see. Lectures are almost obsolete and does not matter to any of the essays or quizzes. Everything graded is on the textbook or the two books you read for the class.

He is a friendly professor, but he takes forever to grade and frequently does not provide feedback for why he is grading you as harshly as he is. Unless you are physically in his office for office hours, he will not respond. Ignores emails, grades harshly, and does not teach the material that you are expected to master.

professor will not answer questions, accuses multiple students of cheating to be proven wrong, gives 0 guidance and will tell you to figure it mout when asked for help. rather than helkping you he will tell you to drop the course. should not be teaching at the University of Florida

analysis.name: Aaron Zubia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very intellectual professor, not a super interesting dude though and lectures are slow and fairly boring. Super fair grader, fun reading topics and very helpful in terms of feedback. Understanding, forgiving and nice guy, class was very straight forward you'll get a good grade with any amount of effort.

He is smart, but as smart as he is, he is twice as boring. Also, if you're a conservative, he will like you more. It is not super noticeable, but he tries to have some gotcha moments if you lean more liberal on the topics we're discussing. But he does foster good discussion, and I never felt super uncomfy giving my opinion.

Wouldn't recommend this class. Very reading-heavy and you will find yourself getting more work from this class than any other (quizzes, reflections, etc). While Dr. Zubia is funny and knowledgeable, he doesn't provide any kind of clear grading rubric & the material is unorganized, so students often have to remind him to upload the assignments.

The readings are a lot. Though they weren't too bad in and of themselves, I often found the quizzes to be more based on memorization of the texts rather than comprehension. That said, Dr. Zubia is an amazing professor and very intelligent. He works to make himself available outside of class, and there is extra credit later on that really helps.

This class had the highest amount of readings and the most difficult ones of any class I've taken. There are also quizzes every week. That being said, he cares about his students. If you go to office hours and engage respectfully in class, you can get a good grade. It will also GREATLY prepare you for any high-level poli-sci course.

analysis.name: Zulma Zayas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Makes you buy a $90 dollar course subscription to get all your homework, quizzes, and tests on top of the tuition you're already paying and converted some assignments to harder, in-person versions to make "grading easier", even though all the homework, quizzes, and exams are automatically graded. Just making things harder for students ultimately.

Yary is truly the best professor I've had at UF. Her enthusiasm and energy created an environment I genuinely looked forward to every day. Even when attendance wasn't required, I still chose to go because I enjoyed the class so much. ASL 1 isn't a difficult course when you put in the time and effort. So grateful I took ASL with her!!!!

Professor Santiago's lectures are very fun and engaging. Classes are canceled fairly often and attendance is not mandatory. Everything is accessible online if you miss class and she's really easy to reach through email or office hours if you struggle with anything or have any questions. I had a great experience and plan to take ASL 2 with her too!

Professor Yary is by far one of the best professors I've had at UF. I had her for both ASL 1 and 2, and her care for the language is evident through her teaching. She is great at explaining signs and will always take the time to answer any question you may have. You can tell she loves what she teaches.

Don't take this course with this professor if you suffer from ANY anxiety. The professor was rudely snapping and groaning at me because I had struggled to sign my name during the first week of class and that behavior continued throughout the semester. So many days I left embarrassed and on edge due to her teaching style.

analysis.name: Andrew Zimmerman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Don't take this class. I needed something for my Science credit and expected a class called Oceanography to be manageable at the least, but it's unexecpectedly (and unecessarily) hard. Professor Zimmerman does not seem to understand that most students are only taking the class to fulfill a credit, and the class seems to be overly hard. Don't take.

Exams are 72% of your grade. Very hard to get full credit on exams. Extra credit of 2% offered for going on field trip. I studied for hours for the first 2 exams and it will be hard for me to get an A with only one exam left. Discussions and exercises are easy and quick to do. I would not take him again because of the grading scale, but nice guy.

The exams are just sm harder than you would think for a class titled, "oceanography." I went to almost every lecture and just still did not do well. He offers extra credit but like idk. Take something easier, it is not worth it.

I took this class for my gen ed for science, and it turned out to be way harder than expected. His lectures are very important to pay attention, and only some of the information you need to memorize is given on the study guide. You should really memorize the practice questions given in lectures and the study guide questions.

Took this class for my gen ed science course, and it turned out to be much harder than expected. Tests were basically your entire grade, and they were hard. Make sure you look over provided practice test, and rely heavily on in class practice questions. Extra credit was given to raise grade 2%.

analysis.name: Jindrich Zapletal
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I have never heard the word "ah" more times in my short existence on this earth before entering into this man's lectures. I would strongly recommend against taking any class of his, as you will be on your own as far as the material goes.

Dr. Zapletal seemed as if he absolutely hated having to teach students. I recently discovered that he is tenured and that helped to explain his attitude. I'm not sure if he had an accident of some sort or if he genuinely has terrible public speaking skills but he stutters like it is his job. It is very difficult to understand him in lectures.

Makes lectures and content pretty digestible and generally easy to understand. Follow along with the textbook and make sure you can do lecture and homework problems on your own. He provides one sample exam for each of the midterms and the final, pretty realistic in difficulty level to the actual exams. Witty guy + keeps it interesting. Fair grading

The class isnt too bad, for what it is, considering the other lecturer provided all other resources and information. Zapletals lectures were, however, awful. I couldnt focus on anything through his speech impediment, and often left feeling more confused about the subject matter.

Prof Zapletal is alright... your grade is based off three exams and six homeworks, so its very easy to quickly drop to a low grade. His lectures arent very clear, and some complicated proofs that dont show how to complete basic proofs using the theorem. Personally, the textbook didnt help me much either, so I had to rely on outside sources.

analysis.name: Yong Zeng
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are meaningless; I went to class. I believe one would've done better self-studying the entire class than listening to him. Originally had 6 homework assignments, but reduced it to 5, leading to less buffer for grade. Talks more about research than the actual class itself. Had extra material to go over, so he had class during reading days.

Dr. Zeng is a very kind professor and was very responsive via email. Grades are based off 2 midterms + 1 Final, which is primary based on chapters 20-26. His lectures were informative but really had no benefits to me doing well on the exams. If you're passionate about chemistry take him. The final exam at the end is challenging but fair. Good luck!

Professor Zeng's lectures are just screenshots and snippets of the book read out, which are not at all helpful.  His grading is very inconsistent, with points being deducted on homeworks for no discernable reason.  There was a large amount of extra credit at the end of the course.

Half of the material overlapped with statistics and gen chem, but I often left class feeling confused. He's kind but doesn't explain content well--definitely read the textbook. Grade is only based on four exams, each with 20 MCQ and sometimes a short response, and you get to drop your lowest exam grade. Few useful practice questions are given.

Dr. Zeng didn't explain material clearly. It felt like it was a better use of time to skip lectures and read the textbook instead. His material was mostly about statistics and a deeper dive into chem 2 topics with a small section on chemistry instruments. Your grade is based on  3 exams and the final, but 1 of them can get dropped.

analysis.name: Laura Acosta
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: BEWARE of her flipped classroom-style class with mandatory attendance. However, she was a really sweet and caring professor. Provided notes corresponding to each lecture and study guides that I relied on to study for exams. Preferred her over the other professor that teaches this class and is prominent in HUN.
The SWEETEST most caring professor I've had. Her exams are very fair, and the material is interesting. Take her if you can!!

Such an amazing human aside from teaching. Very caring and makes material so interesting and helps students without making us feel bad. I think if I paid attention more during class instead of cramming I could've gotten an A. Exam averages were literally 95%, she's amazing

Professor Acosta lectures so well that it makes you NOT want to miss lectures. She is kind, approachable, and is by far the best professor I have had at UF during my three years here so far. I would highly recommend this class. It does require studying, but nothing out of the ordinary. You will not regret taking this class with Dr. A. Loved it!

Dr. Acosta was such a wonderful teacher. This was an Honors Uncommon Read course, and I honestly didn't know what to expect, but Dr. Acosta was warm and genuine from the start. She demonstrated true respect for students to speak truthfully in her classroom and always seemed understanding of everyone's different perspectives.

analysis.name: Lisha Zhou
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 108 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Took this class in Fall semester 2024. Overall, the class was relatively easy. It definitely helps to have prior coding experience coming in as the first few weeks were essentially teaching you how to use an IDE and how to code in python. Labs are easy, exams are kinda hard, and don't procrastinate on projects. They are really long.

Her lectures are hard to understand, her grading is so strict, definitely not beginner friendly. However she is available a lot after class but beware of the queue. Take this class if you started coding in the womb. If not, do yourself a favor and skip

This review is for CDA 3101--wasn't an option in the RMP drop-down menu.   Prof. Zhou is easily one of the most caring and responsive professors that I've had.  She goes far out of her way to make learning comfortable and enjoyable for everyone.   I will absolutely take a course with her again if I have the opportunity.  Inspirational!

workload is insane for a intro class. she doesn't curve bc the average on the tests is around a 70%, but she doesn't consider that most people already have prior experience, and the people who don't get screwed. projects take forever, there's a lab every week, and you don't get a moment to rest and catch your breath.

I didn't rely much upon her teaching abilities, but the class structure is excellent. The projects and labs blend together the material quite well. As long as you are able to keep up it is manageable and even easy. Plenty of extra credit.

analysis.name: Dario Teran Acaro
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: TA Acaro is a great reinforcer for the knowledge tought in Calc 2. At the begenning it may be hard to differientiate between his 4's and his 9's but it will get easier with time. He also is very clear on the grading criteria, and grades very case-by-case basis, potentially leading to you doing very well on exams. His lectures are elite!

He was a very good professor and explained each concept pretty clearly. Everything for the course is explicitly stated and he gives practice tests for each exam that are identical to the exams but with different numbers. Overall a great teacher and very easy class.

He was my TA for Calc 2 alongside Prof Chui. He always worked out problems well for us and was a big part of my earning an A in the class. His grading gave feedback on what we did wrong, and he is such a great person to talk to. Big Ecuador soccer fan!
He was an incredible TA. He was able to make difficult concepts easier to understand and he always helped us with any problems that we had.

analysis.name: Darin Acosta
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Acosta is a genius when it comes to physics, and teachers the material well, but not well enough in comparison to the exams. For PHY2048 Spring 2017, he taught the class until the first exam. I needed to use Study Edge as a supplement to the lectures. The tutoring offered made the difference in my test grade. I don't know one person who didn't SE.

A nice guy, but a horrendously bad teacher. Demonstrations are cool, but can you focus on teaching instead? I don't know how the Rice Physics department manages to hire low-quality professors. The only person who is worse than this man is Jared Stetson.
Excellent teacher. Very fair grading and tests. Very good at getting students to understand the material. Quite possibly the best Physics teacher at UF.

Physics is a tough subject overall. Exams are difficult, but not impossible. They made the class this semester a flipped classroom where you watch lecture videos at home and then do example problems in class. In my opinion, this was somewhat annoying but the videos were very decent at teaching the subject. I recommend going to class for clicker pts

Physics is already a hard class and even though Acosta tried to make lectures worth going, he did not go into depth about topics on exam  or give any example problems for what the exam would be like. He is very enthusiastic but not a great teacher. I used Study Edge to help me because lectures were not helping and got an A- in the class.

analysis.name: Norma Aceves
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Her class is dependent upon three essays you write, three group projects, community service, and attendance, so go to class and make those papers good!  Her class is super easy.  There is a lot to read, but no busy work.  You can get by with Sparknotes for your readings.  However, she never gives clear rubrics for her assignments.

As the other reviews say, she advocates for mental health. She canceled our final essay because she figured it added undue stress. Bless her soul. The reviews that say she grades every once in a blue moon are true. But know that she isn't a harsh grader. I devoted, on average, 1.5-2 hours a WEEK for this class, and it should be the easiest A ever.

She will fail you if your assignments are late. She wont budge on this and it is discouraging. I dont want to complete assignments because she never rewards me for doing them. Its a draconian method of teaching. She grades the assignments through the rubric, but gives you a zero even if you did everything right because it was a few hours late :(

Professor Aceves is one of the kindest, most caring professors I've had at UF. From the start, she was a vocal advocate for mental health and treated us accordingly. The class isn't difficult at all. She's understanding about extenuating circumstances, willing to meet with you to help you do your best work, and wants all her students to succeed!

Prof. Aceves is a queen. She is so empathetic and understanding especially during the pandemic. She cares about her students and is a very fun and nice person. I learned a lot in her class about writing in my industry that I will carry with me forever. She is one of the only professors at UF that truly cares about students mental health.

analysis.name: Charles Acheson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I had him for the section Writing About Summer. He asks questions that open up to interesting discussions in class. He takes his time to thoroughly explain writing assignments and rubrics and if that's not clear enough, he is happy to explain further and answer questions after class. He gives a lot of helpful feedback on papers.

By far my favorite teacher when it comes to a writing class at UF. He provides interesting discussion and as long as you show that you care during discussions and go to office hours to go over your papers, he will help you do very well in this class. Definitely try to get any of his sections because I know he teaches multiple writing courses.

Acheson is a very clear and engaging professor, and he gives excellent feedback which you can then use to earn some points back in revisions. The Ways of Reading textbook is essential at the beginning of the semester because there are passages in there that you will write papers on, but he only assigned reading from the other textbook.

analysis.name: Kendall Ackley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Kendall Ackley was the best TA I've ever had. First of all, she's a genius. Second of all, she's a genius that is easy to understand. She really knows her stuff. I would definitely recommend her! She is very good at explaining stuff and really helped me out with everything. Hands down the best at UF!
Very helpful and laid-back. She tries to help you understand the material and do well in the course.
Pretty cool TA, lets us call her by nicknames. Definitely would recommend her lab to one of my bros.

analysis.name: Georgia Ackermann
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
