review_highlights.comment: Requires a lot of reading, often about the same subject in many different articles.  She's not a bad teacher, but she stresses developing a repitore with students and then makes her students use name tags throughout the semester because she won't learn names.  Not the greatest of classes, but you do learn the law and you'll get through it fine.

She is a fine teacher, but she quizzes on material before she goes over it in class.  The quizzes count for a good part of your grade.  This is why I did not get an A in her class.  The material on the quizzes changes as well so be careful.  Other than that she was fine!

Can't recall the course names, but I had her for two.  The type of teacher and person that reminds you of your own personal responsibilities!!!  You MUST want to be outstanding if you want to rise to her expectations.

This class is useless.  The material is covered with minimal effectiveness.  The material is rum through quickly to meet EAS requirements but there is no knowledge gained.  Professor Ackerman is extremely helpful.
This teacher is great to have for your first semester in Proteach.  She is helpful and knows a lot about the field she's in, which makes it fun.  If you have the option- Take her!!!

analysis.name: Dror Abend-David
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I've taken three classes with Dror throughout my college career. The first as a first semester freshman and the last as a spring semester junior. He has taught me in and out of the classroom very important lessons about life. I enjoyed going to his class and participating. I have the utmost respect for him as a professor and as a person.

Very cool teacher, doesn't stick to the syllabus really but you end up learning something. Grading is a bit weird but if you listen in class it shouldn't be hard at all to get an A. Would definitely recommend.

disorganized, no lesson plan,class time is wasted with games that has no pedagogical reflection,deducts large grades for innocent mistakes, never accept grades negotiation even if all class agreed he is wrong. ask us to prepare no. of pages and the next day he teaches other pages,a very easy course was converted into a hard and stressful.

I took Yiddish Language & Culture. The class was easy, especially if you already know the Hebrew alephbeth (or alefbeys), or any German. The lessons are taken directly from the textbook (can be found as a PDF). There were only 4 other people in the class (!!!) when I took it, so you could choose to accelerate your studies almost one-on-one, or not.

Dror has mandatory attendance, which is necessary as the only way students would attend his dry lectures. He likes to stand up front and talk the entire class, with the occasional calling on students or pairing us into groups. Despite the heavy lectures, you won't feel particularly knowledgeable when you leave. The essays are vague but graded easy.

analysis.name: Abdoulaye Kane
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Becoming Black is absolutely one of the easier Quest 1 classes, considering the horror stories I've heard from others. The readings aren't anything crazy, but you are expected to submit thoughtful questions for discussions. Lectures are nothing super special, but you can tell Dr. Kane loves what he does.

Love Kane! He was always understanding and easy to reach outside of class, and also passionate and well-versed in what he taught. The class is reading heavy. I skimmed most of them. Weekly is question actually a lot of ur grade. Grading is subjective, and based on TA. The TA was Ryan Cousins was cool and funny, but don't expect a free 100 on them!

No final exam, just an essay and a presentation. Few other essays but grading was free. Every week was a reading you could skim and you had to come up with a question for the discussion on Fridays. Reading was dense but you didn't need to know much. Lectures were kind of boring so I did work for other classes. He is passionate and talks a lot.

Great class. Workload is super light. Prof is so willing to help his students and his passion for his work really shows. Wonderful readings. If you happen to not be able to do them then the lectures summarize them. There's only one exam and he's a super lenient grader. Otherwise, it's pretty much a paper, presentation, and small quizzes.

The lectures didn't have much to do with the assignments we had to do, but attendance was mandatory. There are some short response papers and at the end of the semester there was a very open essay and group project. It seemed like if you did it, you would get a good grade. It is evident he cared though and was thoughtful during lectures.

analysis.name: Amr Abd-Elrahman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Great teacher! Very helpful.  He is a long distance teacher, at least for my course, and he was always available to take calls, emails, etc for GIS questions!  Slight accent, but better than almost all other professors at UF.
Is extremely thorough when teaching, takes an unnecessarily long time to explain things. Classes have alot of work but you can get help easily.

Review for SUR3641 - survey computation class. Very fair grading and curves class. If you show up, show your work, and have understanding of the problem the grades will reflect that. Gives credit for coherent attempts. Fast grader and will provide extra time and feedback if needed. Homework is heavy and lots of spreadsheets. Good exp. overall.

Grading scale is so biased toward not getting an A from this course, as if, the aim is not to learn, but to get any grade less than A. Assignment rubrics are not in detail and you get your points deducted for something that was not asked in the assignment.
Overall, I do not recommend this course.

The professor is very knowledgeable and helpful. The course can be demanding at first, but once you advance in the course you just follow the system smoothly. The professor answers students' questions efficiently and quickly. I also learned GIS! I recommend taking this course with Dr. Amr.

analysis.name: Abdolkarim Asghari
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: MCB3020 with Asghari was the best class I could've chosen to take alongside Orgo 1 in terms of manageability. There's weekly homework and quizzes on McGraw-Hill which are busy work (imo they're not helpful, just something you have to complete). W/ extra credit and 90 is an A

The class is pretty similar to genetics in terms of content but just in less detail. I think it's obvious the professor cared about the class and he was quite knowledgable about the content.

Dr. Asghari was a great professor! All the lectures are online, and he posts slides to accompany the videos. I used Smokin Notes to study for the exams, and it helped me do well and understand the content.

Dr. Asghari uploads all of his material ahead of time which makes it helpful for studying ahead. The grading scale is also not too lecture heavy which makes the grading scale manageable, plus extra credit. I found the Smokin Notes study guide suggestions useful when studying for the exams.

Super nice professor overall, and you could tell that he definitely cared about what he was teaching. His lecture videos were a bit confusing, but the study guides helped a lot. The exams were pretty straight forward, and I barely used SmokinNotes.

analysis.name: Abby Owens

review_highlights.comment: GOAT Calc 3 TA. She has a website with past exams for all the tests that are great study resources. She goes over the exact kind of question that will be on the quiz right before you take it. Also very knowledgeable and can explain basically all questions.

If you have the option to choose your TA, take Calc 3 with Abby.  I have nothing but amazing things to say about her.  She clearly explained all content and was very accessible for her office hours.  If I ever had any concerns prior to exam day, she would clearly detail any practice problems I needed.

Abby is genuinely one of the best TA's I have ever had for a class, she explained topics so thoroughly and made concepts so much clearer while also being the sweetest person ever. I truly looked forward to going to her office hours every week, sometimes just to chat and give myself a short break from studying. Highly recommend her!!

Abby was an amazing TA - always welcoming and patient. She explained tough topics clearly and made sure everyone understood. Her relaxed, supportive environment made it easy to engage or just take a brain break by listening or chatting. One of the best TA's I've ever had - I wish I could have her for more classes!

analysis.name: Rock Aboujaoude Jr

review_highlights.comment:
The one thing you gotta understand about Professor Rock, is he's very descriptive on each energy development module of the class. He teaches in a way that made us feel like he was guiding rather than lecturing, unlike many other professors in this department. 

He also uses a lot of Lord of the Rings memes and references 

10/10
I loved Rock!  He was clear about instructions and always took time from his day to help when we had questions.
Rock was the best TA I have ever had! During office hours he would always be available to help with readings and even met with me outside of class many times.

analysis.name: Zhanar Abil
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR FOR GENETICS. She made this class 10x more difficult than it needed to be. First, she gives a final which not all professors do. The exams, except the final, were multiple choice AND short answer. The short answer was extremely difficult (ie. one question asked to draw transcription, like tf???). Very nice women though.

Read straight from the slides.  When I asked her to explain test questions she essentially restated what the answers were without adding any other information.
After publicly stating on canvas that the test scores were far worse than she wanted or expected, she just said "oh well" and submitted grades.  No curve, no extra credit, nothing.

Class wasn't difficult material wise, but it's a lot, and receiving an A is nearly impossible. Prepare to STUDY. LONG textbook. You need a 94 to obtain an A, which meant small wiggle room in this exam heavy class. Hated the group project; graded harshly by TAs, which I felt was unfair. This class caused me a lot of stress. But very nice professor.

Here's the strat:

1. 10/20 lectures for 1% of the grade, up to you to allocate your time.
2. Have the self-discipline to make sure you understand the material
3. iClicker and past test questions make up the exams
4. Textbook and slides are more than enough to gauge what you need to know
5. 94% is an A but it's manageable
6. Do homework, it's light

Extremely bad lecturer, she does not even seem interested in the topic she is teaching, and lectures for two hours in a monotone voice. I was not even going to bother writing a review but even after being a horrible professor and claiming that grade curving was up to her discretion, she would not give me .5% to bring my grade to an 80.

analysis.name: Abigail Held
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You can tell Professor Held is passionate about chemistry but she lacks organizational skills. She often gets off topic during class leading us to fall behind in the lectures. Tests are not too hard just complete the her assigned work. Do go over your tests to make sure there are no discrepancies because she can make mistakes grading.

She is a very likable person, but class is awful. All exam grades were very low. Lectures were so unorganized. Every exam had topics not covered. Test questions built on each other so getting one thing wrong cause you to get the next 5 wrong.Tests on small details instead of big pictures.Homework is nothing like the test material. Take another prof

No point in going to lectures, they make it more confusing. Talks in circles and has no idea if we can apply material. Makes plenty of mistakes and lectures are chaotic. Be prepared to buy study edge. Assignments are on multiple platforms, but content does not go together. On every exam, there was something brand new never taught in class.

She was just okay. I dont think I got too much homework, but learning from lectures were hard. Sometimes it was just the TA and it was hard to hear at times. The homework (ALEKS) was a waste of time. She didnt give out any practice exams to study from so for the 4 exams it was hard to study.

I thought this class was pretty challenging considering it is only an intro level chem class. Professor Held was very caring but often times I got confused during her lectures. Truthfully study edge is what got me to fully understand the material.

analysis.name: Lise Abrams
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Abrams is such an enthusiastic professor who loves what she does. She will always show up to class excited to lecture! Her passion for her subject actually made me want to major. Her exams are a bit tough but she is generous when grading assignments.

Prof Abrams is very caring and a great lecturer. I learned a lot. But her quizzes are SO DIFFICULT, pure memorization: she would pull out one random sentence from a reading and ask you to fill in the blank. She's very nice but very hard to talk to and is so strict about grading. Don't take her intro if you have other choices.

She says the class is tough but fair, which sums it up really well. Abrams is a great professor and you will learn a lot. Tests are challenging so study hard. She also takes attendence on random days.

Dr. Abrams is amazing. Everyone complains about how hard her class is, but come on it college what did you expect? She is the first professor that has truly challenged me, and I love her for it. She loves what she teaches and is extremely helpful. I think he exams are difficult but fair. If you really want to learn cog. psych. take it w/ her :o)

If you are looking for an easy A do NOT take this class. On that note, Dr Abrams is a fantastic teacher. SUPER nice and helpful and uses plenty of examples to make sure the concept really sinks in. Her tests are hard. Really hard. But you can go sit in her office & talk about it later. Very casual, comfortable office hours. Approachable. But tough.

analysis.name: Adam B. Munson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The stats class with Dr. Munson was amazing. He was clear on grading and was fair on everything he did. He used a book that taught the key basics of a very difficult topic. His lectures and methods of working out problems helped students succeed. You should easily get an A if you do the homework and quizzes and study those concepts for the exams.
The class is pretty easy but the tests can be a little tricky, tutoring zone helped with that.

Professor Munson's lectures were long and helpful, especially for the conceptual questions on the exam. He lost me several times when going through the Excel but nothing that a specific tutoring service did not help. The Excel stuff is not hard, it just takes a few times to understand, so go through several problems. His quizzes help with exam prep

Average difficulty business class. Very understanding and very lenient. Not that engaging of a class but he genuinely cares about helping you succeed. You do have to put time into the capsim simulation but as long as you don't do it last minute like a lot of people, you're fine and he walks through it in class. Overall just a good professor.

He gave me an extention/make up for an exam no questions asked. Very laid back and not that hardcore of a professor which is really nice as a senior. If you are failing at the end of the course he gives you extra credit so that you don't fail which is really nice especially since people take this senior year to not delay graduation.

analysis.name: Adam Lebovitz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lebovitz crafted a masterful, thought-provoking course examining democracy's trajectory throughout history. The class style is interactive, and he gives tremendous feedback on written assignments. In this course, you truly get out what you put in; while the readings are difficult, he frames them well and directs insightful conversation.

Take this class if you enjoy engaging with your peers and thinking critically. The professor may be intimidating at first because he expects the students to be engaged, but he is incredibly well spoken and knowledgeable about the subject matter. Good for those interested in pursuing a degree within the Hamilton center too.

He assigns too much work, especially for a Quest I. Classes are repetitive and he makes you feel stupid, no matter how much effort you put into preparation. He does give good writing advice and he's passionate about the subject, but then again, its a Quest course and its not worth the stress. Don't take unless you're really interested in democracy.

[ISS1684: What is Democracy?] Cannot recommend this professor enough. The course does take some time and critical thinking, especially during discussion where he makes sure you know what you are talking about. However, he's probably my favorite professor this semester: gives amazing feedback, is clearly very knowledgeable, and makes the class fun!

ISS 1684: He is SUCH a great lecturer and really understands how to pick your brain. Participation is a large part and it can sometimes feel very difficult or intimidating to engage. Overall, SUCH an interesting course. Don't take if looking for an easy quest class you can sit through. It requires a lot of engagement, but I felt it was worth it!!

analysis.name: Stephen Adams
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 134 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Every type of problem that could show up on a test is in his notes. He's very detailed and goes at a good pace. Lectures are recorded, homework is tedious (as with all math) but incredibly doable with unlimited attempts. I like math, but even if you don't I think he makes the subject accessible and comprehensible to anyone.

He's a good lecturer for most people but I couldn't grasp the content and struggled. Adams & Calc 2 just isn't for me I guess. The exams are brutal. Study ahead of time by using the past exams and resources on canvas. Don't forget to do homework or particpation quizzes. The TAs are helpful. Set up 1 on 1 meetings with them if you are struggling.

Amazing math professor that made Calculus 2 bearable. He has in-depth lectures that explain not only how certain techniques work but also why they work. The Xronos assignments are annoying sometimes, but understandable for this class, and even if the tests are difficult he properly prepares his students for every question within his lectures.

Calc 2 is horrendous (especially for the 2nd time since I have to retake lol) but I feel like if you genuinely keep up and practice the homework every single day, you'll do fine. It just moves extremely quick and I was always behind. Felt like the other prof (Chui) gave more shortcuts/tips on her notes/office h, I ended up going to her to learn tbh

Adams is such a kind, funny, caring individual who I love having as a professor (please be my father). He makes the material feel natural and go by quickly, and I didn't struggle in this class because of him. I highly recommend going to lectures to not fall behind, but it goes by quickly and the homework is short. 10/10 teacher, would take again.

analysis.name: Adrienne Strong

review_highlights.comment: SO MUCH READING but at least it's usually pretty interesting. She makes us read so much but spends almost no time on the readings. The class was structured as team based learning.

Lots of readings each week but they're interesting. The class uses team-based learning and you'll be with the same people all semester. Quizzes and the midterm are straightforward. Other assignments were generally graded pretty leniently. Put in effort and you'll be fine
Great professor and person, cares about students and is always open for conversation on any number of topics.

absolutely the best professor at uf! Dr. Strong is brilliant, funny, interesting, and accommodating. She always gives great feedback and I have learned an immeasurable amount from her and her classes. do not miss the opportunity to learn from her!!!

I liked the class, but Dr. Strong was sarcastic and sometimes arrogant. She was especially picky on quizzes (class averages were always around 60%). DOES NOT GIVE ENOUGH TIME ON QUIZZES/TESTS. This was the biggest complaint students had the entire semester!! She only read the powerpoints for lecture and wasn't very consistent with extra credit.

Lectures start 5–15 mins late, often rambles and repeats- sometimes helpful, but often confusing. Smokin Notes was essential to keep material clear. I hate this prof. He repeats himself in lecture SO much it makes u feel like u are going insane. He always runs out of time bc he shows up 5-10 minutes late. Do not take this class. She grades super late and you don't know your grade up until the middle of the semester. She is not lenient at all and doesn't tell you what you did wrong. You can only contact her throughh Canvas and even then, she takes a while to respond. I had an A+ the last week, and she gave me a C on the final with no feedback or help

She didn't grade anything for a month, then gave very bare feedback for each submission and then took off 20% of my final paper just saying it wasn't specific enough. Don't take with her if you can help it. Material was fine otherwise, really just her.r

analysis.name: Sean Adams
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

review_highlights.comment: This is not the easiest class, but it's one of those where you look back and are glad you took it. Adams was very helpful and passionate about history. He really pushes you on the writing component, but this helps prepare you tremendously for other classes you take down the road. A lot of reading (up to 100 pages/week) but I'd take this class again

I had Dr. Adams three years in a row and took four classes with him. I can't recommend him enough. The lectures are engaging, his grading is clear and helpful, and overall a super understanding guy. He gives feedback on all papers, of which there are usually 3 major ones and several mini ones. The class grade is mostly those, and attendance.

Adams has good knowledge about the subject and uses it to make the lectures interesting. He gave quizzes that were easy if you just paid attention in class. I know he and someone else were grading assignments, and most of the time, there was good feedback.

Dr. Adams is awesome. Extremely interesting class with amazing lectures. 5 ~500-750 word short responses with 2 drops and 3 ~2000 word essays. There isn't enough room to say everything but Dr. Adams is extremely understanding and always fair. He even stayed 10-15 minutes extra after every class to talk to students and answer questions.

LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! Super informative and engaging lectures (don't skip the class!!) and gives great feedback on essays. Not a super harsh grader, but pushes you to do your best and expects you to use the feedback he's given on your next essay. Is incredibly fair and holds himself to same standard of deadlines and professionalism. 100% recommend!

Easy class? Not anymore. You have to read a lot of pages and watch a lot of videos. Just took my first exam and it was really nit picky. I watched and read everything but ended up getting a D on my first exam. Memorize details and scientific terms.

As I am getting close to completing her course, I came to the conclusion:  1. Lecture videos are painful to watch. 2. Quizzes cover modules from the textbook almost every time 3. Exams are tricky, and sometimes seem that were written by someone who wants the student to fail. Mostly, they are not based on her textbook, rather on a mix of books.

This class was definitely an easy class with about half of your grade depending on homeworks such as quizzes and coding assignments. The professor gives amazing lectures and also streams them. This class also has a group project which was very fun to work on.

analysis.name: Agnes Leslie

Cannot recommend Dr. Leslie enough, seriously the most interesting class and her lectures are wonderful. She is an absolute wonder to have as a professor, and super accessible if you have questions. If you are thinking about taking her, please do!

If you respect your time do not take this class because Dr. Leslie will not. Readings can exceed 150 pages a week and then won't even be referenced during the long droning lectures but will feature on exams. I absolutely loved Dr. Leslie. She is so passionate about her class, always smiling, and has a positive attitude. She does a lot of class discussions and assigns readings, but they are really interesting if you pay attention. You get out what you put into this class. Easy A, but I learned a ton.

analysis.name: Pasha Agoes

In-class Canvas quizzes every 1-2 weeks, discussion post, some writing assignments, in class paper midterm exam, and a group final project. The midterm is mainly from the textbook. I would 10/10 take a course with Dr. Agoes again. He is such an easy grader and really makes it difficult to fail his class. He is very strict on deadlines though, so just make sure you have your work in on time and don't ask for any extensions and you should be good to go.

Dr. Agoes is one of the best profs I have had at UF. He cares about the success of his students and is extremely accessible for help. Extremely understanding! Clear syllabus and grading structure. Grades fair and quick. 10/10 would take another class with Dr. Agoes. Really remarkable as a professor.

analysis.name: Aghane Antunes

Great Professor, don't have one negative thing to say about her. Very accessible outside of class and very understanding when I missed an assignment (still got full points). Very simple ppt group project. Discussion post and quiz once a week. Short papers about once a month. Whole class was organized well and assignments were well outlined.

I took this class since I needed 6,000 word credit class. However, I found that the # of words we had to write was WAY more than 6,000. We had large projects (1,000+ word essays, presentations, etc) and discussions due each Monday. They were relatively easy/she is not a tough grader, but I would not recommend to anyone just looking for word credit.

analysis.name: Pauline Aguinalde
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Loved the professor and class. There is a lot of material, but the exams are straightforward, and she gives extra credit opportunities. Super interesting topics, and she is very passionate about what she teaches. I would 100% take this class again

Such a nice professor who genuinely cares about her students. The class is content-heavy but so manageable. Minimal homework besides studying for exams which are straightforward. Would definitely recommend this class and professor

Great professor. Extra credit opportunities for tests, in class test review, no final exam (final project that is broken down throughout the semester). You can tell she is passionate about teaching and loves the subject. Easy A class.
I would highly recommend this professor. The class itself is content heavy so it is fast-paced but absolutely manageable. Interesting topics and exams are very straightforward.

analysis.name: Shubhi Agarwal
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I attended every lecture in the beginning and could barely understand her.  Additionally, she treated us like high schoolers and would call us out for being on our phones/talking.  Mid semester, I stopped attending class because I quite honestly found it pointless.  I got the same score on my second exam as I did on the first, proving my point.

Professor Agarwal genuinely care about the success of her students, and want them to learn as much as possible in her class. However, her lectures are very confusing and it is periodically difficult to understand her. I feel like she over-complicates an already complicated subject. She is very accommodating in grading as she curves the grades.

She knows what she is talking about and delivers the material in a concise and targeted way that makes it extremely digestible. Never read the textbook, just participated in class. Her problem sets are not difficult at all and she is also a very lenient grader and wants her students to succeed. I would take her class again!

Professor Agarwal is a very nice lady and is super passionate about economics, but she is a terrible teacher. I attended every single lecture in fear of getting behind and 90% of the time I had no idea what she was talking about ever. She goes way too fast so it's incredibly difficult to take organized notes or understand anything.

There's nothing necessarily wrong with Professor Agarwal, but I won't take her classes ever again. Her lectures were boring and hard to understand, so I stopped attending at some point and just read the textbooks. Now don't get me wrong, she is a nice person. If you go to her office hours, she will try to be as helpful as she can.

analysis.name: Tolulope Agunbiade
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: To the person that said "they're not ready for a UF education if they complain about Dr. A", I have a 3.8 GPA. But pop off I guess? Dr. A isn't TERRIBLE. She's just disorganized and sometimes goes back on what the syllabus says in terms of exams and quizzes. It's an annoyingly tedious class.

This class is very unorganized. You have a quiz each week that you only get 5 minutes to answer 5 questions and these quizzes dont follow the syllabus. The term paper is graded on two different rubrics we got little guidance on. There have been many times where the modules werent uploaded in time. This class is stressful.

HORRIBLE, AVOID. She litreally does not have an idea of how to respond to emails for feedback. She first said I will respond to emails asking for feedback, then later sends an even vaguer email to the entire class which confused more than it helped. Her TAs are useless, take off points for no good reason, INCOMPETENT!!!

Dr. Agunbiade is very friendly and the TA, Nicholas Martin, is awesome. There are academic review papers that need to be read and write a reflection every week. You also need to work as a group to study one chosen disease over the semester as in many projects. It was an interesting class and not as hard as I thought. It's a good Quest 2 class.

There are exams and weekly quizzes. The class is a decent amount of work so be prepared to put in a few hours. Dr. A is a nice person, but her class is unorganized. However, she is willing to work with students and hear you out.

analysis.name: Aaron King
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There are 4 assignments that all added up to 100 pts, so missing one pt was like missing one pt in your final grade. Please schedule a meeting. It's the only way you'll get a thorough examination of your questions and advice for your research papers. He is willing to help and communicate. Turned in an assignment late and still got full pts.

Professor King isn't the best at communicating. Your grade is determined by 2 papers in the summer term and instructions seemed very confusing and refused to answer any emails about clarifications. Office hours are the only way to reach him and get feedback on work, if not he takes forever to grade. Doable but lots of writing and research needed.

Takes forever to grade and doesn't give feedback, so it's impossible to really know if you're doing anything right. Final paper was a 4,000 word "literature review" with hardly any instructions and midterm wasn't even graded by the time the final was due. Doesn't communicate with students at all, so can't really ask questions or anything either.

2000 and 4000 word paper make up the entire grade. King is a slow grader, hasn't even graded the mid term due 2+ weeks ago. Instructions and tedious and laborious (have to make your own graphs), won't respond to emails. Writing these papers is torture when you have no feedback. I'd stay away from taking this Summer session.

Professor King is very understanding and kind to his students. However, I have no idea what I am doing in this class. I feel like I have no guidance or advice on how to write the papers, which are the only things that make up your grade. I would avoid taking this class, especially during summer terms.

analysis.name: Aaron Karlson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This professor will not grade anything until the very very last day of the semester. Be mindful of this when taking one of his classes.

The work is steady until the last 5 weeks, then it leaps in difficulty. He will take the time to do office hours but he constantly says go back and watch the lecture even when you explain you didn't understand the lecture.

Mr. Karlson's first concern is the success of his students; he responds to questions promptly and with detail, no matter how trivial the question may seem at times. He also encourages students to review material on their own to improve their skill with Maya, which is incredibly helpful. He cares deeply about his students and is an amazing professor

Professor Karlson is amazing! The level of difficulty of this class is high, but its not about him, its just the learning curve of Maya is pretty steep... make sure you attend the lectures and start your assignments ahead; animation takes time. He will answer questions super fast and gives great feedback... Again, start your homework on TIME

Professor Karlson's class was a joy to attend every time! 3D Animation was super fun, and he made the lectures hilarious and a great time to be in. The class itself was hard, but that comes with learning Maya and animation, if you've never done it before. He was super caring and was good at feedback, so don't be afraid to reach out to him!

analysis.name: Ron Chandler
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Chadler is an absolute gem! He is knowledgeable, cares for his students, and is always available for a chat. The class is super easy; there is no homework (everything is done in class), no quizzes, tests, or a final exam (instead, one really meaningful gratitude assignment at the end). Attendance is 50%, though, so don't miss class. Take it!!

Easiest psych class I have taken. The material was very inspirational and easy to understand. Very easy A, and almost everyone ends up with over a 100% in the class due to extra credit at the end. Weekly work is very easy, and you barely have to think about the class outside of lecture. Group work and one scary presentation, but very easy. Take it!

One of the nicest and most caring professors I have ever met. Takes time to get to know every student beyond the classroom and class is very interesting and fun. The TA I had was also fantastic and so sweet. Ending with a 104%, everyone should take this class if they can. The fact Chandler doesn't have a 5/5 is shocking.

Positive psych: don't get the textbook.  This is the easiest class you'll ever take.  I found the whole thing depressing, which I know is ironic.  The whole premise of the class is how to find the meaning of life in a worldview that rejects meaning.  Take the class, it's easy, but be prepared to do no critical thinking at all otherwise you'll hurt.

I enjoyed Professor Chandler. The class was an easy A and he cared about the success of his students. However, the lectures were short and often taught by his TAs. Everything was graded by the TAs too. Its a good class; nothing hard at all, but you hear more from undergrads than from the professor. No exams, just simple individual and group papers.

analysis.name: Aaron Hill
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I would not recommend Professor Hill. While the material itself is not hard, we are graded on things such as "professionalism". I had a situation where I couldn't get in touch with any members of my Capsim team. He claimed that teammates not participating was part of the real world and deducted a full point off of my grade for reaching out to him.

This class is way harder than it should be. Lots of exam questions come from the minutiae of the expensive and very boring textbook. Very much a cookie cutter McGraw Hill class with lecture videos that are delivered robotically. Capsim group assignment was pretty good, however, I still would not recommend this class. Overall not worth the effort.

Disclaimer: I had technical issues for the first month of the semester, and it was hard for me to catch up on all my classes. That is why I gave it an average difficulty. The professor sends very thorough, helpful, and detailed weekly emails with reminders. You can tell he really cares about his students, and is a fair grader.

I found his class very straightforward, and he teaches many of the essential business concepts you may already know. There is a weekly lecture, smartbook, quiz, and group Capsim assignment (which is much harder than intl. business Capsim). There are many drops and grading procedures in your favor. I wish he had more practice material for exams.
Great and easy professor! Simple 3 online exams of 20 questions, 3 case studies, and a simulation. Can get away with dedicating only 40min a week to this class and get an A

analysis.name: Ron Gromoll
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Gromoll has a lot of experience in the hospitality industry and was able to share these stories in each module in a way that related to the material at hand. The big project was a three part group project. I was able to acquire a Hospitality industry certification while going through this class, because he provided the needed materials.

Professor Gromoll was a great professor! The grading criteria was very clear and he graded assignments in a timely manner with constructive feedback. The class mainly consists of 500 word papers on the lectures given throughout the semester and assignments pertaining to career prep such as resume building and interview practice through Quinncia.

I was very anxious going into this semester and I'm ending the semester more confident, better prepared, and very excited for my future. While I didn't end up going the internship route, Prof. Ron's class was so worthwhile. The lecturers he brought in were amazing and it's not often you get a professor with so much job experience.

Professor Ron Gromoll- HANDS DOWN- the best hospitality professor at UF. I took him for LEI3360, LEI3992, and LEI4940. He gave amazing lectures and was so inspiring. He wants to see his students succeed. I recommend following him on LinkedIn, as he kept in touch with me right before his retirement and my upcoming graduation.
Ron is great and super helpful as you work to launch a career in hospitality. Make sure you will be able to make it to the designated class time as attendance heavily contributes to your grade.

analysis.name: Aaron Molstad
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Homework was fairly challenging, but about expected time consumption for a math class. Molstad cares and will help in OH and his lectures are alright. The practice exams are easier than the real exams, but the real exams were not god awful (still hard), but he curves and provides some extra credit. From this you can intuit that he is a solid choice

Teaches material well and is very helpful in OH. Some HWs are lengthy and midterm/final were 5-7 day take-home exams (it will take most of that time to do) but everything is fair. STA3032 was my only prereq which made some topics harder but its definitely doable with enough effort and I learned way more in this class than in eng stats.

Homework load not huge. Lectures very full of mediocre-ly explained material. Homework problems are difficult but manageable. Gives a practice exam that is similar, if not easier. Then exams are extremely difficult and different from homeworks and practice exam. I pay attention, do homework, take notes, study, and do awful on exams.

I struggled a lot with this class but Prof. Molstad was very helpful for clarifying material. Exams make up 70% of your grade but he does curve. Exams were difficult and were somewhat proof heavy which differed from the computational practice exams. Make sure you do all the homeworks and get the highest grades possible.

Dr. Molstad does his best to teach you the concepts and make sure you understand everything as you progress through his classes. I thoroughly enjoyed STA4504 and I would absolutely recommend taking it with him if you get the chance.

analysis.name: Jessica Aaron
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: The semester isn't even over and I have a lot of words to say about this. The class itself is poorly organized and most people complain that they don't ever know whats going on. Her slides are often incorrect and you end up teaching yourself from the textbook. It feels like you set yourself up for failure by taking this class.

She is a very nice teacher, and does try to help. However, if you ask something in class that she doesnt know, it becomes irrelevant. She couldnt teach certain concepts and you needed to rely on the book as your teacher. I was disappointed because I expected to learn more, she used anothers materials that she didnt always agree with, very confusing

I'm minoring in Spanish and have never made below an A in a Spanish class, but I'm all but confirmed to make a B in this class. The information she provides is inconsistent, and my friend and I spent the whole semester teaching each other the info since Aaron didn't do it. Super frustrating professor for what should've been an interesting class.

Jessica Aaron is one of my all time favorite teachers! She is extremely knowledgable and is always looking for ways to make her class fun, interesting, and informative. However, she gives ALOT of reading, so DO NOT take her classes if you know you will NOT TAKE THE TIME TO READ.

Had her for "Spanish in the US". Easy class, nice but lectures can be very long and boring at times, easy group work sometimes in class. 8 homeworks were on Canvas, open-note and everything. Course has a three part project worth 50% of the grade with a presentation at the end of the semester - not bad though. Recommend if looking for light work.

analysis.name: Aaron Ellrich
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: This class is reading and lecture intensive. There are weekly discussion posts and 6 writing assignments, in addition to a final project. It's not difficult; you just have to be prepared to put in the time to read all the materials and put it all together. Overall, I enjoyed this class and have learned to understand things from other perspectives.

The correct course of his that I'm currently taking is actually ANT3451. The previous reviews are misleading and I wish I never took this class because of how horrible this professor is. His grading is extremely subjective and very harsh. I have a 94% so I'm not writing this out of spite, but just to warn prospective students to use discretion.

He definitely seems to enjoy what he teaches. For the assignments, at least for Fall 2020 online mode, you had to read the textbook in addition to the lectures to be able to really understand what was happening, so prepare to read a lot. The discussion posts and assignments were very doable but again require you to read.

Definitely a somewhat challenging course. The labs are incredibly long and mundane, probably the most difficult part of the class. You 100% have to study hard for the practicals and exams. The exams aren't difficult, but if you don't study you definitely won't do well. It's also very lecture heavy each week.

analysis.name: Joslyn Ahlgren
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great lecturer, but make sure you go to class because you'll miss so much if you don't. The only negative thing I will say is that her exams are pretty tough, but they're very low stakes (8% each) so you will be fine if you perform poor on one. An A is definitely achievable, I managed a B+ while being sick for 3 weeks and missing tons of lectures.

Professor Ahlgren is an amazing professor. She is extremely well-spoken and knows the material extremely well. She is not the type to rely on slides and explains things very throughly. She is always open to answering questions and her office hours are extremely helpful.

Great lectures, organized and high quality, with a knowledgeable instructor. However, the workload is intense (21+ hrs/week), making it stressful, especially without an anatomy background. Many worry about AI/Honorlock. I would NOT take this class again. I've gotten A's in my past courses and this is my first C. This course will lower your GPA.

Doc A is so paranoid about cheating that it negatively affected my learning experience. I've looked things up from class using other reliable anatomical resources to find them not to exist or be contradictory. I appreciate being graded on effort for assignments. But some of her questions do not align with what we are being taught.

Great lectures, organized, engaging, and high quality, with a knowledgeable instructor. However, the workload is intense (21+ hrs/week), making it stressful, especially without an anatomy background. Many worry about AI/Honorlock. I would NOT take it again I got a C when I usually get A's in my previous courses.

analysis.name: Angelica Ahrens
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ahrens made sure to always keep in contact with her students. In an online program, this is crucial. However, she also was there for hands-on help and primarily required you to interact with your podmates. She fostered a very welcome and advantageous environment for students. I took this course in the summer and would not recommend it enough!

Dr. Ahrens is the best professor I have had in my graduate time at UF thus far!!! The class has 2 major projects and open book quizzes (3 attempts, highest kept), and a few purusall assignments in-between. She is extremely knowledgeable about the subject, extremely nice to talk to and provides excellent feedback. Put in effort = A! I got a 98!

Very easy class, a lot of busy work, spent 1-3 hours a week on this class. 2 major projects and only 1 was tedious but u have a lot of time to do it. no exams, lowest quiz dropped, everything open note and unproctored. uses a groupme and is very understanding. i submitted a project late due to sickness and she did not penalize me and reached out

Wonderful professor! Long lectures but no exams. Capstone presentation (25 min) and a Ted talk (5 min). Handful of open note quizzes (lowest dropped). Put in the work and you'll get an A. The people who rated her poor got a low grade because they didn't try. She's a wonderful professor!

Dr. Ahrens, was excellent. Now, I will say there were multiple projects, but I loved that the discussions were on a different platform. I loved that this was not a test-heavy course and more aligned with other master's courses than some extremely test-heavy ones. I loved this class. I will say she is slow to respond but always responds.

analysis.name: Jaime Ahlberg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Would not recommend for Quest 1. Entire class was graded on one project and 4 papers. Papers had little to no instruction and if you asked Dr. Ahlberg or the TA for clarification they would say “it depends.” Papers were also graded harshly and feedback was vague and  3 unexcused absences for the semester.

Dr. Ahlberg was extremely easy to understand, especially considering this was my first philosophy class. The readings were extremely interesting and her insight on what we had read connected all the dots, but also if you miss a reading its not a big deal at all. Do NOT be intimidated by this class, it was the perfect introduction to philosophy.

Assigns TONS of reading, and if you're interested in feminism, be careful--this is very much a philosophy class, and she wants her papers written that way without really describing how to. She was very nice, though the lectures could be kind of drab.

If u don't like reading/writing, don't take it. All assignments & exams are written. The TA grades all the work, I had Jim & he was cool. Lectures are required if you have to turn in a paper or don't understand the reading but missing a class overall isn't a big deal. Great lecturer & loves to call people out when their arguments don't make sense.

For a Quest 1 course that is mainly for freshmen to take, she expects more than just introductory college level writing, more like philosophy major level writing. She can be pretty vague in terms of expectations and criteria for papers. Very nice person and was very understanding for COVID. Also great lecturer. Just wished she graded better.

analysis.name: Soohyoun Ahn
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 102 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Remember when learning used to be fun? Dr. Ahn actually makes it fun again. Can't believe I'm saying this, but I actually enjoyed doing the assignments in this class. Super engaging and easy to follow. Definitely recommend it for bio credit, international credit, or just a chill elective.

There is genuinely so much extra credit and opportunities to get an A in this course that you frankly need to be doing nothing to not. It can be a little tedious at times, but it is extremely easy -- and the many assignments can be done in 1-2 hrs.

Professor Ahn was super nice, took this course for credits and gpa boost, and it was super easy. Lectures are on PlayPosit and are super easy. The quizzes are easy, too. No exam, just some discussions and a digital project. I passed with an A, and I'm someone who gets distracted easily.

Super chill class; lectures are split into short videos; weekly quizzes are Honorlocked, but allowed to have a page of notes; 3 major assignments, but none take more than a day; most people end with over an 100 with all the extra credit there is

Man's Food was absolutely amazing online. General class about food- nutrition, food art, flavors, food groups etc. Each week: 10 min lecture, open note quiz, no exams, and one assignment (ex: eat at a restaurant and document the experience, make food art, make a personalized diet plan.) Final exam was a digital scrapbook.

analysis.name: Aida Hozic
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Waste of time. The readings and lectures are awful she rambles and treats everything as profound. She's an inconsistent grader taking points off for not being emotional enough or not saying exactly what she wants, even when it's not in the prompt. She claims not to care about AI but gives 0 based on suspicion alone and won't let you explain.

Professor Hozic is a nice lady. She seems to care about her students and really wants them to be satisfied as well as better off after the class. My biggest issue with her is that she can be quite snarky with feedback. She doesn't use rubrics and can be rather mean if you don't write with complexity or don't do the readings "justice" on quizzes.

-Harsh grader no rubric.
- Quizzes on content to be discussed in coming week make lectures feel unnecessary or unimportant to pay attention to.
- In lectures tends to ramble.
- attending office hours is basically mandatory if you want to succeed in this course- she will hate you if you don't and grade even harsher.

Overall a very caring and knowledgeable prof. Is a nuanced grader but always gave good feedback. Assignment explanations can feel vague at start but expectations are consistent. Readings were assessed before lecture started for the week, sometimes made lecture feel redundant even though attendance was required. Warm and accessible.

Professor Hozic is one of the best professors in the Poli Sci Department and made my time as a Poli Sci major much more enjoyable. She knows a ton about pretty much any subject and has a great wit, both making her classes very interesting, no matter the subject at hand. I had her for Divided Cities and Politics of the World Economy. Take a class.

analysis.name: Theodosios Aivalis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Don't listen to the other comments please!! He actually really cares for his students that he teaches. I had him for multiple calc lectures from calc 1-3. And is super friendly, funny, and helps you understand in a very good way if you don't seem to understand the topic. I would 100% take him again for any single class he teaches.
If you don't like him it's more like a you problem, because he's really cool and nice.
Doesn't seem like he really cares about teaching.

analysis.name: Aishwarya  Shankar
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: LAA2379C- I have never learned so much in so little time, truly an amazing professor. The work is long and sometimes difficult but worth it. If you put in the time and respond to feedback, you will succeed. Professor is also incredibly kind.

Professor is unreachable. Had a situation where my  grade was docked heavily because of something my partner did and I would've received an A otherwise, but the teacher literally never responded back. Ever. Class is structured so bad and uninteresting, so work felt so heavy. Professor didn't start grading until like 2 days before class was over...

I was excited to take the class at first, but I'm so disappointed I got this professor again. The only thing I found "enjoyable" was writing childhood narratives since we didn't have to research. There's actually an insane amount of content she wants you to watch/read, and it makes it so uninteresting. It's easy to get an A but omg it's draining.

Dude the semester ends in one week and she has not graded a single thing. Our entire grade is pretty much one project that we add onto every week yet she has not graded a single submission. How do I know how I am doing if I get no instructor feedback?

analysis.name: Katerina Aifantis
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Got a bad grade but I honestly credit her course structure for my grade not being worse. Her recorded lectures were engaging and understandable. Exams and HW weren't graded too harshly. The kindest and most encouraging professor I have ever had at UF.
very nice professor! she used examples to make things clearer and prepared us well for exams. was accommodating to unforseen difficulties of students. definitely recommend to take classes with her!

Professor Aifantis is a great professor. Currently taking EML 4930 with her, which I highly recommend for a specialization elective. She prepares you very well for exams and gives a fairly light amount of homework (7 assignments for the semester, 2-5 hours each). She radiates kindness and is always willing to help, plus she rewards participation

The best professor I have had at UF. She is unbelievably caring and accessible outside of class time. She will even check your homework before you submit it so you can get a 100% every time. Her exams are fair and her lectures are great. I had a great experience in this class, and I hope to have her again. Highly recommend.

Prof Aifantis is great. Her class is interesting because she briefly focuses on the most relevant topics and then goes through a lot of examples. Exams are similar to homework and shes always available to answer questions by email. Would definitely take again!

analysis.name: Aicha Ouzia
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She deducts points without explaining why or what was wrong. I emailed her asking what the correct answer was on a past test and attached a picture of the question and she told me she was busy and could not look up the answer. This was after she told us to email her with questions.

Rude, mean, and disrespectful. She will laugh in your face and tell you how terrible and awful you are doing. She gives absolutely no motivation. She actually discourages me from learning. I am not being hyperbolic. It is a pain speaking with our. My day gets worse crossing per path. She should not be a teacher. Do not take this course!

Does not give feedback/corrections when grading. She is just using pre-made assignments from when another prof was teaching this course. She does not grade quickly and responds to emails slowly or not at all. When you ask questions about criteria she often gives unclear non-answers. Just don't bother.

She's awful at explaining the material. I'm taking the class online and even though she answers e-mails, she never actually helps you with the question you have. She makes it seem like explaining things is a hassle to her and she's busy to read attachments. She never provides written feedback or comments explaining why you got the grade you got.

There is little attempt to describe how the language operates and she will simply speak it as if you're already supposed to know. She'll get angry and stomp her feet if you phrase your sentences incorrectly or are hesitant to speak in class. There are many assignments due every day online and she won't care if you have technical difficulties.

analysis.name: AJ Jung
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER!! Throughout my time in grad school this is the hardest grader i've had for no reason. Its frustrating because her grading is based off of opinions, so you have to guess what she will like. When I went to office hours she had little feedback and then ended up taking off many points for "potential changes."

Wow where do I begin, maybe avoid at all costs, maybe she shouldn't be teching this class when she isn't the best speaker.  She gives no guidance on grading and then tears you apart in the rubric. analysis.name: Akhil Kshirsagar

Getting 100 on every assignment without any study and effort. Just 5 min pre-recorded lecture per week, then write short essay and discussion. Final exam is somewhat unreasonable, bc he did not teach, but he curved it. All people I know in this course getting an A.

Terrible professor! He ignores students emails when asked about grading! Even when he is clearly wrong! For example, he gave me 0 marks for a criteria that states "Include reference section in APA format", which I did! Overall, terrible professor, and I would absolutely not recommend!

I don't know why this professor has a low rating... I got a ~100% on every assignment he manually graded. Only problem with the class were the quizzes, they're pretty much impossible to do good on, but they are only worth 10% of your grade, so it isn't the biggest deal.

analysis.name: Francis Akanbi

One of the greatest professors i've had at UF by far! Professor Akanbi takes students opinions and feelings into consideration and always does his best to make sure we are doing okay with the material being learned. He is great at teaching and made it seem like a 3 hr class went by quick! Very engaging conversations as well. 10/10 would take  again

Professor Akanbi is an angel. He is by far the nicest and most caring teacher at the CJC. I would recommend that you take this professor if you ever get the chance. He cares about the welfare of his students. Professor Akanbi understands that being a student with other course loads is difficult and he works with you to make sure you succeed.

Definitely one of my favorite professors at UF. If you are taking this class, definitely take it with Francis, you will not regret it. He is so kind and does everything in his power to make sure each of his students succeed.
Prof. Akanbi is an amazing professor. He cares greatly about his students and wants you to learn and grow while taking his course. He is caring, kind and compassionate and is always in a good mood!

analysis.name: Akintunde Akinyemi

review_highlights.comment: easy class, he likes people who pay attention and contribute in class. If you show interest and read some of the materials he gives and talk about them in class you are on your way to an A!!!!

He is a great teacher. Go to class, participate, read the books, do your best on tests. He is extremely understanding. If you mess up a couple times, just tell him the truth and he'll work with you. Awesome Teacher!!
Very easy class. He likes respectful people and people who show interest in his materials. Participate a lot in class and you will be on your way to an A

African Oral Literature sounds boring but he makes it pretty fun. It's a lot of story time and learning about Nigerian culture. Show some effort or interest and you'll get a good grade. Super nice guy. He's also got a really cool African accent which makes listening more interesting.

analysis.name: Nilufer Akalin

review_highlights.comment: The class is interesting and very easy to get an A. You can definitely do really well on exams without reading every single article. Just skim them and you'll get the gist.

Professor Akalin was so passionate and knowledgable about the course material. Many skipped class due to attendance not being mandatory, but those who went formed a great relationship with her. The coursework consisted of minimal assignments that were graded very easy. Don't stress about the exams, there was no final, and extra credit is offered.

I enjoyed Dr. Akalin's class a lot. I found the subject material really interesting. The reading reflections were difficult at times and the class was really lecture heavy/ based on outside readings. I didn't enjoy that participation was mandatory, but she made the class really accessible which I appreciated.

Professor nilufer was so approachable and very kind- you could tell she was passionate about the material. For WST2322, you're graded by few things but the assignments and even tests are very easy. Just show up to class and you should be able to make an easy A
This was a great class with a great professor!

Horrible. Way too hard for an intro class and way too much information for the cumulative final. grades are determined by finals and midterms which are unbelievably hard and can be any detail on the 11 chapters of the core text, 13 cases of countries, or 20 academic journals which serve no purpose. Please take this class with a different teacher.

Just don't take this class if you're a political science major, do the other 3 core classes. Ridiculous amount of material pulled from 3 textbooks, exams worth so much of your grade, 94 for an A and she doesn't round. The content is somewhat interesting but there's no room for fumbling.

Professor Kreppel is extremely knowledgable on the course content. Your grade is determined by two midterm exams, a final exam, and 11 short/easy quizzes. 300+ pages of reading per week, but it is doable as long as you spread it out and know what is important to read (which Kreppel makes clear). Weekly quizzes, writing, and discussion are not hard at all but take some time. Once you get in the groove of completing these assignments the class is a breeze.

I enjoyed the professor. She was very caring, very thoughtful, always responded to her emails, and was truly a joy to learn from. Her curriculum was very easy, and the only slightly difficult thing was just keeping track of the assignments. Other than that, loved the class and it was SO Easy!

Grading is meticulous to a fault — expect points off for things like superscript vs subscript. Quizzes often focus on oddly specific details that feel more like trivia than meaningful learning. :(((((

An easy class to fill your writing requirement. Never interacted with the professor. Just watch all the content (skip the introduction) and turn things in following the rubric. Lots of repeated material in each module. Assigned a discussion, a quiz, two 200-250 word writing prompts each week, and peer grading. Very easy A.
The work is mostly graded by the TAs and will take time to receive good feedback, but as long as you follow the rubric and answer the prompts, you should be getting A's on most assignments.

analysis.name: Amobichukwu Amanambu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: I appreciate the effort put into the lectures. However, they sometimes move off topic, and the added jokes can make it hard to stay focused. In this class, you can tune out the lecture, do the bare minimum on the homework, and still get over a 100% on the tests. He gives lots of opportunities for extra credit and to turn things in late, and the final exam for this class was an attendance grade. Just show up and you should be fine!

His grading criteria is very simple but the only negative about him is that he is very disorganized so there are a lot of back and forth emails for clarification.

The class is self taught but if you have any questions he usually answers very fast. There aren't many assignments but he grades fairly light. The group project was the most fun part about the class and you get a chance to interact with your classmates. Would recommend if you need a filler class or are interested in geography.

Overall, he was a really nice guy. He can grade harsh sometimes, but this happens very infrequently. I would definitely take a class of his again. The course itself just had a good amount of busy work. It doesn't take up too much time though. For a 1 credit course though, it can feel more like a 2 credit course.

She's a new, amazing geo prof! This class is just difficult but she does exam guides & office hours. Pray you get decent TAs bc they grade labs (one TA this year was awful). This professor is always unclear about what she wants on assignments, but then takes points off for things she didn't previously state she wanted. Her assignments are vague, and her grading feedback is rude. I usually enjoy advertising classes, but her class is the exception.

Instructions for assignments can be very unclear or short and then points are taken off for things she wanted you to mention but failed to make it known that this was a requirement. Can be quite rude in her grading which could be justified if she gave better instructions but this is not the case. Made me dread every single assignment.

Best prof in the computer science department. Very clear on theory, great visualizations to help you follow along. Incredibly well prepared, organized class structure. Gamified lecture quizzes for extra credit. Responsive to questions. Open to feedback. Developed an arguably better version of leetcode for students. Actually the GOAT.

The Exams are structured and weighted in odd ways, with a lot of writing in a short amount of time. Lectures tend to derail into nothing as others have said

pls dont take this class. Lectures r so disorganized and exams are so lengthy. Your only grades are 3 pop quizzes and 3 exams.If you HAVE to take this class, make sure you have a good TA. This will ensure you have a good grade. I heard Kim is a good TA and the 2 female TAs are great too.

analysis.name: Arunava Banerjee
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Math (in all its forms) has never tasted so good. Few have Prof. Arunava Banerjee's ability to present the hardest material in the easiest form just so that we have a clear picture and understanding of what is going on.

Here's how you judge whether you should take a graduate class or not :- Uses black board  Knows how to teach and cares if you are learning. (ADD) Uses presentation slides  Lazy and needs to finish the syllabus quickly,you would learn better by reading the textbook yourself. (DROP)
You may not find a teacher with his capability of rephrasing concepts again and again just so that you understand. (Do you want to waste your time taking classes under anybody else? I wouldn't. )

It is challenging to condense years of research into an hour's worth of lectures. However, Prof. Arunava does a great job. The use of the blackboard instead of slides, his ability to pictorially represent mathematical concepts, his check questions to highlight the main concept are some of the best teaching methods I have come across. Sit and Enjoy!

Gather around, for the story starts where we are taken on a journey through the efforts of entities before us, at understanding the most complex organ. Don't forget to get your math, compSc, biology lenses as you will need to see through them, a lot (You have other lenses too?, bring them!). Listen and think carefully, with a great teacher.

Dr. Arce is a great professor! He truly cares about his students suceeding in this major!

Its only once a week and every week he brings in a different professor to talk about their research.  I found all of the lectures really interesting. I 11/10 recommend Asmaa to anyone that plans on taking a literature class at UF.  She is such an inspiration to me that I am going to dress up as her for halloween.  The class is LIT!!!!

Asmaa is by far my favorite TA I've ever had at UF. She is super relatable to the students. She's very approachable, & feels like another one of the students, but is also very knowledgeable.

My absolute favorite TA ever. Definitely made my first semester at UF feel a lot more like home and got rid of the "no one cares about you in college" stigma. She genuinely cares, is hilarious, and will sit and guide you through absolutely anything. Definitely take her if you can, for anything!
