review_highlights.comment: This course was an actual roller coaster. The first couple weeks were brutal, and the material being taught was way beyond the scope of the curriculum. Everyone failed the first quiz, but everything went uphill from there. Tons of extra credit (and Im not exaggerating). You could fail all the exams and still end up with an A.

HE IS AMAZING. HE REALLY WANTED HIS STUDENTS TO SUCCEED. He had no idea what he was doing in the bebgining of the semester (he was teaching discrete math type material that wasnt even related), but the students helped shape him in to a decent lecturer. Tons of extra credit.
Legendary. Dude's way nicer to students than he needs to be

Goes deep into statistics,gives a good amount of homework but the tests are based on them, and is very caring towards his students. Truly passionate in his profession and only wants to share that passion with his students. Book not required, 7 biweekly quizzes, 3 exams.

DON'T TAKE! This teacher was unreachable. If he did respond, it was to direct you to the TAs (who were no help either) or passive-aggressively ask you "Why do you need this?", refusing to answer your question on the material. He drops 3 quiz grades which is nice, but there has been absolutely NO EXTRA CREDIT and most of the students are failing.

analysis.name: Glen Billesbach
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is an amazing professor. He truly understands students, and is a great lecturer, even though it could be heavy on some days. It's a required class for Sustainability Majors, and I really enjoyed it.

Professor Glen succeeded in making what should have been a manageable course unnecessarily difficult and frustrating. Not only did lectures lack any coherency or structure, important concepts were too often explained in a confusing way or not at all. He also rarely gave assignment instructions that were complete.

I had Glen for the Fall 2023 semester for American Political Thought, and he was a very informative and kind professor who truly cared about the material he chose and the student's involvement in the course.

He's the best! If you're looking for a passionate professor with clear grading outlines, great office hours, and an overall happy demeanor: TAKE HIS CLASS. The texts are super interesting, not too difficult to understand, and he's super understanding if you have problems in class. Just listen in on the lectures and you'll do great on the essays.

Professor Billesbach is hands down one of the best university professors at UF! His lectures are fun, easy to understand, and he really tries to break down the content so each student understands the material. He encourages participation, lectures are great, and the readings are super interesting. Take this professor for any POT class at UF!

analysis.name: Binul Dulsara Gulawita Ganithage
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the most caring professors I've had. After doing poorly on the first exam, he helped me a lot and I was able to improve my grades significantly. The quizzes can be challenging and interesting but they're doable. I really enjoyed the class overall and don't agree with the negative review. I would definitely take this course again.

Although he is a really nice guy himself and he is lenient, you won't learn anything. He is really confusing and expects you to know the content without even teaching it. Whoever gave him a 5 is lying to you and praying on your downfall. Just don't take his class if you can avoid it.

The course itself can be dry but he is 110% productive in class going through problems. Course is graded on four exams each 15% of your grade. Another 25% are homework assignments and the rest 15% are random quizzes that include attendance.

analysis.name: Kevin Bird
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is an easy A, especially with Dr. Bird. I overslept and missed a quiz, and he let me take it later with no penalty. He is very considerate and tries his best to keep the class engaging. The weekly discussion posts are annoying but very easy. Dr. Bird is the most far-reaching, grassroots, and consequential professor at UF. iykyk.

Exams aren't hard but you need to study for them, essays aren't too bad either. Don't save the discussion readings for the last minute, some of them are long. Dr. Bird cares about what we need to learn from this country's history and why it's important; highly recommend giving this class the time of day, even if you only take it for gen ed credit!

I took his class as a senior engineering student and actually found the class to be interesting and not just a waste of time. I did feel slightly unprepared for exams due to the fact that he did not give us a guideline of what to study. There were too many questions about dates of events and also small facts that were mentioned once.

This professor has great lectures and very passionate about the subject matter. He doesn't require that you attend but has in-class practice quizzes on most lecture days to make sure that people come. The class is not test heavy, just a midterm and a final. Also, there are planned quizzes throughout the semester.
His class is super easy and he really cares about his students. He's really approachable and funny. He can be rather repetitive and the class has a lot of reading.

analysis.name: Yakubu Bitrus
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This theoretically should've been a very easy class, but the quizzes, speeches, and outlines made it somewhat difficult at times. Professor Bitrus is very nice and understanding, and his passion for public speaking made the class enjoyable. As long as you follow his instructions exactly and don't get super unlucky on the quizzes, you'll be fine.

If you're not religious, pick one and pray. Hes a villain, he'll take points off your speeches for things you didn't do, then when you ask for clarification he won't give it to you. You don't have to buy a textbook, but there's one provided and if you don't wanna fail his million quizzes then you need to read them. He has no idea how canvas works.

Prof. Bitrus was unorganized and the class wasn't well structured, but he is genuinely the nicest and cares about his students. I think this was his first semester teaching so maybe he will get better with Canvas in the future. Super easy A and almost zero homework. He is so chill with the speeches, I basically put in zero effort and did just fine.

Professor Bitrus cares about his subject and wants students to succeed. The course structure was a challenge. Assignments are not difficult, but there was always poor communication about due dates. Additionally, Canvas was not set up in a way to easily understand and also lacked due dates. I learned a lot from the course but beware of organization.

I gained nothing from this course. Professor Bitrus was very unorganized (constantly changing due dates, not updating the canvas, etc) and often put in the wrong grades for me (which I had to request him to fix literally 6 times until he did). The class is a stupidly easy A, but it might test your sanity.

analysis.name: Pietro Bianchi
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
ENG4135 - Italian Cinema

Professor Bianchi is kind, cares about his students, and is clearly knowledgable on the subject(s) he teaches. His knowledge of Italy's history and appreciation of film is evident. He wants his students to succeed and is not a harsh grader. Watch the films, go to class, and you will succeed. Entertaining and educational.

History of Film pt 3 was one of the best classes I've taken at UF. Prof Bianchi does a great job demonstrating the continuous themes of this era of films and provoked me to think more deeply even about films I'd already seen before the class. He gives very thorough feedback on all assignments and is accessible outside of class.

Bianchi did a great job of emphasizing the historical context of the films we watched which enhanced my enjoyment; the films themselves were interesting and easy/fun to discuss in class. You are required to informally present about 1 film he assigns to you, he permits 3 unexcused absences. Covers important readings in class that will be on quizzes.

I had Professor Bianchi for both ENG3125 (History of Film Part 3) and ENG4133 (Cinema of the Global South) and he is for sure one of the best professors at UF. He's passionate about what he teaches, picks awesome films, and gives great feedback. I recommend taking a class or two, or more, with him, you'll learn a lot!

Bianchi is an awesome Professor. He cares about his students' and wants to see you care. Attendance is mandatory and your grade will go down if you don't go. If you watch the films and post the discussions, everything is easy. Two quizzes on the films, main grades are attendance and discussion posts. He's my favorite professor i've had.

analysis.name: William Billups
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Billups is a great professor, and this class was top-tier. The best class I've ever taken. Super interesting material. It's a ton of reading. Attendance mandatory. Classes are mostly discussions related to the readings, with the occasional lecture thrown in. A good number of essays that are graded firmly but fairly.

Primarily a lecture and class discussion based class, with essays and written work for at home work. Gives lots of take home reading but most of it can be skimmed and/or read right before class to participate in group discussions. The first half of papers use readings but the last half is independent from the readings.

Dr. Billups is very passionate about teaching history. However, if you do not like engaging with LOTS of dense literature and participating in class discussion, do NOT take Media in American Democracy. Compared to other history professors, Dr. Billups is a moderately tough grader, but he genuinely wants to see you succeed!

Dr. Billups truly cares about the students. He will schedule half of his week for office hours. I've heard most of the TA's can be quite tough. Please take Charlie Davidson as your TA. He is not only easier, but he will make you think and contemplate history in a different light during discussions.

Dr. Billups is AMAZING! He is my favorite history professor I have had at UF and would 100% take his class again. He is very knowledable on his topics and cares deeply about the success of his students. Class is very reading heavy but the readings are extremely interesting and relevant. Could not recommend DR. Billups enough.

analysis.name: Ragnhildur Bjarnadottir

Raga was great. I've had her for two classes in my graduate nursing program and enjoyed both. Great name, makes her memorable. Just goes by Dr. Raga. Very smart and a great professor. You get the sense she cares for her students. Also she is doing (or did in the past) informatics research I believe.

analysis.name: Karen Bjorndal
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bjorndal is the best! She's been the head of the Archie Carr Center for Sea Turtle research for years and has so much knowledge, wisdom and passion. She loves and cares about her students. Class is geared toward real learning, no exams just group projects and journal club each week but she picks the papers and they're pretty short and simple.

I love this lady. She is just soooo sweet and really engages with class. Show up for class and you're gonna get an A. I never had to worry about my grade in this class. It was so refreshing to just show up, talk about conservation, and just learn.

By far the best professor I have ever had. She is one of the few professors that take the time to connect with every single student. Always a joy to go to class and she was so passionate and knowledgable it made you want to learn more. I really wish she had more classes because I would take her again in a heart beat. If you like turtles take it!!!

Dr. Bjorndal is so passionate in her field of sea turtle ecology and biodiversity. I recommend taking this class if you like sea turtles and if you don't! She lectures/traches based on learning and with group participation. Great GPA booster, learning experience for research presentations in a group, and amazing subject material. The best class.

She always made sure to take our feedback to heart and check in that we were enjoying the material. Grading was primarily based on attendance and discussion classes, with a research project ongoing through the semester. Class can drone on a bit unless you are 100% passionate about sea turtle conservation, but still was an incredible class.

analysis.name: Sylvie Blum
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My goat. SO entertaining, really values participation and getting to know her students. Values ideas over grammar. Let me throw a backpack across the room as part of a scene (this class was 20th century french theater) and gave me extra credit for it. Love her down.
Dr. Blum is amazing! She genuinely wants to help you and is super flexible. She's funny in class too. Go to office hours just to talk to her! I wish I had taken her classes sooner!

She is  truly passionate about fashion and film. I learned so much, and it was genuinely a pleasure to attend her class. The structure was well-organized you watch the films at home and discuss them later in the week, which allows for better time management. She is also also very understanding and approachable.

Professor Blum is a fantastic professor who cares about her students. You must do the homework and be prepared to speak in class. She randomly calls on students to speak which is intimidating at first but it leads to great improvement. Just be ready to be called on 1-3 times each class. I would totally recommend her if you have the chance.

Took this my 1st sem & was worried I wouldn't keep up - she speaks French 95% of the time. Felt way more comfortable by a month in. Truly cares abt her students, gives lots of not-that-hard small assignments, generous grader. 5 "major" essays, 1-2 pages, interesting topics. Very French & endearing humor. Discussion participation matters. Love her!

analysis.name: Roger Blair
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The only grades for the course were three exams, but they weren't particularly difficult. He rambles a lot, but he is very knowledgeable about the matter, and textbook chapters are posted online if you don't attend class. The class material revolves around monopolies/monopsonies and Anti-Trust Law.

He is very kind, however, he doesn't use powerpoints, he provides a couple sheets of graphs at the beginning of lectures and then just talks. Most of the time the graphs aren't detailed so you have to make sure you're following along to make your own notes on them. Class is only three exams, he is very nice to talk with and very intelligent.

This class should have been miles easier than it was but this guy never failed to impress me with how quickly he overcomplicated simple subjects, how subjective he made the exams, and how ridiculous the grading structure was (your only grades are the three exams, no curve btw & completely subjective grading.) Lectures are also slow and monotonous..

I really enjoyed Dr. Blair's course and he is very knowledgeable and willing to explain anything from the class in office hours. Be prepared to study hard for exams and make sure you use all the materials he gives you. His lectures are very important for the exams, so be sure to stay on top of the content and ask questions if he is not clear.
Prof. Blair is extremely knowledgeable and always willing to help if you're genuinely interested in learning the material. Don't skip lectures or you will fall behind!

analysis.name: Laura Blecha

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Blecha is universally beloved. Mech 1 is a super easy class if you were good at Physics 1. Blecha makes it even better with spectacular lectures and great posted lecture notes. Quizzes are super easy and last one (ALC) is extra credit. Exams give back 20% of missed points via corrections (i.e. 80 goes to 84). Python hw helped me learn SciPy.

Professor Blecha has been one of the most understanding professors I have had. She truly wants to see you succeed. So accessible outside of class (spent an hour going over gravitation with me). I took this class as my first physics course ever, and I got an A. She is so kind, will offer help when she has time and is extremely considerate. 10/10

Professor Blecha was amazing with our Enriched Physics 1 class. She was very accommodating and understanding of the stressful events happening this year (COVID-19, election). Instead of a few big exams, our class had weekly quizzes. I prefer this format greatly and feel like I learned more. Textbook homework is challenging but helpful.

LOVE. THIS. WOMAN. She is the nicest professor you will have and you can tell she cares about both her students and what she is teaching. Only 12 quizzes and 12 homework assignments AND she drops the lowest 2 of each.

analysis.name: K  Blasco Soler

review_highlights.comment: I ACTUALLY TOOK THIS CLASS FOR AML2070 (American Lit)! However, I truly loved both the class and the professor. She is a kind and caring person who genuinely wants all her students to succeed. Attendance is mandatory, but she understands if you miss a few classes. I am not a big fan of poems or American literature, but I truly loved this class.

Amazing professor! She is very chill and understanding, doesn't expect you to be perfect and provides lots of resources to help. Attendance is mandatory but you can miss two classes without penalty. She truly cares so much about her students and making sure they are doing well. Can't recommend her enough!
She is sooo sweet and understanding. Attendance is mandatory but you can talk to her if you have any issues. She is so good would definitely recommend.

analysis.name: Susan Bluck
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Don't take this class. This professor is ABSURD. She randomly tanks the grades at the last minute and gives no care about it. This class is a waste of time. I spent my time making discussions THAT ANSWER EVERY QUESTION ASKED IN DETAIL; yet, she gives a 42/60 and this is the only grade that is worth over 20 points. What a scam of a class & professor

DON'T TAKE. The last week of the class, WHEN WE barely have ANY MORE ASSIGNMENTS TO BRING OUR GRADE UP, she dropped a major grade bomb. NO discussions are graded throughout the semester. She chooses 2 random ones to grade and PICK APART. I participated in each discussion every week and answered all questions just to get a 70%. absolute BS!!!!!!!!!!

I just cannot believe a class about old people is going to be the reason my GPA drops. Don't waste your time in this class. Seems like you need be to Edgar Allen Poe to do good on the two random discussions out of all 13 during the semester. Unfortunately my major is not english and my answers to every part of the discussion is not enough.

Just absolutely awful. Don't waste your time in this disgrace of a class. Take a class that you don't have to worry about your GPA dropping. Crazy that I currently have a B in a class about old people... This isn't a writing class so I'm confused how a singular discussion grade counts for this much. Honestly I am horrified.

What a terrible and unorganized professor. It's almost as if she wants her students to do badly. I thoroughly discussed every point in detail, yet I was robbed of my grade because she is too lazy to grade every discussion, so she chooses only 2 from the whole semester to give horrible grades on.

analysis.name: Brianna Blassneck
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Unreasonably difficult. Inconsistent deadlines. She assigned homework due over Spring break. She's a "nobody's perfect" grader so even if you follow the rubric to the "T" she'll still mark something off. Majority of the grade was based on a MASSIVE group project with 10 separate assignments. Lectures & text are from a previous year and not current.

This course was extremely informative. The semester long project is a great and a practical way to apply the information learned throughout the course. Her feedback is above and beyond appreciated, although it takes a while for her to return graded assignments. She offers lots of extra credit options throughout the semester. I highly recommend her!

Brianna is an amazing professor who really cares about her students and takes the time to help them succeed. Her class is very straightforward and as long as you come to class and pay attention you will do well. Brianna took the time to give helpful feedback on every assignment and even took time to help me find somewhere to gain event experience.

I'm Brianna's first class and it has been a joy being in her class. She has a lot of background in the hospitality event industry. She is a very caring and kind person with a good personality. There aren't exams- 4 module assignments in groups with quizzes, 2 site visits, and an easy 5 points if you do the active learning assignment in class.

I'm Brianna's first class and it has been a joy being in her class. She has a lot of background in the hospitality event industry. She is a very caring and kind person with a good personality. She gets back to you via email very promptly and wants you to succeed.

analysis.name: Jeremiah Blanchard
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: He is really cares about the students in his class. The class I had him with had 500+ students and he would respond individually to everyone. He is very active on the class Slack and would answer questions is a timely manner.
Awesome professor. Helps you whenever you need and loves his job! He always encourages us to go outside our confort zone and become better programmers! 10/10

Great professor and an even greater person. He truly cares about his students. The class was easy if you actually read the online books and studied. His exams are difficult, but he gives plenty of extra-credit to balance it out. If you put in the work you will easily get an A in the class.

Great professor. Projects are pretty tough and requires effort, but the prof is always available and willing to assist students even outside of office hours through email. The prof explains concepts really well for students to understand.

He's a great lecturer but exams and quizzes are oversimplified to true and false questions, which doesn't really encourage you to learn material. He gives a ton of assignments, a lot of which have poor descriptions, especially for projects. He's definitely a better CS professor than average, but not a model of perfection.

analysis.name: Bojan Lazarevic
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. L is the best professor! He is supportive and accessible, and he is willing to help with anything ID related. His assignment feedback is extremely personalized (and often is in video/audio clip form). I marked average difficulty, but I really mean, he is fair. I had a wonderful experience in both his courses I took. Would 100% recommend!

Dr. L is amazing. He is accessible through email and truly wants to support students. Also, his courses' designs are great. He is a fair grader and very kind. Ask him anything EdTech and he will certainly help!

As long as you submit your assignment by the deadline, you're going to be fine. No busy work. Everything is planned with a purpose. Dr. L is really good about leaving personalized video feedback and making an effort to know students. I have taken three classes with him and he is by far one of my favorite professors.

The professor is amazing and always responds within a reasonable time. He is a super fair grader and always leaves great feedback on assignments and posts. The course work is not difficult as long as you read the instructions and understand the topics you should do great.

Dr. L is a very respected professor at the University. His modules can be wordy and uninteresting at times, but he explains everything very thoroughly and assigns lots of in-class assignments for credit. If you need help with something, he is always willing to go out of his way for his students. I highly recommend any of his classes!

analysis.name: Joel Black
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Way too stressful for a gen ed. Ridiculous workload. Lectures were from another prof and discussions were student led, so he never taught nor prepared students. He gave no instruction leading up to the exams, so no one knew what to expect. He graded insanely harsh. Doable, but way more effort than it should be. Avoid if you can.

Lecture slides were vague but packed, and the professor seemed to be reading off of his own separate outline that he would never upload. His lectures always felt disorganized with how much he goes off on tangents. I had difficulty keeping focus in class, but easily did assignments since you can honestly ignore the lecture and just know the readings

The class was to substitute what is a good life because I heard so many people say they hated it. Well, I highly disliked this class. He barely knew what he was talking about and talked too fast, didn't even explain the slides he was presenting, and went on tangents every 2 seconds. He is a really nice guy and he really cares, but the class is bad

Anyone who complains about him being not helpful or not being clear is obviously one of those people who has to strictly memorize their notes and flips out if they are thrown a curve ball. He kept lectures interesting and his tests and papers left alot of room for your own opinion. Talks with a stutter, so sometimes hard to get. GREAT TEACHER!

His lectures revolve around class discussions, but he'll never call out on a student or make them look dumb if they give the wrong answer. A LOT of required reading and reading the recommended reading is sometimes necessary if you want to understand certain concepts better. Cons: he's vague with assignment details and student expectations

analysis.name: Stephanie Bogart
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I'm currently taking this class and it's being treated more as a writing class than a Quest class. Both the professor and TA are hard graders, every assignment I've submitted has had numerous comments on it, and I've very rarely gotten a 100% on anything. It's taken way too seriously for what it is. Just take a different class.

Dr. Bogart is one of my favorite professors at UF thus far. You can tell that she truly cares! Attendance is not mandatory, but she gives extra credit if you go. The exams are also a little tricky, but if you do your readings and take notes in lectures, there's no reason why you wouldn't get an A/B.

Exams were easy and open note. The lectures weren't really interesting. The writing assignments were quite doable. Just make sure to start on the last 3000-word final paper a week before it's due. The discussions were fun and you didn't have to prepare a lot for them.

I took this without the WR, so I can't speak on that. The lectures were engaging and she knows what she's talking about - I came to respect her a lot. The tests are ridiculously easy, and I barely remember the homework, so insignificant. The TA section was also a lot of fun, but my TA was a hilarious grad student who barely cared, so that helped.

Fun and SUPER EASY course. I spent minimal time on this course and easily got an A. Exams are open note, but very specific to the lectures. Watch lectures (super short) and take notes on a computer. There is 2 kinda big projects that have clear instructions and don't take too long. She offers EC zoom sessions where you can ask questions.

analysis.name: Miklos Bona
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great at answering questions and explaining the content. Grades are based solely on exams (6 progressive, and 1 final). Partial credit is given on exams, but its out of 4 points per exam. Study hard, and though homework isn't "assigned", it is best to actually use the textbook and practice questions from there. SUPER HELPFUL TECHNIQUE TO PASS EXAMS

This class was 100% participation! You are given a proof from "Proofs from the Book" and, as long as you give a reasonable presentation of this proof, and attend all other presentations you will get an A. Bona, after the presentation will give a few words on it and, I must say, the man is a genius and just listening to him is enamoring.

One of the best teachers I have had in any subject. He may seem a bit gruff at first, but he is truly interested in helping you learn the material as long as you are willing to put in the effort. Pay attention in class and do the homework (which is optional but very helpful) and you will not only do well but will actually develop an understanding.

Bona is a great professor. He's probably the best math professor I've taken, however his class was still extremely challenging. The class was structured in a way that required constant studying, but in the end that made studying for the final easier. Great class overall, but not for someone who isn't willing to put the time and effort into it.

I took him for a simple credit honors class, and it was pretty easy, but worth taking. I learned a lot about the proofs behind many math principles. I can tell that Bona is an extremely intelligent man, and he KNOWS his stuff. I don't doubt other reviewers who say he make his classes challenging, but that you learn a lot.

analysis.name: Bonnie Dorr

Projects are kinda pointless but considering most special topic courses are always full, this is a great alternative. Slides werent downloadable which was kinda a dealbreaker for taking notes but its wtv considering how free this class was

Dr. Dorr's class is extremely valuable. She is extremely competent and has been doing research for decades. It can be hard to reach her outside of class, but the TAs are very available. If you study, you'll learn everything you need to know.

Very chill class, easy assignments and projects, and Dr. Dorr is very passionate and knowledgable about NLP. This semester she implemented BLADE which is an AI chatbot specific to the class and it helped a lot. The lectures/quizzes/exams are straightforward with no surprises.

Always impossible for her to be wrong. "Some of you guys call advanced concepts trick questions." Honestly, if you need a good understanding of grammar to get a good understanding of the course. Projects are easy as hell, but quizzes will mess you up. 3 hour class, but the whole time is for reviewing the weekly quiz and answering general questions.

She's not a kind person. For some reason even though she's teaching a class, she has a general animosity towards students. If you have any issues in her class, be prepared to be blamed because she can't be wrong about anything
She also doesn't teach actual NLP, just gives you the esoteric textbook explanation. Too lazy to host her whole 3hour class

analysis.name: Maha  Bouhnin

analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class itself was pretty easy. The due dates weren't accurate, so make sure you do the homework a few days in advance. The lectures were all you needed, the textbook was unnecessary. Quizzes were open-note with no time limit. Assignments were simple. The professor didn't grade in a timely manner and several grades were posted on the last day.

The class was tough. Professor Bouhnin didn't help: slow grading, no feedback, and assignments often ungraded until the last minute. Without timely feedback, it's impossible to improve before the next assignment. Several tasks from months ago were graded right before the end. This approach was frustrating and needs improvement overall.

The class is easy because it is online and no exams, if there was I would fail. She posted deadlines to a canvas announcement multiple times, only to change them to be earlier causing numerous students to submit assignments late. Overall, a very nothing burger of a class, waste of time I wish I chose another class. Doesnt count for H credit

analysis.name: Markia Bowe
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her lectures are good but the 1st exam was very difficult harder than what she taught and she graded it harshly. I got the first part of a question wrong, but everything else was right and marked it all wrong. We just did our 2nd exam and she adjusted the difficulty. However very slow grader 1st exam was Sep 23 and we got results over a month later

Dr. Bowe really tries for all of her students to learn. At times, it is a bit obscure on what we will be tested on and I often felt unprepared for the exams. HW every other week that takes a few hours, 3 exams based on practice exams, and a lot of Extra Credit to boost your grade. Overall average teacher for a weird class.

Barely any practice for the exams and I often felt unprepared. Gives a good amount of extra credit but it would be better to have more practice for the exams. Class feels very unorganized and very less time between feedback and exams to cover up.

Classes are not mandatory so only 1/4 of class goes. Dr. Bowe is a nice person but a horrible teacher as you never know what you're learning and don't leave the class with anything gained. The grading is also random/inconsistent so be prepared. Not a difficult teacher but a 3/5 was given because of the grading. Lot's of random group presentations

not many materials to prepare for the exam. at no point could I predict what type of questions she would put on the exam. Is very caring if you reach out if she happens to answer your email. Class feels very disorganized

analysis.name: Michael Bumbach
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Bumbach was a great teacher. Really friendly, knowledgeable, and always available for help. Seemed to really care that we understood the material and explained things well. Lectures were online and somewhat dry. Tests were a little difficult due to the material and NCLEX style questioning. Would definitely love to take a class from him again.
online lectures are kind of useless but the class was great. He was an amazing instructor. Kind of sad to see him go. Be ready to fill out like an entire workbook though lol

While others are harsh for Dr. Bumbach, I don't think this is a fair or accurate description. He teaches in a graduate program, so I anticipate his courses to be more difficult. There is a lot of reading and exams are pretty tough. He is accessible and always willing to work with any issues. I would take his classes again.

This is a tough class although he is very upfront about this. He is a tough grader, but this is graduate school and should be. There is a lot of information, get ready to read. Also, this is an online course, I did love that I can read/learn when I wanted.

Took two of his grad courses. Clearly recycled material. He was responsive via email but his responses were usually not helpful. I understand he prob has a huge workload but I'm not even sure he understood his own rubrics and guidelines. Poor instructions and guidance when it came to assignments. Really inconsistent grading. Exams straight textbook

analysis.name: Christine Bucan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Such an amazing professor. She has so much PR experience under her belt and her lectures reflect it. Textbook is useful for studying but not mandatory. Her review sessions are amazing! As long as you attend lectures and contribute with the group project, it's an easy A. She also has tons of guest speakers and networking experiences in her lectures!

to pass the class, you def need to attend the lectures bc she'll tell you what's on the exam and what isn't. the exams are all situation based, so her wording can be more difficult at times. it's not hard to get an A, but you have to attend lecture. i didn't read the textbook and just attended lecture and ended with an A. very test heavy though

I love her! She was so knowledgable and experienced. As long as you attend and put some effort in, you'll do well. It's a few easy assignments, 1 group project, 3 exams (read the textbook for it). She lets you drop the lowest exam and assignment grade if you complete everything. Couldn't recommend this enough if you're slightly interested in PR.

So informative and clearly passionate about what she is teaching. The class isn't super difficult, but spend time memorizing key terms for the exams. She offers lots of extra credit and connections to people she knows in the industry. However, my TA gave me great grades on all individual assignments and a pretty bad grade on the group project.

Christine is great! There are only a few assignments and 4 exams for the course. However, if you sit for the first three exams and do well, you do not need to take the final (she drops your lowest exam grade). Exams are not too hard as long as you read the textbook and review lecture slides. Assignments are not too hard nor time-consuming.

analysis.name: Derek Burdette
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed going to this class every week. Homework once a week. Lectures were very good. Take lots of notes and follow the rubric given to a T and make sure to answer the question in the discussion as a whole and mimic the language in the readings. Not that many readings for this class.

Passionate about subject, but extremely knowledgable. Any BA or BFA major looking for an art history credit take this. Focuses on both the ART and the HISTORY which I feel many other professors in art history classes focus too heavily on the art without explaining the history or context. Burdette goes above and beyond explaining both's importance.

I never interacted with Dr. Burdette, but his lectures were AMAZING. If you are even a little interested in art, I highly recommend taking ARH2000. Because of this class, I want to take more art classes in the future. This is also an easy A (one short assignment and quiz per week) and an easy project instead of a final.
Dr. Burdette is the best professor I've had at UF. He is smart, funny, and down to earth. He knows his subject really well.

This class was a piece of cake. I took it for the diversity credit. There was one assignment a week plus a discussion board as well. I did read the chapters and honestly, I thought they were interesting. There is an essay where you have to go to a museum but it wasn't too bad. There is also a recorded final presentation that you can just read off.

analysis.name: James Bonczek
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 160 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Simply one of the easiest classes ever. I just needed a science course and this class was a great filler for the summer semester.    Just dont get lazy and wait to study the day of. Its not fun to listen to multiple lectures per day. Spread the lectures out, study, fill out the review sheet and you should be fine come test day.

I took this class for fun and always found his lectures passionate and interesting. The lecture quizzes are in-class only written assignments are extremely easy, and exams are taken outside of class and open-note. He drops a few of your lowest scores too, very easy A and I learned a lot about Florida's hydrology

This is an amazing professor who understands that most students are only taking the class to fulfill a science credit. He is very passionate about what he teaches and outside of the lecture quiz taken in class and an open note quiz every 2 weeks or so, there really is no work required. The exams are open note and can be taken wherever.

Could literally say nothing bad about Mr. Bonczek. He's clearly into what he teaches, and his lectures are always interesting. There are lecture quizzes almost every lecture, but if you are paying attention, they are very easy. Tests are open-note and online, and they aren't taken in class. Such a nice and funny teacher, I highly recommend him!

Professor Bonczek is an incredible professor who is very passionate about what he teaches. You can miss up to 7 lecture quizzes but I never wanted to miss a lecture as I always learned something fascinating about water. Exams are open note, I highly recommend this course!

analysis.name: James Bunch
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bunch is so fun and extremely caring for his Ag Ed students! I took AEC4324 which is a discussion based class where participation is crucial to getting anything out of the class. He is has a wealth of knowledge in this field, so ask questions and put forth an effort to get to know him. This class has a low workload but is an intro to Ag Ed.
By far my favorite professor since I got to UF. Lectures are actually really interesting and he makes them fun. Tests are also really easy.
Great professor, the class isnt easy but offers valuable information.

analysis.name: Jason Butler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is really really hard but good. I def remember everything from his class but be ready for super challenging exams that make up 100% of your grade and a fast moving pace. He is helpful though, but just be warned when he says something will be simple that is a lie.

Butler seems like a mean guy and that's because he is(he says it) but deep down he cares for the students. His lectures aren't the best, I never understood what was going on at all and I was below the average on all the exams. But I killed on the final and ended well. My advice, youtube every topic and don't be afraid to ask butler for help!

Dr. Butler knows what he's talking about, but sometimes had trouble conveying it to the class. Tests and HW were usually pretty tough (averages were in the 40%-60% range) but grading was completely scaled so it worked out.

Clear lecture style, a lot of algebra workouts left to the student. You must know and understand the homework to the point of being able to teach it to others in order to pass exams/quizzes.  Very difficult grader, not a lot of partial credit. Do extra homework problems and go to his office hours. Final exam is difficult.

Jason is tough but extremely helpful. He's quite knowledgeable and a great resource. Always answers emails. Swallow your pride and he will help you. Tests and quizzes are HARD but doing the homework will partially prepare you. He has optional texts, reading relevant sections of those helps too. Try to understand, not figure out what's on the test.

analysis.name: Taryn Buckley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is a great, easy elective. There are weekly quizzes that are not honor locked, and a midterm + a final that are honor locked and you have a week to take. There are also extra credit opportunities. The class was interesting and assignments are easy with most answers being found in the textbook.

Super easy class if you just work on the flashcards, the assignments are easy and interesting, and the tests are the quizzes but longer. The professor was kind and nice, and overall present for an online professor! Would recommend!

Great class. Super helpful if you're prehealth and very low maintenance. Midterm and final were super chill and if you do extra worksheets you can get extra points put towards ur midterm and final. Never had to worry about my grade in this class. I strongly recommend it!!!

Super easy class. You can finish the course (other than the midterm and final) in probably less than a week. Easy A and helpful for pre-health! The prof was very clear in her grading, though did not always respond to emails.

Very easy class that provided me with a lot of practical knowledge. Memorization based, so tests were very straightforward and easy to ace. A lot of extra credit provided, 12 points per each exam. Only two exams, a midterm and final. Professor seemed very nice and caring. She wanted the students to understand the content.

analysis.name: Richard Burt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's perhaps the most notorious professor in the English Department, and that is a wildly good thing. Burt has something of a cult following and that's because of the way he has students engage the films and writings. You will never watch a movie the same way again. Also, the class is pretty easy, just expect a lot of watching/reading.

There is A LOT of reading.  It can get pretty confusing and philosophical, but is mostly enjoyable.  Every now and then we watched films.  Course is discussion based, with Burt acting more like a moderator than a lecturer.  So you need to speak up.  He values all opinions and makes jokes every once in a while.  Burt is great!

I took three classes with Burt because I respected him and his teaching style so immensely. He challenged his students with difficult texts, and guided us through discussion like a lighthouse. Burt makes his classes accessible  to everyone, while leaving room open for people to excel. He receives criticism well, as he is humble and hilarious.

But is an eccentric and interesting prof. He is genius and you'll learn a lot. But his classes are not easy, you will have to think critically, read a lot, and write a lot. He is a good Prof. Show up to class, do the work, pay attention, and try and you should be okay. But you will be busy! Short notice on deadlines as well.

Assignments were unclear, expectations were less clear, discussions were mediocre, and the professor was breathtakingly unconcerned about his students. His classes are on fascinating topics, but he makes them suck. Which is quite a talent, in its own warped way. Avoid.

analysis.name: Emily Butler
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Butler is an amazing teacher. She's really knowledgeable in her field (Applied Linguistics) and current on what's happening in language and communication.  There's a midterm, 4 reaction papers as well as a final project consisting of 8-10 page essay with presentation. Be prepared to work but it will be worth it.  Her class is never boring!

Easy class but did not grade anything during the semester and shut down students when we asked  about when she was going to grade things and her messing up the dates for our final exam and project. Also, hearing her say the n word (hard r btw) and other slurs does not need to be a part of the curriculum.

She is EXTREMELY helpful in understanding the materials she teaches. She's patient and very understanding of the student culture at UF. She will challenge you but not overwhelm you. She teaches very understandably, even for people new to the linguistics/communications fields. She strives to build relationships with each class she has!

I took as many classes as I could with her! To me, it was clear she got excited over the content she taught, and it was contagious! It's as if we were both thinking, "This stuff is so cool!!" I will probably remember a lot of what she taught me for the rest of my life. She is the best professor I could have asked for. I'd endlessly recommend her.

I hate public speaking I get terribly shaky, but I still thoroughly enjoyed this class. Everyone was so nice & reassuring. She gave me great feedback on my speeches. Each assigned speech was interesting to explore, & it encouraged us to get creative or get passionate about the topic; some of them were really fun to prepare & share/listen to as well

analysis.name: Leon Brown
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is challenging without a textbook and in such timeframe (8wks), but he gave us soo much material to review even without a textbook. He also makes himself available to help students through regular office hours or you can just schedule a teams meeting with him. I would say it's a lot for a 2credit class but he's a good professor.

This course has way too many assignments. There are quizzes, labs, discussions, and two exams. He covers way too much material in 6 weeks. For the quizzes and exams, I felt very overwhelmed with the amount of material I had to know. I would have to constantly study to keep up. If there is another professor, take the class with them.

I've had Dr.Brown for both ISM3254 and ISM3255 now and I think he is incredible. I've had many coding professors in the past who can't seem to grasp the fact that coding is a new subject for many students. Dr. Brown walks you through Java so clearly and the assignments all have purpose. He is a gem of a professor.

Poor course structure across all his classes. With such a bad rate my professor at his previous school it's a mystery why UF hired him. He seems almost panicked teaching and gets himself always behind which puts us at risk consistently. Doesn't look out for student success at all.
He assigns convoluted assignments and never grades them so you do not know how well youre doing in the class. It is a 2 credit class that takes like 6 hours each weeek

analysis.name: Bryon Moraski
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Moraski is a great guy, very knowledgable. Theres a lot of readings, and the class is only really graded by attendance and the exams, which aren't too bad, but he likes to throw a couple curveball questions in there about niche things, and that can really mess your grade up because of the lack of any other assignments.

He's passionate about teaching and means well, but his exams are highly specific to lectures & readings. I had to study at least two hours a day to keep an A, and he doesn't share his slides. Paper was tough, and he's really strict about attendance and participation. He can seem timid when you ask for help. There are easier classes.

Please do not take this professor for your own mental health. He is very specific with his exams and participation. His paper was not hard to write but he is a tough grader. There are far easier classes to take as a poli sci major. Attendance is mandatory and he does not share notes or his power point at all.

Very interesting class but is difficult if you have no previous knowledge of Russia. Very informative but his slides are bare, so you have to pay attention and take notes. He wants students to succeed and be engaged. The class can attract strange people but he handles them. It's important to read and study. The tests are specific but managable.

Dr. Moraski was the best professor I had at UF.  He is insanely approachable, and his lectures were always interesting.  His classes require a good bit of reading and work, but it ultimately made me a much better student as a result.

analysis.name: Jonathan Brooks
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Brooks is compassionate, personable, and very knowledgeable. He was not once stumped by a question asked in class. He is a solid lecturer and usually had a few "when are we going to actually use this" examples. He makes a notoriously dry subject relevant and as interesting as it can be. Great guy, great teacher. Take him for numerical!

He's a really good teacher who cares a lot about his classes. He gives hard homework but he gives so much time to help his students understand it. His exams aren't bad if you pay attention to his lecture and he gives a lot of hints about it. The topic is kind of dry but its not really his fault. If you put in the effort you'll get an A.

His lectures are very enjoyable if you pay attention and really try to understand the material. The class requires a little more MATLAB than students are taught in COP2271, but the homework is doable, and sometimes enjoyable if you have a good understanding of the concepts being taught. Exams are mostly conceptual.

Dr. Brooks is the best professor I have had at UF! He puts lots of effort into making class as engaging as he can and making himself available to students outside of the classroom with lots of office hours. Go to office hours. He gives plenty of time to complete homework assignments, but they can be overwhelming if you wait too long.
Brooks does a good job of teaching a pretty dry subject in a way that is entertaining while in class. His homeworks take forever but that is the nature of the class. Overall great teacher

analysis.name: Brian Ray
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Took this class thinking it would be a relatively easy elective, seen as it is taught by two guidance counselors.  Awful tests and lots of lengthy assignments. They try and justify the difficulty of the class to other 3000 level business classes, but there is just too little substance for how hard and specific the tests are.  Really time consuming

The only positive reviews on this page are probably Ray himself. The class is not only useless, but requires a surprisingly high level of rote memorization. Avoid if you're looking for a course to further your education. Take this if you enjoy memorizing useless facts and spitting them out on exams.

Loved Professor Ray! I had a back injury midway through the semester, and he accommodated me instantly! 9 Assignments, 2 exams, and 3 papers for the ENTIRE class! He gives you plenty of time to complete all the assignments, just make sure not to procrastinate! Work gets graded by PAs, you'll be making your resume, LinkedIn, and autobiography.

Dr. Ray is one of the most inspirational and easygoing professors I've had at UF. He truly cares about his students and looks to make an impact on them in the long run. Class is very straightforward and clear on what is expected, would definitely take again.
Ethical Leadership is a very easy class and fun class! The professor cares about students and does not grade harshly at all. This is one of the only classes I actually enjoyed attending!

analysis.name: Brian Cahill
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 163 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Cahill wants you to succeed, but he's not really going to hand out A's like candy. He can come of as callous, but I think that he's just more into tough love than into coddling his students. He's willing to work with you and is very easy to approach, will make an effort to help people who are failing if it's a big problem.

Amazing. I love him. he is so passionate & makes you feel like you matter as a person. He offers help outside of class, and despite all of the extra credit opportunities I still MAY NOT pass the class. Hardest class of my life, no doubt. Incredibly difficult tests. As a person, Dr. Cahill rocks and I look forward to another easier class with him.

Very hard exams and quizzes, which make up almost your whole grade. Gives study guides but they're not any help for exams. Grades harshly and you don't get the opportunity to see what questions you missed on assignments. Class is extremely hard, take it with a different professor if you can. Would not recommend any of his classes.

Genuinely the weirdest prof. I've known. 

Assessments are assigned over holidays, refusal to accept verified medical notes. 

For such an easy class, he is very demeaning. He presents himself as relatable and "cool" at the beginning of the semester, this is a facade.

For the sake of your mental, find an alternative professor.
Great class that opened me up to a new area of psychology. Really knowledgeable, fun lectures, and interesting class. Easy A!

analysis.name: Paige Bressler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This is a rating for Federal Income Tax. She waits till the last minute to post everything including homework and study materials for the exam, she says incorrect things about the material in class, is unresponsive, and combines the undergrad and graduate version of the class so take the grad. Pros: She gives a study guide. Be prepared to cram.

She was very clear on what was expected on exams and quizzes, she gave us a review sheet on the exact topics to review and textbook questions that were very similair in difficulty to the exam questions. I didn't get automatic tutoring and feel that it isn't necessary to get an A as long as you go to lectures and complete the suggested homework.

For FAR1 at UF, Bressler is hands down the best option.
Before each quiz and exam, she tells you exactly what types of problems will be on them and example problems that are similar. If you study a few days before, you're guarenteed to do well. FAR will be hard regardless of your prof, but an A is absolutely achievable with Bressler if you study.

This class is essentially Corp Taxation again. It's more code heavy, which is annoying as you have to sift through IRC instead of being taught formulas like with Schadewald. However, Bressler is super nice, and really cares about the students. She grades extremely easily. Show up and pay attention and you'll be good.

analysis.name: Sarah Brunnig
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This professor rambles a lot and her lectures are usually just asking students to read/watch things outside of class. She cares A LOT about participating even in big lecture halls. You really just have to teach yourself the information outside of the class. She tracks attendance and sometimes twice a class. Also won't believe you for tech issues.

Exams are pretty straight forward and align with the study guides she provides. Weekly in-class group assignments. Mandatory attendance. Goes on tangents and is adamant about participation during class. Tedious international project. Extra credit provided. TLDR; average difficulty, fair professor but really annoying format-wise.

Records attendance based on chat and iclickers, up to 7 absences. The subject isn't hard, but you do need to study to do well on exams (reused parts from practice). 5 min assignment due Sundays and discussions. Expects posts to be college level, kinda strict but doable. Likes to ramble in lectures but interesting! Old fashioned and expects effort.

Such a bad lecturer. The whole class is poorly organized. She's a nice lady, but she does not know how to use technology at all, which makes it literally impossible to navigate the course. Also, the iClicker is so annoying bc she literally stops it after 30 seconds and then gets upset when not enough people have answered it.

She rambles a lot in her lectures which made me lose focus even when I was actually trying to learn. If you want to do well on the exams focus on reading the textbook and doing the adaptive quizzes. While I wouldn't take her class again, she is very kind, responsive and helpful when I messaged her. Do the extra credit!

analysis.name: Charles Bwenge
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Take this class! Dr. Bwenge is maybe the most caring professor that I've had at UF. His style is "untraditional," but in a good way. He mixes readings and films for an interactive conversation rather than a lecture. I was always excited to come to class and I surprised myself with how much I learned as the class was essentially a completion grade

He is very unorganized. He speaks very quickly and rambles often. Additionally, the work that he tends to give seems like busy work rather than valuable knowledge. This class is not very flexible and needs and online option as well. Everything he gives out is printed and in person which is difficult for when unexpected emergencies come across.

Professor is really passionate about the class and loves to hear what students have to say about the different topics that are explored. There are only 3 short papers you have to write, 4 reading quizzes (the readings are short), and a group project at the end. He gives very clear instructions for all assignments and answers all questions.

the best humanities class ever. He is the most entertaining and lively teacher. He has a strong accent, but hes SO flexible. NO exams. easy quizzes on like 3 pages every now n then. gives out A's like no tomorrow. 2 papers and 1 group project. LOTS of movies. BUY THE BOOK, you need it for the quizzes.

One of the best/most interesting professors I have had at UF. Bwenge is amazing. He has a true passion for the subject, and he cares about his students. Assignments are easy, and the projects help you learn a lot about Africa. Take this class for a requirement or just for fun.

analysis.name: Kathy Byrne
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is a little quirky but I loved her class. It was interesting and funny. What she goes over in the lectures is on the tests so attend them. If you can't, make sure to attend the review sessions because those are hands down the most important days (next to the tests themselves). Have fun with her and get to know her. You'll love the class too.

easy easy class. really boring and strange but almost no work. u do have to go see 3 plays though. test review with all the answers right b4 the test so go to that. the teacher is not the best but just bring something to do during lecture since they take attendence. ta's not hard graders. group project at the end. good way to get a diversity credit

I took the online section of this class.  It was the most time consuming class that I had the whole semester.  While the assignments were easy and I got an A in the class, each assignment is only worth 10 points out of about 400 points possible.  You end up doing a ton of busy work.  If you want an easy A, go for it, but be prepared for busy work.

I took her for TPP2100. At first glance the semester seemed like it might be horrible. However, she taught us to get out of our shells, especially for those who had no prior acting experience. The class we had became one of the most close group of friends I've seen in a classroom setting. It was truly an honor. Take this class. You never know. :)

This is such and easy class, dont even buy the book. Its an extremely easy A. The problem is that I really like theatre, but there is not passion in this class. Take acting for nonmajors if you like drama and actually want to learn about it-its not a hard alternative. I didnt learn anything from the actual teacher, but the ta's showed passion. :)

analysis.name: Judith-Kelly Byram
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst teachers I've had at UF, and it is not because the class material is challenging.  Her attitude is the worst, she thinks that because she has a PhD in neurology she is better than everybody else.  Directions were never clear until papers were graded.  Also, she bases particpation grades pretty much on whether or not she likes you.

Unclear on assignments, refused to answer some reasonable questions unrealistic expectations, made 25% of the midterm on a question the class was confused about and told us she didn't have time to go teach it to us easily upset & often perceived as rude not helpful with any solutions when I reached out for help Worst scholastic experience to date

Believe me when I say this woman is insane. I am certain she has anger management issues because she screams at people for no good reason. NEVER have anything out unless its related to her class because if she sees even a planner she will embarrass you. Do the readings and take detailed notes because she asks for very specific answers on quizzes.

This class was HORRIBLE!! She is very unclear about what she expects from the assignments until after they're graded. Her grading is very inconsistent among different students. She never gives clear answers to questions either. Good luck in this class! I don't know how, but I somehow managed an A, so it is possible.

analysis.name: Fred Byrd
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Summary: Take the class. And Go to his office hours, people.   The Backstory: I've always sucked at math. But The Byrdman was really helpful.  I was intimidated by his beard at first, but he's actually super nice. Knows a ton about math and worked hard to help me understand. I feel totally less mediocore now.

I loved this class a lot. He was very helpful and understanding. Just study your notes and complete the H.W. assignments and you'll be good. He was the best math professor that I experienced at UF. I finished off with an A.

I was pretty nervous about Calc 2 coming into this class since I was never really great at math, but Professor Byrd made it easier with his discussions and notes. I also used study edge and that helped a lot!
Mr. Byrd was very helpful. It's clear that he likes what he's teaching and wants you to do good. I took Trig and Precalc separate and recommend it. I would take his class again.
His helpfulness in office hours helped me pass. Personally I think Fred is a really cool guy.

analysis.name: Byung Ho Kang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst professors at UF. Should have been a simple science elective, turned out to be my worst class of the semester. The material itself isnt that bad, but the teacher thinks hes teaching at Harvard.The questions are so convoluted, you dont even understand what it is asking. Must teach yourself everything, forget understanding him speak.

If you have taken BCH 4024 then this will be extremely easy for you. If you have no prior knowledge of biochemistry then you are going to be utterly lost  but the textbook is written in very simple language so just read it and you'll be fine. He gives extra credit for coming to class. Study the practice questions and you will do well on the exams.

This class turned out to be way more difficult than I expected. Dr. Kang's dialect of what I assume resembles the English language to him is pretty much unintelligible. I feel like most professors are more concerned about the big picture when it comes to a class that covers a lot of material, however this guy wants you to know every little detail.

I thought this class would be just like any other Biology class where you put in the time to read the book, go to class, take notes, and do the practice tests and you would be fine. Wrong. I study so much for this class and still get low grades on the exams. Questions are extremely tricky. You should probably read the book twice to do OK on them.

His accent isn't a big deal and he's actually kind of funny.  As others have said, his tests are based off the practice problems he gives,a few might be verbatim but most he gives a different twist to the question and it can be really tricky.  Reading the book is really helpful need to make sure you UNDERSTAND the CONCEPTS not just memorizing.

analysis.name: Jason Byrd
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Don't take his classes ladies! It was evident that some students received preferential treatment, while others were often dismissed or criticized harshly. It's crucial for educators to foster respect and professionalism in their interactions with students. I observed him harass a student employee. UF did the right thing in firing him. Toxic!

This was the best class I have taken. Dr. Byrd is the best professor. He has so much experience which makes his lectures so much more interesting.  He's incredibly intelligent and hilarious. Definitely go to class! It's necessary to be able to pass, plus it's just great to listen to lectures. He's not bad to look at and crush on either.

He is a horrible professor, one of the worst at UF. He constantly makes really big assignments all due on the same day and then more big assignments due right after that without any kind of break. He can also be really mean and patronizing, especially if you are trying to advance yourself in the field. If you do not have to take him, then do not.

I took both of Dr. Byrd's classes and they were by far the best classes I've ever taken at UF. Dr. Byrd is extremely helpful & honestly cares about his students. Class is easy and interesting. You don't really need the textbook. I highly recommend his classes!

Very interesting class. Easy A as long as you go to lecture. Dr. Byrd is extremely helpful and sweet, and definitely not bad to look at. ;) Highly recommended. He's the only prof I've ever had a slight crush on!

analysis.name: James Cain
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is the chillest professor I have ever had. Some musical experience is required, but he is very helpful with any problems you may encounter and will stick around after class if needed.
Super chill guy, fun to work with. You kind of have to have some background knowledge of singing/sightreading but at this point in school most people in chorus have already sang before.

Great choir director, really chill guy. Doesn't provide many resources for beginners unless you ask, but I found most of what we sang was relatively easy to pick up with practice even without being able to sight read.

Professor Cain conducts the Choral (treble choir) and the Glee Club (tenor-bass choir), and his good personality makes learning about music and performing it fun and relaxed. I have been in Glee Club for 3 semesters now, and each semester has at least one concert to perform at, and Dr. Cain frequently looks for more performance opportunities.

Less experienced students aren't helped much with performances. Often criticizes smaller things in comparison to glaring problems with performances. For a class marketed towards students of any experience level, it's not clear how much that is considered. Overall, seems like a chill guy.

analysis.name: Karina Cadena
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My intention here is not to be mean, but honest: Prof. Cadena is a very nice person, but she is not the greatest instructor. Her class was very hard to follow, the quizzes often had nothing to do with the exams, and I basically ended up teaching myself the entire material of the class. Old exams were helpful, but I would not take her class again.

The class is graded on 3 exams worth 75% and 10 quizzes worth 25%. Be prepared to study. I did not do well on my second exam because I skipped lecture and did not study so do not do that. Class is in person but she does zoom lectures. Quizzes and exams are difficult but fair and manageable. She posts old exams to review which are VERY helpful.

Good lecturer, very receptive to questions/comments. She also holds a zoom which is convenient if you can't make it. To study for the exams, just do the old ones (which she gives you so many of). There are online quizzes, which help make you stay up-to-date with the material, and they are multiple attempts so it's chill if you mess up at first.

This professor was rude to me in front of the entire lecture hall. She may have had good intentions, but she didn't have the decency to think through what she was doing. Because the class also had online lectures, I attended those instead. Although I didn't do as well as I hoped, I still ended the semester with a relatively high grade.
easy ahh class. for tests just spam the old exams and you're chillin. ended the class with like a 100.

analysis.name: Laura Cruz Castro
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 59 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I loved her class! She cares a lot and it shows. Her tests were not the best, they were hard and there was A LOT for relatively little time. Projects were better. She gives you a lot of time, explains the necessary things, and is flexible with deadlines when a lot of students are struggling. Very understanding and caring, skilled teacher.

This class wasn't the easiest but also wasn't the hardest. If you already know python/coding then itll be a breeze but if you're completely new it's kind of tricky if you're taking it with other hard classes. Assignments arent too bad, Labs are kind of time consuming,+theres usually a 2-q quiz weekly. Projects are DEVIOUS. Exams are ok but get you

She is so chill, if you can take this class with her, do it. Avoid the in person sections of Python with the other profs, heard they are much harder. Everything is open note and there's extra credit on almost anything. Super responsive outside of class and clear on grading. The homeworks can take a little while, but besides that easy A class.

Amazing professor. I was taking the in-person Python coding section and struggling, but her online section is very slow-paced and thorough, so I felt like it was much easier to understand the language. Very helpful and kind, responds fast to emails/discord and always on the side of the student/helping the student. Exams and projects are open note.

If you want a professor who genuinely cares about her students then look no further. I have no doubt in my mind that Professor Cruz wants what is best for her students and is patient, kind, and will work things through with you. Having a Professor like her is a rare and incredible experience that I highly recommend you take.

analysis.name: Luca Di Cerbo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
This was one of the only classes where attending lecture actually mattered and made sense in real time. I didn't feel like I had to reteach myself the material afterward.

That alone puts him among the best professors in the department, in my opinion. I highly recommend taking this class if you have the opportunity.

I'm not gonna lie, Dr. Di Cerbo was behind the main professor in lectures for the whole semester and he didn't explain the material quite as well, but if you happen to make your way to his office hours, he his very good at helping you understand the material. Only 75% attendance required for a 100% in the grade book. Beware of the tough final.
