Quizzes are attendance-based and exams are straightforward with no tricks or surprises. He's also really funny and lighthearted. Take for a chill math elective
He was great would 100% recommend over pretty much any of the other math professors

I enjoyed this class. It was the first time he taught calc 3 and he explained the material very well. He answered everyone's questions thoroughly and is a very caring professor. The final is very difficult. I got high As on the first 3 exams and failed the final, the material got exponentially harder. But I am a freshman, and I am glad I had him!

analysis.name: Celeste Martinez
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She was not made to be a teacher. Unorganized, unclear with directions and grades on what is not included in rubric. The rubric will show you did A+ work but she will give you a full letter grade off for kicks.

I have tons of respect for Professor Martinez because I can tell she is genuinely passionate about social media management. However, her class is one of the hardest classes I have ever taken! I am a straight A student taking five classes, and thought that social media would be a light course load. WRONG! She is unclear, unhelpful, and intimidating.

This is my 2nd time around with this professor and I can assure you I didn't select this class based on the instructor. As is often the case, UF will work with some lackluster professor based in another country who could not care less. The curriculum is full of technical issues that should have been fixed long ago- highly unprofessional.

This professor is a very tough grader and extremely strict, with little room for flexibility or accommodations. She doesn't even hold lectures at all and grading was harsh and didn't always reflect the effort put into assignments. I didn't feel supported, and it was difficult to get clear answers when issues came up.

AWFUL!! She is the most nit picky professor i've ever had at UF which is ridiculous for a class about social media. Grades so unfairly no matter how much time you put into an assignment. She takes a week to answer an email, I had to follow up twice before getting a response. Avoid her.

analysis.name: Recep Celebi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Recep's lectures were engaging, but make sure to write fast because he doesn't stop going once class starts. He was pretty funny and kind, and wants his students to succeed. Make sure to go to office hours if you are struggling because he does randomly call on students during class for answers, which keeps the class engaged.

Mr. Celebi cares about his students and is happy to answer questions in class or office hours. However, he is exceptionally particular about the take-home quizzes, to the point where he would critique my handwriting and formatting of my work. This was my first math class at UF and I hated it, but it also prepared me for my future classes.

I took Calculus 3 with Professor Recep Celebi in summer 2024. His enthusiasm for mathematics and willingness to provide additional support outside of class significantly enhanced my learning experience. I highly recommend his course to anyone looking to deepen their understanding of calculus.

I honestly did not struggle to get an A in this class but I know that was not true for most of our class. His tests were really hard but he awards a majority of the points for the work and the tests have bonus points, so I found it easy as a non-math inclined student to get A's on them. He gives EC + weekly at home tests. He's also really funny lol

I'm not going to lie, Recep was a tough TA. However, I wouldn't have any other instructor for Calc 2. He genuinely cares for his students and wants them to succeed. His lectures were so clear and easy to follow. However, he did single out students sometimes, which is the only thing preventing me from giving him a 5/5.

analysis.name: Erta Cenko
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I absolutely loved Dr. Cenko! She is one of my favorite professors here at UF simply because of how kind she is to her students and her passion for public health is clear. The class is simple (I took it in-person) and the requirements to get an A are clear. She is also always open to feedback, which I love in a professor.

Cenko is the best professor I've had at UF! I took two classes with her in Fall and she was amazing in both. She cares for the students and wants us to learn. I messed up an assignment and instead of giving me 0 points she offered to meet and review the module together to make sure I understood. She was also very helpful with a rec letter. 10/10

Great professor. Things felt a bit disorganized but it's obvious she cares about her students and the subject matter. Basically everything involves a group-project, which wasn't my favorite. It is such an easy class, only 2 quizzes are graded and there are no exams. Grading was a bit slow at times, but that was mainly the TA, not Dr. Cenko.

If I could take another class with Dr. Cenko, I absolutely would. She is hands down one of the nicest and best professors I've had not just in PHHP but in my entire time at UF! Probably one of the best decisions I made was taking HSC3502 with her over Hanson. Everything about this class from tests to projects was handled so great. 1000+/10 for sure

Dr. Cenko is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about public health and teaching it understandably to her students. We had a hybrid class that met once a week and made our semester-long groups at the beginning of the semester. If you're looking for a light workload class that you'll enjoy, this is the one. Would definitely take her again!

analysis.name: Celeste Wagner
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I am so sad that she left UF. She is honestly one of the nicest and caring people I've met. Her class was full of discussion where people could freely say and think without judgement. You can tell that she put a lot of effort into her lectures and the assignments were simple enough to teach the material without overwhelming you.

Prof. Wagner was such a joy. I think the class would have been better if more people responded to her questions, but it was pretty easy and she made her assignment expectations clear. She did always take a point or two off on the group projects but she left feedback on ways to improve that I think was valid. Definitely the best option for MMC2604!

She's one of the sweetest people ever! She's incredibly accommodating, understanding and flexible. She gives really good and interesting lectures and tries to engage class discussion. There's a lot of readings, supplemental materials but if you find your way to more easily go through it you should be fine. I'd definitely take her again!

The difficulty of this class honestly depends on the TAs. I got stuck with very harsh graders, so understand what their expectations are. Dr. Wagner is great and tries to keep students engaged. She listens to the needs of the class and adjusts her lectures based on that. I'd recommend going to the office hours before exams and the short essays.

analysis.name: Cecilia Schulz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cece is a great teacher who tries to make every topic fun and interesting. She really knows so much about the retail industry so you know you are getting correct information. There are only a few assignments and pop quizzes but overall not too difficult!

I never know what to expect! Every day in class is something completely different. You can tell she puts in a lot of thought and effort in making her lectures interesting and FUNNY! Youll definitely learn a TON about he retail industry in this section. I know I feel more prepared now to head out into the field. Worked hard but definitely worth it.

Just read the chapters 1 day before and make sure you know the vocabulary. There are 4 exams (50 questions each) composing 200 out of the 300 possible points. There is a presentation about a current event article(10pts), a group project(30pts) , 3 pop quizzes (5 points each) and 40 points ( 10 each) of online HW and attending retail bash (5pts)

Great one credit class and great if you're interested in retailing.  There are guest speakers every class and it's easy to get an A.  All you have to do is attend a luncheon (great food), write a paper on one of the speaker's presentation (3-5 pgs) and attend a focus group.

Lectures are enjoyable and workload is minimal. 4 exams that primarily cover the content from the online textbook on Connect. Do not skip the short "lecture extensions" as it is common to be asked about them on an exam. Do the extra credit and you should get an easy A

analysis.name: Carol Demas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 115 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The course content could be valuable, but the teaching and support did not meet my expectations. Instructions and grading expectations were not always communicated clearly, and when I reached out for help, my questions often felt dismissed rather than addressed. The classroom and office-hour interactions did not feel consistently welcoming

The professor is very strict and expects close attention to details. However, the teaching style and communication approach can make it difficult to fully understand expectations. In my experience, feedback and grading felt rigid, and small administrative mistakes (such as entering the wrong exam ID) resulted in point deductions.

Dr. Demas is a wonderful professor! She explains the material clearly and makes the math as approachable as it can be. She may come off a bit cold at times, but it's really not hard to get on her good side; just don't skip every exam. I cannot recommend her enough. She's the go-to professor for Elementary Differential Equations and for good reason.

Stay on top of the homework, I know it's alot. It is great preparation for the exams. Makes sure to do the past exams. It's very doable to get an A in this class, especially with the extra credit. The final exam was probably the most difficult but I did well on the first 3 so I didn't have to learn too much of the new stuff. Great professor.

Lectures very well, she made the class pretty easy since she taught the material well and was pretty clear with what was going to be on exams. It is a decent amount of work with the lectures and quizzes for them, but if you watch lectures and do assignments you will do well. In one of the lectures I think she said 80% of students get an A or A-.

analysis.name: Hadder Ceballos
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This was probably the first time I actually enjoyed a Spanish class and it was all because of Hadder! He was hilarious, and always made it a point to get to know everyone in the class. He was also a super fair grader. The only reason I got an A- instead of an A is because I didn't really study for anything in the class, so I'd recommend practicing!

My favorite professor at UF by far. He is very laid back, loves teaching, and is very in tune with his students' lives and interests. He is very understanding if you miss class and will do everything he can to help you learn tough topics. He makes learning Spanish so easy and fun. I looked forward to going to his class every day!

This professor is the best I've had so far. He's so helpful and caring. Spanish can be difficult but he makes it fun and I actually looked forward to going to class. 100% recommend. Thinking about continuing further with Spanish. This prof makes getting an A very doable.

Prof Ceballos is one of the best teachers I've ever had at UF. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to see us succeed. He goes out of his way to make class fun! I honestly can't say enough good things about him.
While this class has a major online component with quizzes that werent very enjoyable, its fairly easy overall. Professor Ceballos was great! I loved going to his class.

analysis.name: Douglas Cenzer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cenzer makes this class very easy!  Don't read the book, it will just confuse you.  Cenzer's lectures are very clear and show you exactly how to do the test questions.  At times he loses himself and stands muttering to himself, but this minor flaw is greatly overshadowed by his greatness as a professor.  Take Cenzer for Differential Equations!

He seems to be a nice guy, but he is definitely not a good teacher. His lectures are unorganized and sometimes incomprehensible. Since he is not much of a help, the course becomes unnecessarily more difficult, especially if you are new to the concept of mathematical proofs. Be prepared to grind the textbook. Please avoid him if you can.

He offers little to no explanations; one time he literally said no when I asked him to go over a problem. His lectures are all over the place and impossible to comprehend. I have to rely heavily on the textbook, yet it's not enough and he doesn't offer supplementary learning besides that, classwork, and homework. Avoid him if you can.

if you are going to take this class, you better make sure you have this teacher, he has been one of my favorite teachers so far. VERY VERY clear with his lectures, made this class really easy, 4 exams (final optional), exams questions come exactly from suggested HW problems, knew every student's name, very kind and encouraging!

Seems like a normal guy compared to many in the math department. Nice and helpful person, but one of the worst lecturers. He isn't prepared, mutters to the board, you can't understand him, searches notes frantically, forgets how to do proofs, just stands drumming his fingers on the desk. Each lecture is improvised with him.

analysis.name: Christopher Dorst
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took Dr. Dorst for PHI4930 Philosophy of Quantum Mechanics. Dr. Dorst is one of the most understanding, accessible, and knowledgeable professors in the UF Philosophy Department. His class is difficult, and he tries his best to explain dense material. His class is exam-heavy, and his grading is challenging. Going to office hours is a must.

I've taken two courses with Chris. He is an incredibly thorough and talented lecturer - I was definitely not at my best during either course, and the lectures carried me into understanding the material. Gives great line-by-line feedback on exams. All-around an incredibly compassionate and knowledgeable person. Take a class with him if you can.

Absolutely fantastic professor. Two readings are assigned per week and discussed in depth during class time. The readings can be somewhat difficult, but he explains the content of the readings clearly during lectures. You are graded on 2 papers and 2 free response assignments, and some easy reading quizzes every class to encourage participation.
Cool, funny, accommodating, provides excellent feedback, and evidently very passionate about his philosophical niche. Phenomenal instructor--take him. Huzzah!

This class had 4 papers, reading quizzes, and participation as your grade. The participation is based on the discussion section so you don't really need to talk in class (I never did). The papers are graded based on how well you form your argument, its not very strict but you will never get a 100. All reading quizzes are free response. Great class.

analysis.name: Nathalie Ciesco
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would strongly discourage anyone who is not genuinely interested in learning French from taking this course. To those who are, however, I would highly recommend it: Professor Ciesco designed a really efficient online system that covers a lot of material for just one semester. The assignments can get pretty tedious but there's plenty of groupwork

I was scared by the reviews here but this class was great. Yes there is a lot of homework but it certainly did not take up 5 hours of my week. I have a very intense class schedule and this one is the least of my worries. VERY accommodating whenever I emailed her for an extension.  In my opinion, if you have to take a language this is the way to go.

Definitely a lot of HW but it was all very relevant and useful. I feel like I've significantly improved my french language skills. Quizzes are pretty easy if you study and she gives many opportunities for extra credit. Gives half points back on all writing exams.

Definitely my favorite french teacher so far!! Nathalie is lots of fun and very entertaining. She's also VERY willing to help outside of the classroom, and will work with you to help you succeed. She does expect a lot from her students though, so come prepared to class- and be ready to participate! :)

This is a very intensive class, but the professor is very accommodating. You have to do 5 talk abroads and I think 5 group assignments a semester. The homework is very intensive and the tests are difficult, but they always address what was taught in class. You will pretty much be doing homework everyday for the semester, but it's a 5 credit class.

analysis.name: Chuck Peek
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Negative experience with this professor. Lack of professionalism in the classroom. Much is said of this man and little of it is good. Nay, none of it's good. I totally regret taking this class. Grading criteria is unclear, but expectations are high. Sir, you must meet us with effort - you expect the world but give but a crumb. Try again.

I do not recommend taking classes with Dr. Peek. Rubrics and grading deductions were unclear and often arbitrary. He was a tough grader and frequently gave zeros without clear justification. Communication felt dismissive, reflecting a focus on punitive grading rather than pedagogy, even in an introductory course.

the MOST UNCLEAR GRADING CRITERIA EVER!!!!!! do not take him unless u want a mid grade for good work its like he wants his students not to do well. He takes off an insane amount of points when you dont follow instructions he never had listed, rubric is insanely unclear and for ur own sanity RUNNNNN FROM CHUCK/CHARLES PEEK.

The rubrics provided are unclear and set up unevenly to the point that one mistake or slight underdevelopment means you go from an A to a B. That paired with the late grading time and vague feedback means its difficult to learn from your mistakes and by the time you do, you would have done 2-3 weeks worth of work with no improvements.

Worst professor I have ever had at UF! Not helpful at all. I attended class and took good notes but when I asked him for extra help he denied it. Does not care about students. Makes notes and exams as difficult as possible. Theres a reason so many people got C or less in the class. Only a few A's out of a few hundred students.

analysis.name: Cindy Spence
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was very tough in the beginning and had a harsh learning curve, but Spence made me such a better writer in the end. She will be very tough on you, but listen to everything she says, and you will become such a better writer because of it. I started the class with a 58 and ended with a B, and three papers were published! Go to her for help

This was by far the hardest class I have taken. Spence gives out 2x more assignments than other JOU3101 professors. I recommend Ross. Spence was difficult to communicate with; more than half my class dropped out.

Prof. Spence is the best. I am so happy I had her as my lab instructor. She is so encouraging and really cares about the success of her students. She is also super accessible and willing to help outside of class. She gives great feedback and honestly just wants to see her students do well. Don't let this course intimidate you!
Really tough but you will learn a lot from her. I went from a 44 in the beginning of the class to a B. Do Not Give Up.

analysis.name: Daniel Cicenia
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Likes participation. takes random attendance. tests are multiple choice, gives good review though. really listens to students and is open to debates and concerns. really easy class and cool professor. Attend class to get participation points.

If you are a poly sci major or you are going for the Political Campaigning Certificate, TAKE THIS CLASS! There is no easier class at UF. All the lectures are on powerpoints that he emails you. He takes random attendance. All his tests, including the midterm, he reviews the class before. In his reviews he practically gives you the answers! Take it!

Boring teacher but easy class and very helpful.  Gives random attendance so you should go to class.  Before every test he gives a review and basically tells you every question that will be on the test as well as the essay question, so it is very easy to do well if you just study for 15 minutes.  Definitely recommend taking this teacher!!!!

He's a really nice guy, but a bit of a pushover so his class is REALLY easy. Go to reviews before the tests - he'll pretty much give you the answers. If you participate in class and go to his office hours, he'll go easy on you when grading your papers.
Take him! you learn a lot and if you put in a little effort you can get an A. He does go over everything before the exam. Takes random attendance so go.

analysis.name: Cindy Dosch
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Best professor I've had at UF. If you have the opportunity to take her at a decent time slot, do a favor for your GPA and take FAR 2 with Dosch. Very tough exams, but extremely fair and she prepares you well. Everything you need to know is in her lecture slides and in the assigned homework problems.

Great public speaker. Nice. Funny. Goes above and beyond. Very caring, if you're going through anything personal she will help A LOT. Amazing at explaining content. Very fair. Takes one week to grade. Send you an email if shes concerned about you not passing. Simply deserves every award and raise out there FR

Professor Dosch is the best! I am an accounting major who took the ACG2391 elective for fun, and it was extremely worthwhile. I am actually looking forward to FAR 1 in the future, since she is the professor. If you have a chance, definitely take Exploring Careers in Accounting and get to know Professor Dosch.
A simple Pass/Fail class, definitely not difficult at all, just show up. Dosch is lovely and very charismatic, clearly cares a lot about working with students.

If Cindy Dosch has a million fans, then I am one of them. If Cindy Dosch has ten fans, then I am one of them. If Cindy Dosch has only one fan then that is me. If Cindy Dosch has no fans, then that means I am no longer on earth. If the world is against Cindy Dosch, then I am against the world.

analysis.name: Cindy Prins
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Course was hybrid, with lectures recorded online and discussions in class once a week. It's an interesting course and I've come to like it. The book is a must because the lectures are based on the book. It's very helpful in clarifying concepts because the lectures do not cover everything.

Good class, first half was great but second half was not my favorite. Tests are ambiguous and difficult. Study hard; be ready for anything and give as much detail on free response questions (70-90% of questions are free response on exams).
Dr. Prins is an incredible teacher! Epidemiology is awesome to begin with, but she mak
Great teacher! She is very nice and her lecture notes are mostly from the textbook.
Good epidemiology professor. Helpful, and cute too.  Overall satisfactory.

analysis.name: Cindi Figueroa
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Keeps my interest and brings clinical life experiences to her teachings. Highly recommended if interested in becoming an Adult Nurse Practitioner at UF in the College of Nursing. She is a faculty who truly listens & understands her students! Glad to have Dr Figueroa-Haas as my advisor & looking forward to continuing in this program. BSN-DNP student

It was a difficult & disruptive class for Dr Haas to teach, but she did the best she could with what she had to deal with..a new unprepared,cooker,lab professor in 3067L,who did not cover the required objectives for her course and the multitude of rude, immature students that kept talking while Haas lectured. Hands up to Dr Haas for getting us out!

Dr Haas is an exciting, enthusiasic,awesome professor that keeps your attention at ALL times during lectures. I've learned so much from her...love the stories! It's obvious that she loves her students, faculty & job. I hope to be just like her one day! Thank you for being such a great role model for me. I will never forget you. YOU ROCK MY WORLD!

I learned so very much from Dr Haas, my experence on the Unit was unbelievable & life long rewarding. I hope Dr Haas nevers leaves UF/CON...she is such an asset to the college. She is so smart, caring & fair to all her students. You can tell she loves teaching & working with us. Thank you Dr Haas for working so hard with us, We ALL love you!
Dr. Haas is super helpful and enthusiastic about everything! She makes the class super fun and interesting. Awesome professor! =]

analysis.name: David Clark
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took this class thinking I wouldn't gain that much from it, but I was wrong. His lectures are very engaging and will keep you interested, whether you like plants or not. This class is extremely easy, but you need to study for the quizzes They are pretty specific and may include things that he only covered in lecture. Do the extra credit. Easy A.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS. The professor himself was very nice, but the quizzes are hard even if you pay attention and study. It's a 1-credit class that I took for fun, but I ended up dropping it after taking two quizzes because I was failing. There is so much information in the lectures, and if you don't write down every word he says...good luck.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Overall, the professor was nice. There are only 4 quizzes, and they are very difficult and do not follow the lecture at all. I took it for fun, but ended up dropping it after 2 quizzes because they were so hard no matter how much I studied. He will put random information on there that he never said in the lectures.

Who doesn't want a plant every time they go to class?!? Prof Clark is basically a comedian and is passionate about his work with plants. The notes are essential to passing his quizzes and final, but you can take pictures of the powerpoints. Just make sure to know the material for the quizzes and final, or you wont pass.

Very harsh grader not many assignments based on 4 difficult quizzes. Quizzes supposed to be based on the lectures but are not accurate, making studying impossible. Claimed effort mattered most but despite trying best studying, going to class, taking notes, that didn't matter in the end. Very upset, took this class for fun, but my GPA paid for it.

analysis.name: Linda Clarke
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is terrible. She does not care about her students at all. Her lectures are incredibly boring and tests include material that was never discussed. If you have any type of flag during an exam she doesn't even look at what the flag was and just sends you straight to honor court and then proceeds to ignore your emails. Avoid her take someone else.

I found Dr. Clarke to be a joy. She is a demanding professor, but I can't believe the amount of OB knowledge I'm walking away with from this class. We probably read every page of that book, but I don't see how anyone can hope to be a good leader without having the information she imparted on us. This class was A LOT of work, but learn we did!!!

One of the worst experiences I have ever had through 6 yrs at UF. Lectures were awful, so awful that even though attendance & participation is technically graded, only 10-20 ppl/65 showed up to class.
Criteria for assignments is both unclear and used against you with confusing wording. Group project heavy w/ no safeguard for problems. Be aware.

Professor Clarke is very straight forward with her materials. The class is made up of three open note exams and extra credit. The exam questions are very basic and have no tricks. I would recommend reviewing her lecture slides and tabbing the textbook for main topics. SmokinNotes is also extremely helpful to use as a condensed textbook.
Professor Clarke is very enthusiastic and supportive of her students. I really enjoyed her International Business course and the group projects in this class.

analysis.name: Paul Ciesielski
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 144 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The ebook is outdated, very slow to navigate. There's also no copy n paste function in there for notes, which I found necessary to study for tests. The tests require memorization of every detail, picture, and module. This class is essentially self-study with memorizing the ENTIRE textbook, and half the material isn't even on dinosaurs but rocks.

By far the worst class (with the WORST professor) I have taken at UF. I took this class because it met the requirements for a credit I needed, but it was such a mistake. The program used for this class is literally impossible to figure out, and Dr. Ciesielski makes it very clear he doesn't want to offer help or be bothered. Don't take this class!!!

Easy A besides the fact that the TA's are the ones who grade group projects. Not really sure what this professor does, he didn't even have answers to questions. The software you have to purchase is $100 and outdated (not to mention frustrating to use). This class is easy but annoying & a pain in the ass. Take it if you have to but don't expect much

An inadequate professor in every way. Doesn't care about the student actually learning anything. Just here for his paycheck. SAD! The software was a ridiculous waste of time & money. Even the software support person said they can't believe anyone is still using this outdated, glitchy garbage. UF, I expect more from you. Such a disappointment.

I took this class online during the summer. The textbook is a software you have to buy so you have to take notes by hand. This class is too hard for a 1000 level class. You cannot use notes on the midterm or final since it is Proctored - ridiculous. However, I failed the midterm and final and still got a B in the class. Quizlet will help with hw.

analysis.name: Michael Clark
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Although my course was 100% online, Michael Clark always responded to Canvas emails and resolved issues incredibly fast. During the one mandatory live meaning, he provided great career insight and seemed genuinely interested in mine and my classmates' futures. I'm now taking DIG2121 with him this semester, highly recommend!

The course was being remodeled in real time so there were a couple of bumps along the road, but overall the class was really easy. Lots of drawing, fair bit of typing, but it is very straightforward especially if you already know how to draw digitally. The quizzes weren't too difficult, discussion boards were straightforward; easy class.

He is very caring and enthusiastic about his subject. He let students have a say in what rules were put in his syllabus. We do fun assignments during class and have little homework. He makes the class enjoyable, but his assignment instructions are often very confusing, and he has a lot of problems with Canvas.

He seems like a good guy, but his instructions for the assignments can be weird and confusing. Also, he will give you 2 days to complete a quiz on canvas, but if you take it on the second day, you will have a late penalty, which would not be a problem if he clarified.

He is very nice with students, and he clearly has a passion for what he teaches. However, homework instructions can get very confusing; he will post a lot of documents and not post what they are for. Also, takes a while to grade your assignments ( 2 weeks average)

analysis.name: Lynne Clark
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took Clark's Quest 1 (Nothing Left Unsaid) and had the best time. Every week I would look forward to her class, as they weren't lectures at all, instead, thought-provoking discussions. There are only a handful of discussion posts and very few projects, light work only. If you need a Quest 1, please take Professor Clark's, you won't regret it.

Overall, there is nothing particular challenging in this class, just a lot of little assignments. The hardest part is probably the short essay midterm (which is hard to study for, I recommend smokin notes). The weekly discussions are easy, but very tedious in my opinion. There is a 20 point extra credit assignment, DO IT!

Lynne Clark is one of the best What is the Good Life professors. The homework was annoying but it wasn't hard and the prompt for our final essay was relatively easy. Her lectures can be a bit boring but they were easy to follow and you can tell she is passionate about the material.

Just take this class, it's a good way to get this humanities credit out of the way, and Clark seems to be the best Good Life professor. There's weekly homework, but they are just discussion posts that you can B.S. and the final essay prompt is easy.

Loved this professor and the way that she handled considerable topics that could be boring. There is a lot to read with her course, which is not entirely her fault, but she made it more palatable. She also stood up for me when there was another student who was not considerate of me. If you want to take Good Life, make sure she is your professor.

analysis.name: Jennifer Clark
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The main problem stems from the fact that she is entirely unresponsive to any concerns students have - emails or discussion boards alike. Lots of busywork assignments that aren't necessarily hard, but are so tedious nonetheless. Easy enough grade, but the class is so frustrating to deal with that it doesn't feel worth it.
She was great. Very open to student involvement. Easy A just a lot of busywork. Very flexible.

This class was terrible DO NOT TAKE IT. Dr. Clark could not be reached by email or office hours at any time during the semester.  It was about 10 hours of work for each module. 1 module was due weekly. Instructions on ALL assignments were lengthy and unclear. Content was understandable but the way it was "taught" was unbearable.
Format of online class is confusing, disorganized, and tedious. Communication is not good. The class itself is interesting and easy!

This class will have you working up to 4 hours per day for one lesson...3 lessons are due weekly. This does not include the lengthy discussion posts and assignments. Though the content is not very difficult, this class is very time-consuming. 
This professor isn't the best at answering emails, I recommend emailing a TA and finding a GroupMe.

analysis.name: Gladys Cleland
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor is the antithesis of what a teacher should be. She singlehandedly made me question if I want to stay in school. The combination of ego, sarcasm, condescension and confusing assignments and tests makes this experience frustrating and counterproductive. I know less now than when I started this class. Take a different class!

If you want bizarre, off-topic, research-heavy assignments masquerading as tests, then this is your class!!! The "critical-thinking" questions are really just an exercise in frustration, and it seems like she keeps trying to get television show ideas from her students.

If you have to take a Cleland class, RUN! If I could have given her a 0, I would have. She lives for the GOTCHA! moments to throw unnecessary wrenches into your plan, she creates convoluted projects, assignments aren't released early so you can work ahead. College is hard enough, this prof makes it harder with surprises. DON'T take her class!!!

I wanted to love this class, but was very disappointed. Some of the feedback seems overly critical and illogical. Assignments are outside of the reading. Tests are not based strictly on assignments, a lot of subjective influences with the grading. I would not take another class with this professor.

The class itself isn't exactly difficult as long as you know APA very very well. She gives good feedback and overall seems like a good professor...Just don't expect to have free time with this course there is so many assignments, weekly bookwork and a 750 word discussion response w/ 250 word student response due weekly that needs APA cited sources.

analysis.name: Lawrence Clark
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is a complete waste of time - you learn nothing, you hardly do any writing, and half of the class time is spent waiting for him to come up with something for us to do. He is extremely disorganized and confused with his other classes at UCF and has a difficult time working with technology/Canvas. I would not recommend this professor.

He has unclear expectations; the class is 2 hours of nothing. He refuses to help or guide you, because "you don't learn if you don't get there yourself." As a student with a high gpa, this class is a waste of time, and stress that was completely avoidable. Do not take. If other class is full, wait a semester. It sounds harsh but it's true. Trust.

Professor Clark was by far one of my favorite professors I had at UF. His grading is very fair, and he really cares about your work and will let you know if he thinks your work will have a real-world impact. Clark prepares you for the job market in the industry ahead of you. His lectures are rooted in his 30+ years of experience in the industry.

He is awesome in almost every aspect of the course. He is not great at elaborating when you do not understand what he expects. I think the disconnect is that he thinks elaborating on a subject is holding our hand and the students (me) think of that as teaching... which some would say is Clarks job.

analysis.name: Tyler Cline
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is super nice and provides good feedback. Assignments were easy and exams only required light studying. During lectures, it could be hard to tell what was important to know for exams (also, slides didn't have much info and weren't posted), but I took notes on everything he said and used the textbook to fill in missing info and I did well.

Very nice professor and for the times I turned in something late I was simply honest about why I did and he always understood and didn't take points off. Lectures were lowkey boring, exams are straight from study guide and weekly reading assignments that you do. Overall, should be an easy A.

You won't spend too much time learning new material in this class if you payed attention in American History in high school, the main thing is getting through the lectures, which Tyler can make hard to do specifically because he seems unenthusiastic about the subject itself. If you can stay on top of attendance, the class is a breeze.

The class covered basic high school history material. Lectures were boring, but attendance made grades easy. Content and tests were simple, with light workload (1 assignment per week, occasional book reviews). Cline was patient and understanding about hurricanes affecting deadlines.

analysis.name: Stephen Coombes
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had Dr. Coombes for my first APK class at UF. I do not have a sports science background and he made my first class at UF go smoothly. The lectures were great and informative, he is funny and caring, I loved listening to his accent, and there is not a lot of busy work. Watch lectures and take notes. I learned a lot and it was an interesting class.

Dr. Coombes was a pleasure. I took advantage of e-mailing him and he provided great feedback.  The labs were short but important. Liked the yellowdig approach which gamifies engagement.  Limited discussion ecological dynamics, but that was ok, because we dove deep into information processing theory. One request: more on attentional awareness.

Dr. Coombes really seems to care about his students doing well and succeeding. He gives dynamic lectures that really teach you the subject. His quizzes are easy if you go to class, take notes, and read over them the night before the quiz. Exams are heavily based on quiz questions. I'd highly recommend him!!!!

Dr. Coombes class is a hybrid (online lectures and in-person quizzes and discussions). He loves research and is a very thoughtful and kind professor. Although there is little room for error as he only grades with exams, quizzes, and a tiny bit of participation, the material is really interesting and challenging enough to enjoy the class.

His lectures were all pre-recorded and put on canvas,. Each chapter is between 1-2 hours of lecture and they're simple and clearly explained. Quiz at the end of week on lecture with straightforward questions. Tests similar to quiz. In class time, we do a group project that we work on whole semester and get feedback each week. Very cool and nice guy

analysis.name: Jennifer Clark
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 101 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class is about what you'd expect. There's a lot of reading/lecture-watching/work involved but assignments have VERY clear criteria and she's an easy grader. As long as you keep track of when things are due you should have no problem doing well.

I had to WORK for my A-. 3 assignments per week.  Contrary to what others on here say, she doesn't give much extra credit.  Organizational skills are terrible. Tries to make the information tricky by embedding core information in paragraphs of text. Obtainable A, but beware she will try to trick you.  100%s on everything is necessary for an A.

I didn't enjoy this class at all. It's not difficult but things are due at 6pm on random days so it's hard to keep track of. She doesn't teach. She gives a topic for the section and assigns "find an article that relates to it." The only things I've learned in this class are from finding news articles, not her. She also NEVER answers emails!

Terrible!!! Clark was late in releasing every module and she rarely responds to email. The TA almost never responded to inquires on the Chat because questions pertained to when (and if) the modules would be released or Clark's poor instructions. Currently, less than a week left of classes, and two modules (4 weeks worth) are yet to be released...

I hate that I have to take Dr. Clark for so many classes in my major. She is the most unorganized professor I've ever had (that's saying a lot) who doesn't follow the syllabus, doesn't know how to use Canvas, and posts assignments/quizzes last minute so if you have work or other classes to worry about you are out of luck. Easy class, bad professor.

analysis.name: Colin Smith
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed this class. Dr. Smith is really funny and that's my favorite part about the class! Interesting material and in my opinion it's worth it to go to class, because he helps you learn it but it's not really required to go if you read the book on your own. He makes his lecture slides himself with funny or cute pictures. 100% recommend!

Dr. Smith is the best of the best. If you want a great upper-level psych elective, this is your course/man. I wish all of my psych courses were taught by him. One pretest (easy), discussion (easy), a writing prompt (easy), quiz (easy) per mod for 13 mods. This guy is a gem! Take him and you will not regret it, he is one of the best at UF. PERIOD!!!

Dr. Smith is a great professor who cares about his students. The exams weren't very difficult, but you did need to study the lectures' content well (there is no textbook). The readings and lectures were interesting. Papers were fun and easy. I loved the class and would highly recommend taking any course with Dr. Smith! If you can, take this class!

Professor Smith is phenomenal, despite the online course setup. He genuinely cares about his students and sets up the course to encourage that you are learning the content. Lectures are interesting and easy to understand and they never total more than 45 minutes per week. Easy and fun assignments and super nice TAs. Overall, great course! 10000/10

Social psych with Dr. Smith is the easiest thing ever. Just discussions, short writing prompts, and quizzes. The textbook is necessary but you can find it for free online. Never had to watch lectures and finished all the work each week in a matter of two days. He's also the nicest and coolest prof I've had! You won't regret taking his class

analysis.name: Danny Coenen
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Course: Pros - Easy class, easy quizzes, easy exams, very informative presentations Cons - Weekly essay-style homework (400-500 words), 2 major essays (800+ words) Professor: Pros - Good presenter, funny, very knowledgeable, passionate Cons - Grades some assignments such as the international presentation harder than one would expect

This was an online class but I still feel I got to know the professor well as he always answers his emails and is super accessible via office hours. He gives lots of EC. Know your APA 7. If you follow rubrics for all of the writing assignments, it is easy to get an A. Textbook assignments I just skimmed, not quizzed on.

Dr. Coenen is knowledgeable and entertaining. I definitely agree that his exam questions being very niche and specific. It's great that he allows you a one-pager, but it ends up being not super helpful as his super specific questions tend to account for that. If you're used to exams that ask about the big picture concepts, you're going to struggle.

Caring professor with clear grading. Expect a heavy workload: 12 Playposits, 12 textbook annotations, 6 quizzes (drop one), 2 projects, and 3 reflections. Assignments are time-consuming and graded harshly. Offers about 30+ points of EC. Know APA 7. Quizzes can be random—study the PlayPosits religiously as he never asks anything from the textbook.

Took environmental science online, each week had a reading, lecture videos, and assignment.  Content was clear and lectures were engaging and relevant.  Quizzes a tad difficult, but nothing crazy and you could use a cheat sheet for them all.  Take it online, though, if you have the choice.

analysis.name: John Conklin
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Conklin really cares about his students being successful. He is a great teacher and very clear in his examples. The Homework is MUCH harder than the exams. If you work hard on the homework, and really try to understand the material (TA Office Hours!), you will do very well in the class. His exams are VERY reasonable if you study hard. No tricks

A great lecturer who actually wants his students to understand the material. He covers the material slowly and does lots of example problems. My only critique for him is that he gives a lot of homework, in which one problem takes about an hour to figure out and finish. If you can master the homework (he doesn't give out solutions), you're golden.

Dr. Conklin teaches dynamics in a clear and organized way. He breaks all problems into 7 easy steps, which made challenging topics easier to understand and apply on exams/hw. His lectures were engaging and well structured, and he was always helpful during office hours. He genuinely cares about his students, is the best professor I've had at UF.

Conklin is so great for dynamics I wish I could take him for another class. His exams are very fair and was very open to giving points back if any issues were brought to him. He makes the content digestible and easy to follow. He gives you access to past recorded lectures and has one big homework every two weeks or so. Overall amazing professor

There is a textbook but it is available online. You are graded on 2 quizzes (basically exams), 6 homework assignments, and a final exam. The homework is long but is 2-3 times a month and graded VERY leniently (i should have like a low C if graded by correctness but my hw avg is a 91 right now). He goes over what is on exams, doesn't try to trick u

analysis.name: Judy Colindres
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Judy was always willing to interact with her students to make their day better as well as making class fun. I feel like I learned so much while having fun and enjoying the class. Not too hard, just a short discussion post before each class on a reading and then a few projects/assignments that aren't too hard. Would highly recommend.

Ms Judy is funny and easy to connect to! She's so funny n makes you want to go to class. The readings she assigns are so intriguing n good. Only abt 3 papers(none over1000), other grades come from discussion posts, where all she wants is to see your reaction to whatever the reading was. If you have the opportunity to take a class w her, take it!

Judy is the best! She supports everyone throughout the entire semester, and you will never worry about getting behind or being confused. Just dedicate a few minutes to reading before class and the discussion post, and the rest is guided by her. She makes sure to assign work that is doable and will not overload you. I enjoyed class every day!

Live, laugh, love Judy! Super caring and funny, classes are super fun and also extremely interesting. Judy cares about what she teaches and it shows. There's a daily reading assignment and discussion post, it's not that difficult as long as you get it done before class and follow the instructions. Take this class with Judy, you won't regret it.

Judy is absolutely amazing, made me actually want to go to class. While some of the novels are confusing, everything makes sense by the end in terms of the course's overarching ideas. She also helped me learn to actually write college level papers and was always there to support me in any way I needed. Would heavily recommend :)

analysis.name: Crystal Tisby
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I cannot believe that she is able to represent FYCS, much less the University of Florida with the way she treats students. She made me question my major and my purpose at UF.

Ms. Tisby was always accessible outside of class and never hesitated to answer any questions I had about any assignment. All her assignments have clear instructions in the rubric. As long as you complete all the assignments on time and participate during lecture, you will do well in the class. The feedback from the mock interview helped a lot!!!

Professor Tisby was one of the best teachers I had at UF. She is nothing but caring and wants all of her students to succeed. All of the assignments fully prepared me for practicum and future professional interviews. Be prepared to engage and learn about essential topics that you will use for the rest of your life in whatever career you pursue.

Tisby didn't seem to have a clear set of standards for assignments and graded in contrast with the rubric. Spent the semester on a mock interview and completing resumes. Didn't mention final assignments (30% of grade) until the last few weeks. Most assignments were fairly simply. Strict on deadlines. I did not gain what I hoped to from the course

analysis.name: Carl Crane
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This was one of the flipped classroom styles where you watch lecture videos at home and then go to class to do a quiz and/or a class activity about the video. The class is somewhat time consuming with having to watch some videos at home that are an hour long. My recommendation is to download them and speed them up. Start the group project early!

Absolute sweetheart of a professor! The man LOVES to teach! Even after 40+ years of lecturing experience, it's awesome to see that he is still so passionate about the material to this very day. Make sure to watch the lecture videos to really understand how everything is derived. Exams can be a bit tricky but he gives you plenty of resources for it.

You watch videos for homework, go to class and do assignments, and then have more homework. Don't wait to study for the certification test since it is insanely hard. Study for GDT test early on since it is 15% of grade and bites a lot of people from getting an A or B. Make sure everything is fully defined. TAs love taking off hw points. Great guy.

Easily the worst class I've taken. Instructions are vague on homework, rubrics are inconsistent, and the grading is excessively harsh. Save yourself the stress, this course is not worth risking your GPA

absolutely terrible human being. Did I pass the cert exam, sure, but hes still a POS. this semester, he was incredibly condescending to everyone and embarrassed people in front of the entire class. He also formally accused almost 15% of his 120 student class of plagiarism for HW assignments. Hes also very boring.

analysis.name: Rayven Crisafulli
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you have the opportunity, take this class 100%. Attendance isn't mandatory but the lectures won't be posted so make sure to go or get the notes from a friend. With the notes every quiz is super easy. She is really passionate and made the lectures entertaining by incorporating her experiences in the field. There's also a bit of extra credit.

Rayven is absolutely amazing! You don't have to be in class, but she does not post the slides, so find a friend! She is great at providing feedback and is clear on grading expectations. Quizzes are very easy if you take good notes, and she always will look over your projects to give input before the final submission. I highly recommend this class!

Rayven is an amazing professor! Her class is comprised of open note weekly(ish) quizzes, about 5 projects, and 2 exams. Do not let the projects scare you. The projects vary in size and are not very hard. She gives you everything you need to succeed and is always available to give you feedback. You also can either work independently or in a group.

Loved her! She is very passionate and loves her students. Quizzes are straight from notes and you are given exam questions beforehand. The only thing that is a bit hard are the projects, but nothing too bad.

Attendance is not technically mandatory, but she won't post the lectures so you should just go. I didn't need the textbook, and she really tries to make a connection with her students and genuinely wants to know what/how they're doing. She has her own company and will ask for volunteers if you want some event experience too.

analysis.name: Alan Cooke
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 141 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Cooke doesn't care about student success and he genuinely tries to make things harder for no reason. Exam reviews are worthless because he's lazy and only goes over the formulas. 7-8 chapters is too much for him to review but expects students to remember the HUNDREDS of definitions on the exams. Insanity. Avoid him, he doesnt want you to succeed.

Nice guy but the exams are weighted too heavy in comparison to the amount of effort other assignments require. 3ish mcgraw hill assignments every week with much reading, but they're not weighted enough in your grade. The extra credit helps. Lectures cover important stuff and textbook chapters has so many unneeded topics, so know the lectures.

Weighs HEAVY on 3 tests, where wording was confusing/convoluted. I attended EVERY live lecture, paid for Smokin' Notes and paid for professor's printed note packet as he recommended. HW scored 100s, tests 60s (class avg 70s). Final grade 71% which is "C". Professor submitted "C-". I didn't pass "C or higher" pre-requisite. I have to retake course.

Awesome professor, really cares about his students and responds to email very quickly. Exams can be hard if you dont study. READ THE TEXTBOOK AND USE SMOKIN NOTES. Smokin Notes saved my grade and make sure you do the extra credit!! Took the class online and didnt watch the lectures, just watch the exam review he posts. I enjoyed the class.

Exams cover both lectures and the textbook, with several chapters included. Focus on applying concepts rather than memorizing definitions. Exam questions are often scenario-based. Completing the extra credit is recommended. The professor is very passionate about the topic, but the amount of content makes it challenging.

analysis.name: Crystal Marull
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Offers a multitude of different platforms, but unequally grants credit for homework. Not good at speaking Spanish? Not a good test taker? You probably won't pass because she grades almost solely on the recorded activities and tests. Very accessible for extra help, but feedback comes off very short and condescending.
If I had to choose between failing and taking this class twice I would be on the streets

I had her for intermediate spanish and was very nice and gave great feedback. You have 30 minute zooms every week speaking spanish but it was very easy and I had a basic comprehension of spanish. Theres a pass or fail option as well but it is unnecessary if you do the work.

All college language courses have lots of homework but Professor Marull is also a really tough grader on the little things that aren't automatically graded by Pearson (which is the worst platform for learning to begin with). Lots of money thrown away on programs that suck, I've learned more from outside sources. Defeats purpose of paying for class.

I have taken Professor Marull for SPN1130 and 1131. All the resources are easily accessible, just put in the work. MAKE SURE TO ATTEND LINGUAMEETING SESSIONS, as this accounts for a massive part of your grade. As long as you put in the effort to participate, you will be fine.

analysis.name: Richard Crew
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are useless, he is impossible to follow and doesn't care if the whole class has been lost for weeks.  Often uses messy or even incorrect proofs.  Homeworks often contain mistakes and ask you to prove things that are false.  Does not attend his own office hours.  Avoid him.

Horrible. The man made each class a speedwriting contest, jotting along the board as quickly as possible. When he finished on the chalk board he would turn around, gasping for breath, and ask if we understood what he had vomited on the board. The man has weekly quizzes, and grades very strictly. Only class I failed at UF.

This is coming from a failed math major. Professor Crew is the only professor that taught linear algebra in a way that I could grasp. The majority of your time is spent doing homework while the majority of your grade is determined by exams. Make sure you've seen every proof at least once as the exams are proof heavy.

Dr. Crew was a decent professor. His lectures were quite messy and made on the spot, but the tests were relatively easy. He doesn't go over all the material in the course, so if you want to learn the stuff well, I'd advice seeking another professor. Regardless, he was charismatic and sometimes funny, making the lectures confusing but not boring.

Why is this professor's rating so low? He's very flexible. Sure, he's a boring lecture, but you could just stay home and read the textbook because everything's in there. Memorize all theorems, do all assigned homework, and attend his review lectures, and you'll do just fine. Loved the class structure. I never attended class and still learned a ton.

analysis.name: Cristian Munoz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: You can tell he cares about the class and makes class interesting and easy. It's a pretty easy class for being so abstract since he started using slides(Fall 24). The in-class essays are not too bad since you see the questions before and the other projects are not crazy. It's worth attending lectures because reading everything is tough.

Prof. Muñoz is fantastic. His Policy Process class is theory-heavy but super engaging, and he explains complex frameworks clearly. He's approachable, fair, and creates a respectful, thoughtful environment. If you want to actually understand how policy works, take this class—you'll come out smarter.

I love this prof so so much. He sounds a little like Gru and his lectures are funny and very helpful. He is super knowledgable and the readings (though there are a lot) are interesting. He cares a lot and prepares you well for the two tests. He gives you 10 questions before the test and picks 2-3 for the written exam.

Excellent professors & TAs. 5 grades: discussion attendance/participation, short paper, short presentation, 2 essay exams (in-class). You're given 10 prompts based on PowerPoints & chosen 2-3 on exam day. Content is not challenging but not very fun and takes a lot of time to grasp because they're very extensive. Professor is very engaging in-class.

There's only 5 grades but the paper, presentation, participation, midterm, and final are graded easily. Grades are reliant on the TA. Wallie was a great TA and taught more than the professor did. Professor was funny, lectures sometimes random but he posts the slides and you can use those to prep for the exams which are written essays. Easy A.

analysis.name: Matthew Cretul
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, not much work but he isn't very clear or responsive. I learned next to nothing.

Professor Cretul is the best instructor I have ever had in college. I loved this class and was disappointed when it ended. Cretul kept the class nimble, mixing online lectures with interviews, group discussions, and videos. In addition, he was interesting and was clearly invested in his students. Fantastic professor.
He's a bomb teacher. Like I loved his class and always was willing to give me advice when I needed it. Hard grader, but gives you good feedback.
tough grader but gives good feedback, about one assignment per week plus a midterm and a final
Loved Cretul! Great teacher, very patient. He makes you want to go to class

analysis.name: Elizabeth Cronin

review_highlights.comment: One of the greatest professors in the Arch department and one of the sweetest human being ever!! Workload at times could be difficult but that's just the major, it was never too overwhelming

Professor Cronin is a kind soul and any Design 1 student with her is in good hands. Architecture is a tough major and like 10% of students switch majors by the end of the first semester, but it definitely won't be because of her. Professor Cronin is honestly a blessing to teach architecture. It is extremely daunting at the beginning, but her friendly and caring nature guided us through the whole way through the semester. If anyone is considering to major in architecture, having at least one class under her is a must.

Architecture in itself is an extremely hard course and therefore so is D1.  However, if you have decided this class professor Cronin is awesome.  She is so positive and genuinely understanding of the amount of work you are being given. Would definitely take again.

She's amazing, I loved taking d1 with her. It was a great introduction to architecture. She's incredibly nice and patient. Great professor, wish I could take her class again!!

Studio is hard but it's just bc it's studio, Cronin made it as easy as possible .

analysis.name: Stephen Craig
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: WORST and RUDEST Professor I have ever had, period. He grades papers on how much he likes you, not joking. This teacher makes you buy $200 worth of books that he has articles in just to bring in royalties. He's totally boring and in a 4000 level course he talks to the class like they've never read an academic research paper. Only take this course from him if you actually haven't.

This was actually my favorite class I have taken at UF. He provides critical, yet very helpful feedback on all of your writing and really takes the time to read through all of the work you submit. This man is the worst professor I have ever taken at UF. Not only condescending towards students he also clearly does not know what he is looking for when grading. All of the feedback I received was extremely harsh and unprofessional. He does not provide a rubric for grading scales so he will determine your grade on how he feels that day. AVOID HIM

analysis.name: Curtis Taylor
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great Lecturer looked forward to class. And knows you're in college to get a job not be an academic. Test, quizzes and homework are challenging but not impossible. Make sure you know how to do all of the homework well and you will do alright on the exams. His exams are similar to past semesters try to get a hold of them. Helpful guy but challenging
Great professor, super understanding and accommodating. He made the class so simple and I learned a lot, he really cares about his students.

You can tell he enjoys teaching and wants students to do well. Not a ton of homework and everything was super fairly graded. Group projects throughout the class and for the final. Nothing was super difficult. Have to put in some outside work to really succeed but not really homework, just watching tutorials and such.

Mechanics of Materials can be a very easy class and Taylor makes it that way. His quizzes are usually easy with big bonus points to be gained by simply showing up to class on his special days where he goes off on tangents. His tests combine PE probs and fairly easy examples similar to class/hw. If you did well in statics you'll do better here.

Great Professor, doesn't like to teach anything he thinks is a waste of time, so he skips a few sections in the book. Attendance is optional, but he likes to give pop quizzes every once in a while. He will give you hints to what will be on the test, so take note of those hints and study them well before going into his tests.

analysis.name: Charles Cummings
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

Every project will have you up front speaking. He will grill you in front of the class. I think this is the worst class I have taken.

Professor Charlie Cummings is a professor for the Innovation Academy at UF. As long as u show up to class, submit the assignments he assigns early or on time, and actually show interest in the class it will be an easy A. I currently have a 98 in the class. It's not hard. Don't halfa** ur assignments and don't act like you're still in HS.
He praises one group only. If you aren't in the group, the class is extremely hard. He won't answer any questions. You need the ta for every assignment.

Mr. Cummings gives you exactly what you put into the class. If you slack, don't try, or cheat, you're going to get a bad grade. If you do the homework, work on the projects with the group, and don't cheat, getting an A is all but guaranteed.

As for Mr. Cummings himself, he is direct but fair, calling you out on the work but also providing feedback

analysis.name: Darlena Cunha
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Darlena is by far my favorite professor here at UF! I loved attending her class. She is so funny, outgoing, and really passionate about her job. Always down to help her students get stories published because she has many connections.. Her exams and quizzes come straight from Powerpoints and grades mostly come from lab.

Darlena is so funny, unfiltered and interesting. I looked forward to attending her lectures. Never missed a class! It was an honor to take class from a woman who has articles published literally EVERYWHERE. You don't need the textbook  quizzes and exams are straight from PowerPoints and lecture. Be aware that lab counts for most of your grade.

Darlena is a great professor. She tries to engage the class by using relevant examples (Beyonce was part of our PR lecture) and is enthusiastic when it comes to the material, even when she knows it's boring. My only complaint is that she tends to a little too free with her political opinions in class. However, none of the tests have bias in them.

Her lecture videos are kind of long and repetitive. I honestly learned nothing but she's nice and an easy grader. Papers aren't hard at all. There's textbooks but I literally never opened them. Very experienced in her career and would probably be a great connection if this class was in-person. Wish I could say I got something out of this class.

Great professor! She was funny, laid back, and very experienced in the field of media and politics. Gave good extra credit opportunities. Not a lot of assignments but they're all very doable, interesting, and relevant to the current world of politics. Three exams but the study guide has all the answers in it so if you use it, you'll do great!

analysis.name: Lexi Cunio
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: She was very nice and accessible. Would definitely recommend her if you need to take public speaking. Not too harsh of a grader if you actually put effort in. Exams are pretty easy, she basically tells you the exact questions during the in-class review.
Amazing teacher! I really enjoyed her lectures and she never failed to give us the help we needed to succeed!

analysis.name: Carlos Cunha

review_highlights.comment: Multimedia Writing with Carlos was somewhat difficult. Reporting was definitely the hardest class I've taken at UF so far. Cunha was one of the better TAs in my opinion. He is a very tough grader and will give you honest feedback that is ego-crushing but ultimately in the end, you will learn more than you thought. This is the class I've learned the most in even if it caused a lot of gray hairs.

This professor made me question my entire degree. He put me down when he graded my work and in front of my classmates. I would get my grades with no feedback. When I asked him what I did wrong and how to improve, he would tell me that I just didn't understand what he was trying to teach. Whatever you do, do not take his lab.

Professor Cunha made this class unnecessarily difficult. There were a lot of writing assignments, and there was no schedule for the class just random due dates that changed each week. He is very nit-picky when grading assignments. I recommend taking this class with another professor.
Lots of assignments per week, thorough grader but can be nitpicky

analysis.name: Cara Cummings
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Even though there are a lot of readings it is so worth it. she is an amazing professor and she's my favorite class. I loved her. Her personality was great and she used interesting examples instead of the usual boring ones to explain logic. Her class was not hard if you paid attention and did the homework. She was always helpful if you didn't understand. Great teacher!

She had a great personality, really nice but her test are WAY harder than what the HW are. She just started teaching and its clear she needs to learn how to.  I would take a more experienced professor so your grades wont drop.

Cara was extremely nice and accessible and very laid back. She also understood the material very well and was able to explain it fluidly. She is a nerd at heart and makes quirky jokes which keeps the class fresh.

analysis.name: Genevieve Curtis Murphy

She is extremely passionate about what she's teaching and taught very relevant information that was interesting and applicable to our lives. The exams are easy and she lets you use study guides, and the rest of the time she taught whatever we wanted to learn.

analysis.name: Cynthia Simmons

"Difficult," in every sense of the word. Grades very thoroughly, but to the point of being overly critical. She is also very helpful, but ONLY in one-on-one setting. The thing that I love about her classes is that she does as much work as she expects you to do.  She is a very through grader and is always around to ask for hel

She is really nice and kinda reminded me of Oprah.  She has real world experience but is sort of ambiguous in answering questions. The lectures I never watched, the quizzes are open note, but the PAPERS. omg the papers are nuts. She uses 3 different online platforms for the class which is annoying and just busy work. This class is easy, but it just sucks to complete because of how it's structured you don't actually learn anything in it. analysis.name: Cynthia Chennault

analysis.name: Cynthia Willming
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
