review_highlights.comment: She does not post assignments online, only tells students in class. She goes on random rants often that are off-topic. You must follow her formatting or you will fail. She will not correct grades even if she grades an assignment wrong. UF could easily find a better professor.

I went into the semester hesitant but overall, Professor Willming was great. There are two tests, a few group papers that are only 250 words max, and a few quizlets online to help with both exams. Easy class!

Professor Willming is amazing to say the least. She is super kind and she actually cares about her students. She makes the effort to learn your name and things about you, which is super rare these days. There was a lecture everyday with an activity every so often. If you engage in the lectures you'll be just fine.

Dr. Willming is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. She provides engaging lectures. Course is just a weekly online quiz and two exams, with no assignments. Attendance is taken about once a week. She provides a study guide for the exams and if you know that you should be good.

Dr. Willming is one of the best professors I've had so far at UF. Her content makes sense and it feels like I learned valuable information from the class that I can use in the future. Weekly discussions and vocab quizzes but they are very helpful in understanding the material. You earn a FEMA certification from this course which is good for resume.

analysis.name: Cynthia Shen

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely amazing and very sweet professor. After two semesters, she treats you like her children; is always extremely accommodating. She is one of the nicest professors I've ever had, and she's pretty funny. There's something due all the time but it's not too difficult as long as you stay on top of it. Would highly recommend her.

Shen laoshi is a great teacher. She is so nice, funny, and most importantly helpful. Her class is not easy but you can get an A. You just have to stay on top of everything, something is due nearly everyday between hw, quizzes, and situational responses. She also tells you pretty much exactly what will be on tests so they are doable. I loved her!!

learning Chinese is not easy, and you can expect lots of quizzes, homework, weekly tests, and oral presentations.  The workload will exceed that of your other classes combined.  Shen is extremely nice and very helpful.  Go to her office hours and she will help you to improve your pronunciation. Take Chinese if you are very serious about learning.

analysis.name: Jack Davis

He's strict with grammar, but gives you a guide on his rules. Follow it and you'll be fine. Just a few easy assignments and a group project, which was easy too.

I liked this class, but Dr. Davis is a stickler about niche grammar rules and I always got points taken off of my papers even if I ran them through grammarly and Microsoft Word. He is great, and this class is not hard at all! If you take it, you will definitely learn something new and interesting!

Definitely would take another class that he teaches. Papers are a bit rough as he is a Nazi when it comes to grammar and citing but he is very fair when he grades. Don't have to attend every class but I would recommend going to most seeing as how your essays are going to be what his lectures were about.

Dr. Davis chooses to make his seminar class more of a study of grammar than of the course contents. He is funny, passionate, and nice, but his obsession with grammar can easily tank your grade, upset him, and take up time in class every day. Dr. Davis is some good, some bad.

analysis.name: Daniel Czyz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Czyz is an amazing professor. His exams are exactly like his reviews and lecture videos. It took a LOT of studying and hard work but it was a very interesting class. He reuses quiz questions, and offers easy extra credit assignments. Anyone complaining the class is too "content heavy": it's a 4000/graduate level class what did you expect lol.

I hate this man and his course. The first 3 weeks you must learn every class of antibiotic, function, side effects, MOAs, structure, etc. For this insanity he provides 100+ pages of AI slop "mneumonics". The rest of the course is nothing until the last 2 weeks we repeat for anti-virals, fungals, malarials, and cancer drugs. The final is cumulative.

AMR is a really cool class. LOTS of memorization and tests are about 75% of the grade but there's a drop score and if you put in the work, you can get an A. The lectures are super thorough and everything on the exam is in there. Dr. Czyz is obviously very passionate on the subject and makes the lectures super interesting and enjoyable.

Dr. Czyz is passionate about AMR, but the course is much harder than needed. Exams are 600/775 points, with two cumulative tests. The final is 38% of your grade and tests on everything. Doesn't allow review of exams or practice exams. Study slides marked by a peptide gator logo—but almost all slides have it. Too much memorization hurts the class.

Take another elective unless this is your only class. 4 total exams, 2 and 4 are cumulative. Tests are unnecessarily long, the final is 150 questions. Not allowed to go back and review old exams. They are basically worth your entire grade. He drops either exam 1 or 3 to boost your grade. Slides are easy to follow but way too much info to study!

analysis.name: Tammy Davidson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 90 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The labs and midterm are easy. As long as you don't get busted equipment for the practical you will be okay as well. Pretty much everyone goes into the final with an A so the quiz is designed to shake out a grade distribution. Do not get lulled into a false sense of comfort with the easy midterm and your grade before the final.

Dr. Davidson loves organic chemistry, and it is evident that she is excited to share organic chemistry with her students. She is helpful, clear, relatively organized, and understanding. I thoroughly appreciated the fact that she posts outlines for the notes that I could print out and use to follow along in class.

The lab at UF is actually fun but the grading is ridiculous. The actual hands on work that you do in lab is not worth much of your grade but the lab quizzes are worth 65% of the grade which is quite ridiculous. The midterm and practical are easy but the final will shoot your A down to a C if you don't do well. Probably done on purpose. very cunning

Professor Davison is the best professor I had during my time so far at UF. She explains topics in detail with analogies that helps connect ochem to everyday topics, class quizzes and tests are fair and reflect lecture topics well with some reasonable additional challenge. It is critical to attend classes, her office hours are also extremely helpful

my favorite professor ever- but don't underestimate the content because it builds overtime and the final is really tough. go to office hours, get to know her, she's the most helpful resource for learning the content. 

can't recommend her enough, truly a joy to learn from!

analysis.name: Marcin Dadan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Possible #1 prof at Pitt. Marcin teaches all polish language courses, polish short stories, and I believe linguistics. I highly recommend taking his classes. He always adds a bit of linguistics into the lectures, which is very fascinating when you are interested in indo-european languages. I end up learning a lot more than just polish in class.

Dr. Dadan is so caring and funny! If you are having any personal troubles in your life, he is very kind and will work with you. You can definitely tell he cares about his students--even in an online class! The course is very easy if you keep track of deadlines, but also very interesting! I took Languages of the World btw.
Class was asynchronous so there was a lot of flexibility for work. Definitely an amazing person if youre willing to do the work or just get to know him during office hours.

analysis.name: Santanu Datta
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Does not know how to lecture and tests were made poorly. Take any other class if possible.

the TA basically teaches the class. this class isn't hard, but the hw is useless busy work which is a complete waste of time. we barely learned about any health professions since she heavily focused on social disparities in healthcare (this bugged me bc i wanted to learn about health careers). too many ted talks and painfully long videos each week.

Dr. Datta was a good professor, but the TA, Dee, taught most of the course. There is a lot of reading that must be done every week because we had weekly quizzes. If you do the reading and watch the assigned videos, the quizzes are easy. This class was an easy A, and I learned a lot!

Dr. Datta had the most unclear grading expectations for every assignment. Even the TAs were confused. He took a large chunk out of my teams grade for not doing something that "should have been obvious" even though he never gave us a rubric or clear instructions. He also gave us a team presentation that was due during finals week. Boring lecturer.

We had weekly quizzes based on long readings but workload was manageable. Later, quizzes could be done whenever on HonorLock and you were given multiple attempts. I enjoyed the discussions we had on real-world situations(ex. vaping, healthcare). The professor & TA Drew were very lenient/kind. I enjoyed this class so definitely would recommend.

Convoluted lecture slides that he just glosses over during lecture, homeworks having nothing to do with said lectures, and some exam questions being unnecessarily difficult. Go to lectures, do the iclickers/homeworks and you should be fine but Dr. Denard was unhelpful

DCI student 2019-2020 Does not grade by school grading policy and just waits for a student to do something remotely off task to get them in trouble. He is very aggressive with students and forces students do do things out of stress. Overall worst teacher Ive ever had.

analysis.name: Darragh Devine

review_highlights.comment: I actually agree with the previous reviewer. I personally love(d) neuroscience. I had the most interest in this course.  The exams, however, are ridiculously difficult relative to other exams, just by the specific MEMORIZATION required to answer the questions. Memorize all of his slides. No main ideas are tested, just specific knowledge.

Nice guy, but hard class.  The people who did well in this class already had a lot of biology knowledge.  If you don't like biology and learning about neurons, don't take this class. To get an A, you really have to read the textbook before class bc otherwise you'll have no idea what he's talking about (unless you're a pre-med major).

Dr. Devine really ignited my interest in neuroscience and inspired me to actually switch my concentration to Behavioral and Cognitive Neuroscience. He is so well versed in the topics he discusses and genuinely cares about students. He was always very responsive over email, answered any questions students had in class, and his office hours helped!

Dr. Devine is an amazing professor. I have a lot of respect for him and plan on taking his graduate course. You learn so much about the brain and how it works through his class. Overall, there are  4 tests that make your grade, one of which is dropped. It is crucial that you go to the lectures and read the text book if you want an A in the class.

Really sparked my interest in neuroscience, and his lectures are pretty interesting but he does go VERY fast and you do need to read the textbook to pass in my opinion. It is possible to get an A with a lot of hard work and preparation, not easy at all but the subject matter is very interesting. Essential class to those truly interested in neuro

analysis.name: Daniel Dickrell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Most overrated professor at UF. I personally think he was a terrible teacher who oversimplified almost every single lecture. The homework was always 1000 times harder than his examples in lecture, which SUCKS for the not-so-mechanically inclined. No partial credit on STATICS exams?! WTF is that? One math mistake and you're down a letter grade or 2.

His exams are not fair. They are short-answer and you do not get to show any work for the exams. Even if you understand the material you could still end up with a bad score on your exam by getting one part of a question wrong.

He's charismatic and pretty funny. But at least during my semester, the tests really felt unfair. There's no partial credit at all, make a math mistake and you're down a few letter grades. It's pretty intense. However, he'll probably try to make up for this in someway. You don't really have a choice but to take him though. Just get ready.
He over-simplifies lectures. His exams and quizzes are significantly harder than the examples he gives in class and there is no partial credit on his exams.

Make a simple math mistake and you're looking at the loss of a letter grade. While this may seem to make sense, sometimes under stressful situations people can punch a number into a calculator wrong - of course if this occurs, it invalidates all of the knowledge gained that can lead somebody to a right answer. Brutal grading scheme.

Diego is a gem of a professor. He really cares about students and respects us as individuals. This class on heritage speakers was super enriching for me and honestly changed my life! He is genuinely my favorite professor I've ever had. He's so insightful and really cares about his students and fosters amazing discussions about really important topics. There is a lot of homework and assignments but he grades based on care for the material, so if you try it isn't hard to get a good grade. I can't recommend him enough!

This is one of the best professors youll ever take. He cares so much about the students and the material, and if you would prefer to do things differently (change of assignments, due dates) he is flexible. Such a caring person and very intelligent professor. I wish he taught all my classes. Just do all your work and respect him plz

analysis.name: Larry Dimatteo

Bad: His lectures are downright painful to get through, in our curriculum, easily the most challenging so far. They seem to ramble from point to point and are difficult to follow.

Professor DiMatteo taught very practical and useful concepts and knowledge in International Business Law with an approachable and engaging style. At first, I was a bit worried about taking a law course because my friends often said it was difficult to understand. However, I truly enjoyed his lectures. The exams were also very straightforward.

Larry is hilarious. His lectures are extremely engaging, and he makes 5 controversial jokes a class. However, he knows this material extremely well, and you will really learn a lot if you pay attention. His tests aren't hard, but they're very detailed, based off lectures and handouts strictly. No computers is annoying but you really get used to it.

The class is painful, pretty boring because the class is centered in him speaking only and the book for the class reflects more on the tests. The first test he makes it look easy but the second test is extremely difficult and the class is more inclined for an attorney not for an entrepreneur. DO NOT TAKE CLASSES WITH HIM

Please don't let the previous bad reviews dissuade you from taking a class with Dr. DiMatteo, they are entirely untrue. Dr. DiMatteo sincerely cares about each student and is extremely passionate and knowledgable about international business law and all it encompasses. He makes study guides for each exam which prepare you extremely well for exams

I study hard for my grade and would hate if some other student got a good grade by cheating.

This was the worst APK class ive taken at UF. be prepared to feel constantly unprepared for her quizzes and final because shes offers no practice questions and won't let you review old quizzes. the only practice she offered was practice questions made by the students taking the course (who don't know anything), and there was only 1 posted

Definitely take Dr. Mani if you want an A in physio. Exams are only 35% of the overall grade, so you can average a C on them and still get an A in the class. Her style of teaching is poor and she explains the material without much grace. She doesn't believe that she can make mistakes. Threatening to send people to honor court for asking about extra credit is wrong on many levels. She also doesn't understand how Honorlock works but will insist that it is something wrong on your end.

Great professor. For an online class, gave you all the materials you needed to succeed. Watch lectures and read textbooks (clinical connections). Majority of the grade is from exams so make sure you study. I used smokin notes for every exam and ended with an A. They provide all the notes in an organized way to help you best succeed.

She reuses old lectures from several years back and when she does rerecord lectures she reads them verbatim. Relies HEAVILY on her TA and provides no interaction. She is lazy with online students and provides no real instruction.

While the textbook is not neccesarily required, it is a good source to look for extra information.

sadly I have had her for many courses which has led to headaches. However, please note her actual exams and quiz questions are simple! She is bad at communication and often does not post the lectures on time.

Dr. Difino is very sweet & easy to talk to when it comes to the class. All of her lectures are online so you really dont need to go to class as long as you keep up online. Quizzes and exams are straight forward and you can use notes. I found the class really uninteresting but it was definitely not her fault as she tried to make it fun for everyone.

analysis.name: Diego Alvarado

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: SUPER nice prof who cares about all of his students. Lots of OH & responds fast to emails. 1 week grace period on all assignments + TAs grade very leniently. Be aware that assignments are VERY surface-level. If you have background in CS/prog/AI and want to dive deeper into more technical topics the assignments won't really do anything for you.

Took this class for my AI certificate. Content was straightforward, and work was manageable. There were some bigger projects that could be time-consuming, but it was kind of up to you how detailed you wanted to be. Could tell the professor really cared about his students and was very passionate about the course.

You can tell that he's passionate about teaching this course, and it's really cute and inspiring. The class is pretty easy content wise, and you can pass the quizzes without watching the lectures. The writing assignments were short and quick, and I was able to get them done by seeting aside an hour every week.

Weird class, assignments seemed a little like busy work, but you can get a solid foundation of machine learning from the course. Professor Alvarado is great, he was super helpful and nice in office hours. His lectures were concise and entertaining. Would gladly take him in a  more meaningful course.

Professor Alvarado is very kind and accommodating, and the class is relatively easy. However, I strongly recommend taking full advantage of it because the material provides a solid foundational understanding of AI concepts. Even though the class isn't particularly challenging, it offers a great opportunity to learn and grow in the field.

This course should not be condensed to 6 weeks.
